item.title: Deadlines
item.author: bounce+2edd00.7bdc18-5mr68b7cb43ac2h04ai5=kill-the-newsletter.com@m.ghost.io
item.content:encoded: Sometimes you stop writing for a while, start writing a piece about why you haven't been writing, and then fail to finish it for so long that your surroundings get back to a state where you actually feel like writing again.That's basically what happened with this post, which I started drafting shortly after the trade deadline in August (hence the title). A lot of deadlines—personal and otherwise—have passed since then, and this has evolved with them to become significantly less morose than its first few iterations. Most of the original material isn't worth presenting anymore, but I'll retain the brief recap of the biggest events that kept me largely out of commission over the summer:After finishing grad school, I had to go to physical therapy for a super-duper fun (read: agonizing) shoulder issue that I alluded to in the vaguest of terms . Thankfully, PT helped a lot, but it put a huge damper on any sort of writing efforts (and pretty much everything else).I moved out of Boston and back to North Carolina, which tragically necessitated spending a day or two sorting all of my baseball cards so I could get rid of a bunch of them to try and fit everything in my not-very-large car.I presented my expanded master’s thesis at ! It was a blast, except for the part where I was frantically finishing my slides a couple hours before my presentation while simultaneously trying to listen to a panel discussion. You may notice a few changes to the site, most notably the absence of the donation page that previously graced the navigation header. That's because I have an honest-to-goodness full-time job! It's no longer breaking news, but I'm still very excited to tell you all that I am now a software engineer with , a company that needs no introduction to anyone who reads this blog. I have less time to write than I used to, especially since I'm still writing for BP, but I also don't have to spend a ton of time and energy worrying about employment, which is better for the creative spirit. (It helps that it's a really great job on all fronts.)Okay, enough personal updates! I'm not planning to go through the recent rash of signings in too much depth, but while we're all here, I may as well address the herd of elephants in the room.Around 4:45 PM last Sunday, despite wanting to do basically anything else, I left my house and drove down to Target in the pouring rain for a long-overdue errand. At 5:01, I parked, killed the engine, and opened my phone to a dozen group chat messages and an headline that read Mets To Sign Tarik Skubal. I kept my wits about me long enough to break the news to my father, which went as follows (verbatim):Then I got out of the car, hustled across the quarter mile of pavement between me and dry land, and wandered around the store for far longer than necessary in a haze of disbelief. I'm sure you probably experienced something similar upon hearing the terms of the deal. As one of the wonderful editors at , , put it, Over the course of the next nine years, will receive gross pay equal to almost half the gate receipts for Shrek 2And who's mad about it? Sure as hell not me! Yeah, I could get a head start on catastrophizing, but... as much as I've said over the past several months that I don't want him—that I barely want us to sign because they'll just be tainted by the curse—it feels a little different now that it's actually real. Maybe we will ruin him somehow. Maybe we won't. It's hard to be pessimistic about everything forever, even if it the Mets. Plus I'm trying to practice better mental habits, like not worrying about future events that are totally outside my sphere of influence, and last I checked I don't work for the Mets pitching lab. has done a fantastic job assembling the full context of the deal in , which I highly recommend to anyone who wants far more regular and in-depth updates on the Mets than I can provide. Some of the more interesting tidbits beyond the contract itself:The traditional introductory press conference is penciled in for December 1, right before The Lockout is supposed to start, so mark your calendars.The Blue Jays were indeed all in on Skubal, offering $420 million over the same nine years. It's a good thing the Mets were willing to keep upping their price, because it would take a lot of money for most reasonable people to relocate to Canada.The Dodgers, on the other hand, were all but out, allegedly gesturing to the CBA negotiations as a vague excuse to not spend money. That's also how I would defend myself if I were a coward and hated fun.Will Sammon at provided some into the negotiations that highlighted why our famously pitcher-shy front office was more eager to take the plunge than usual:Skubal lucidly outlined items of importance, from family concerns to aspects of winning. He impressed Mets officials with his discipline when the pitcher detailed his workouts. When he spoke about the Mets, he didn’t just tick off the obvious components of the roster; Skubal rattled off names of pitchers in the farm system. He had done his homework. He showed up prepared, interested. He struck Mets officials as sincere, articulate.I'm not sure he had to study much to assure them of his sincerity. seems like sufficient proof that he's long since embraced the local culture:I mean, can you blame him?I already know I'm going to spend all year getting confused when people talk about , because "Goldy" is already a guy to me. His name is Aaron Goldsmith. He does fantastic play-by-play work for the Mariners. And I'm sorry, but if there is any justice in the universe, he'll take up a lot more broadcast time on my screen than Paul does.Goldy 2.0 is joining the Mets on a one-year, $8 million contract to (presumably) do what he does best: platoon. You'll hear about his ability to hit lefties over the coming months, and for good reason; I won't be the first person to mention most of his stats, so I'll skip the paraphrasing and just quote directly. From Roger Cormier:Goldschmidt, the 2022 NL MVP, was indeed a left-handed pitcher’s nightmare in 2026 while playing for New York (AL). He hit for a .967 OPS in 183 plate appearances against them. And it isn’t a fluke: his career OPS against southpaws is 1.004.Forty-seven players have faced southpaws 500 times or more in the last three years, and among them, only two⁠—Jose Ramírez and Ketel Marte⁠—have a higher OPS than Goldschmidt’s .930.For my part, I'll point out that despite Goldschmidt's recent struggles against righties, he has never finished a season with a wRC+ under 100. Even at the age of 38 last year, his numbers against lefties were exceptional in all sorts of ways: .299/.393/.573, 12% walk rate vs. 18% strikeout rate, .411 wOBA, and 168 wRC+. Cormier also notes that Goldschmidt has been unusually healthy throughout his career—knock on wood—and reportedly a positive presence in the clubhouse. There's still quite a bit of risk involved, of course, but a Goldschmidt/ platoon (best wishes for his recovery!) at least has the potential to be pretty solid. It also makes look even more like trade bait after being tendered a contract.Rather than putting it off like they did with Skubal, the Mets for Goldschmidt via Zoom on Wednesday. If you don't feel like watching, he recited the usual lines about joining a great organization that really wants to win and wanting to help the team however he can even if he isn't playing every day, yadda yadda yadda. In line with what other veterans like Soto have expressed, Goldschmidt said he was excited about the bumper crop of young talent and the possibility of being a mentor in the clubhouse. He also mentioned his existing connection with manager Andy Green, who crossed paths with him as the Diamondbacks' third-base coach in 2015 (Green also managed several of their minor-league affiliates from 2012–14, when Goldschmidt was in the majors). Oh, and he's just as thrilled about Skubal as everyone else.The remaining Mets transactions of note:A number of old friends have moved to new places:And last but not least, a couple updates from the Mariners:The headliner here is the involving , who's joining Seattle alongside and in exchange for sending , , and to the Royals. This is an interesting (if mildly confusing) move that I like for the most part; Patrick Dubuque wrote up a nice analysis of it at BP. The major upsides, in my eyes:Garcia is an exceptional fielder. Prior to 2025, he wasn't really much good on the other side of the ball, and the potential effects of T-Mobile Park on his bat are a meaningful concern, but I'm just going to be optimistic about that for now.I no longer have to see Bryce Miller pitch for the Mariners. (Unfortunately, I might have to see him pitch for the Royals, who I sometimes tune into to see and .)The organization is also reuniting with on a with an invite to spring training. My friends who are long-term Mariners fans have informed me that he was one of the creators of their little infield dance celebration and are very excited about this development.Have a good weekend! I'll see you when I see you.

item.title: datasette-charts 0.4a0
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: The new datasette-charts plugin has its own plugin hook to allow other plugins to define new chart types, but I hadn't actually used it for anything yet. I had Claude Opus 5.5 build an experimental plugins just to try out the hook and it came up with a bunch of friction points in the design. This release addresses those, which should make building additional chart plugins a whole lot more ergonomic.

We hear what voters are worried about, we see what's at stake, and we're working every day on behalf of all Americans to build a stronger, more accountable democracy. We need your support to do that today. item.title: Sea Urchins Wearing Hats
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: The sight of a spiky sea urchins wandering along the floor of the ocean wearing a hat is pretty funny, and even more so when it's a bunch of them (I don't know the collective noun for sea urchins) all wearing a variety of hats that are really rocks, shells, and other ocean debris. One even carries a shell with a hermit crab living in it! But why do they do that? And how did they learn this new behavior? In this clip from the new BBC nature series Blue Planet III, Sir David Attenborough narrates a sea urchin fashion show and explains what benefit this adaptation gives these brainless sea creatures. (via Born in Space)

item.title: Watch Transformers: The Movie (1986) for Free This Weekend
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Just for this weekend, you can watch the 1986 animated classic Transformers: The Movie for free on YouTube, starting tonight at 8pm ET. The showing also includes a 2026 short film based on the movie called Optimus Prime: Awakening.Transformers: The Movie was stacked with voice talent: Eric Idle, Judd Nelson, Leonard Nimoy, Casey Kasem, Robert Stack, and even Orson Welles, in his final film role. The movie didn’t do very well at the box office, but over time it’s become a bit of a cult classic. (via tim carmody)

item.title: Everybody hates Pat McAfee
item.content:encoded: here’s an election next week, which means that you and I are currently being bombarded, ceaselessly, with unwanted voices. Here’s one such voice that, alas, we cannot vote out of office come Tuesday:That’s ESPN commentator and one-man pandemic Pat McAfee. If you’re unfamiliar with McAfee’s work, I envy you. No seriously, if I could trade bodies with you right now, I’d do it in a heartbeat. I don’t even care if you’re 85 and dying of gonorrhea, I’d still do it. That’s just how much I can’t stand Pat McAfee.Article continues below this adAnd I’m hardly alone. The clip you see up above is McAfee’s response to the harassment (NOTE: term used with ultimate generosity) he endured before co-hosting “College GameDay” for the four-letter live from the Salt Lake City campus of the University of Utah this past Saturday. McAfee is a known quantity to college football fans by now. They know that he’s the former Indianapolis Colts punter who abruptly retired from pro football to take a job for the chauvinist liberation front that is Barstool Sports. They know that McAfee parlayed his Barstool gig into a high-profile radio show where he paid Steelers QB and emotional cancer Aaron Rodgers literal millions of dollars to come on the air with him to muse at length about the dangers of getting vaccinated. And they know that ESPN, desperate to appeal to teenage gambling addicts, scooped up McAfee to become the de facto face of their network, now to the tune of $60 million a year.They also know that McAfee absolutely, unequivocally sucks.That’s why, prior to McAfee’s arrival in SLC on Saturday, a few Utah students made a short video of Utes fans doing their best McAfee impressions, which the university found harmless enough to post to its Instagram account (since deleted). I cannot stress how gentle of a ribbing McAfee gets in this video. Even Mitt Romney thinks these kids could have gone in harder on him. But McAfee himself found the video incredibly distressing, so much so that he told his studio bros afterward that he feared for his life going into the belly of the beast!Article continues below this ad“The university puts that out? Like as I’m about to go out and do an infomercial for the place? And then I’m walking in front of thousands of these people. This is how the university feels about it? It’s an uncomfortable feeling … I thought to myself, has anything, like, really scary happened at a college gathering in the state of Utah recently?”McAfee there is referring to the late Charlie Kirk, who was fatally shot while on stage at a campus event at Utah Valley University over a year ago. For reference, the UVU campus is located some 40 miles away from Salt Lake. So why would McAfee instantly think of Kirk getting killed right after a handful of mean and nasty college kids taunted him for always taking his shirt off? Well it’s because, like Kirk, McAfee is a self-absorbed asshole.Article continues below this adAnd even more galling than McAfee’s inability to tolerate low-ABV jokes from a bunch of Utahns is the fact that ESPN took his security risk comments at face value:“The safety and security of our on-air team, crew and fans is paramount at ‘College GameDay.’ We are committed to ensuring a safe environment, and given the very real threats that members of our team face, we take issues involving their safety seriously. We support Pat and recognize the very real and valid concerns he has around safety and security.”According to a report in Front Office Sports, the network apparently feared for McAfee’s safety on the road immediately after Kirk had been shot dead, and the FBI even advised McAfee to wear a bulletproof vest afterward. Although one supposes that McAfee would have simply torn that vest off while on the air to brandish a couple of “guns” of his own.But even if McAfee was justified to feel skittish about appearing in public crowds, it’s pretty telling how ESPN responded to his concerns with such an outlandish show of force. Because what’s so valid about this man’s safety concerns compared with the concerns of the women he works with, or the women he’s endangered? Are they more valid than the VERY real safety concerns of “GameDay” field reporter Holly Rowe, who was the subject of an AI-generated video of University of Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian punching her in the face ... a video that future fifth-round pick Arch Manning openly laughed about at an official UT presser? Or Mary Kate Cornett, that Ole Miss freshman? After McAfee slandered her on the air to an oblivious Adam Schefter, Cornett’s home was swatted, with armed police knocking down her door. Were either Cornett or Rowe afforded the institutional, DEFCON 1 level response that McAfee got from ESPN (and from the University of Utah!)? Of course they didn’t. That’s because they’re women, and because ESPN didn’t pay either of them $60 million a year to be professionally unfunny 20 hours a day. Even in Donald Trump’s America, the injustice on display is blinding.Article continues below this adThere will be no consequences for McAfee from all this. “College GameDay” has enjoyed record ratings since he joined the program (I’d argue this is because college football, not Pat McAfee, is more popular than ever), and ESPN already stood by McAfee in the wake of the Cornett scandal. As far as that network is concerned, there’s big money to be had in cheap trolling. It’s why they pay Stephen A. Smith millions of dollars a year too, after all.And so, you and I must bear witness to yet another unremarkable man in Pat McAfee failing upward while also clumsily making a martyr of himself. This whiny tank top will never be held accountable for his worst offenses, and he’ll always be shielded by the empty suits working above him. The whole thing is an insult to my intelligence and yours. And I already get my intelligence insulted on a daily basis in this country. Do I really need it from ESPN, too? I’m just trying to watch some football without some wildly self-absorbed, MAGA-coded jackass constantly trying to reach through the TV to suck my brains out. And yet ESPN can’t even afford me, or a handful of clever kids in Utah, that basic courtesy. So I hope that every other “GameDay” crowd from here on out makes Pat McAfee even more uncomfortable than he already is. After all, it’s only fair to return the favor. Article continues below this adHearst, the parent company of SFGATE, owns 18% of ESPN.

item.title: The Cheesecake Factory aesthetic won’t save MAGA
item.content:encoded: As soon as former president Barack Obama described Donald Trump’s aesthetic assault on the White House as “looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” the current president did what he does best: seethe. Ever since Obama’s weekend joke at an Ohio rally, Trump has been complaining non-stop. On Sunday, he posted on Truth Social that Obama was “a grossly incompetent President” and accused him of “campaigning for a Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist.” The following day, he told reporters that Obama is “not a smart guy.”At a campaign rally to shore up Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith’s fledgling re-election bid in Mississippi, Trump chewed on his grievance even more. After calling the Cheesecake Factory a “successful company,” he launched into a confusing defense of his garish White House redecoration. “A guy like Obama,” he said, “doesn’t understand the White House has to be clean, pristine, beautiful.”There are a lot of words for what Trump has done to the White House, but “clean,” “pristine” and “beautiful” are not among them. The president has covered every corner of the Oval Office with cheap-looking gold-paint and elaborate carvings. The once-stately decor now has a cluttered and claustrophobic feel — an embarrassing departure from the dignified appearance that all modern presidents, regardless of party, adhered to, which had a simplicity meant to reflect the sober responsibilities of the citizen-leader. But to understand why Trump clings to words like “clean” to describe his chaotic and overwhelming design impulses, it helps to look at how authoritarian movements like MAGA relate to kitsch. As I wrote in 2019 about Hallmark films, schmaltz creates a safe space the right can escape to — a cavern where they can wallow in fake feelings and nostalgia, without having to face complex realities that might challenge them. What makes something “clean” or “pristine,” then, isn’t actual clean lines or even a lack of clutter. It’s a conformist fantasy where everyone is white and straight and knows their place in the social pecking order. For Trump in particular, “clean” and “pristine” are racially charged words, building on his long history of equating whiteness with purity and diversity with disorder. Trump and his fellow MAGA leaders are engaging in performative outrage over Obama’s comments. On Monday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose net worth hovers around $600 million, ventured to a Cheesecake Factory in suburban Maryland, where he participated in a photoshoot. It was just the latest in a series of MAGA’s long list of kitsch-related tantrums, which have seen them feign enthusiasm for middlebrow corporate products as evidence of their identity as “real” Americans, unlike those snooty Democrats with their fancy mustards. This schtick has worked plenty of times to rally the MAGA base because, in this world, “elitism” has nothing to do with money or status. Instead, it’s a code word for the racialized paranoias that unite small-minded white people across the class divide. Just last year, MAGA propagandists got a huge boost when another restaurant chain, Cracker Barrel, tried to change its logo from the overly busy image of a man leaning on a barrel to something more minimalist — or, one might say, “clean” and “pristine.” This update was spun as a subterranean assault on white culture, an effort to smuggle in those “elite” and urbane values into the restaurants cornpone comforts, a place Fox News Grandpa used to feel safe from having to hear hip-hop music in the parking lot. This time around, my sense is that the Cracker Barrel Panic of 2025 cannot be remade into a Cheesecake Factory October Surprise that will save the Republicans in this midterm cycle. I’m a Cheesecake Factory virgin, but my gracious Bluesky followers and old-fashioned internet research revealed that the restaurant’s marketing is a lot different from the white-bread Christian brunch vibe that Bessent and other MAGA leaders seem to assume it must have. Apparently, it’s a deliberate, self-aware camp rather than dime-store kitsch, appealing to a younger, more modern audience that doesn’t take itself seriously. The Cheesecake Factory is supposed to be silly, which is why its fans don’t think its look is appropriate for the White House. Its famously long and decadent menu is also part of the joke. But at the same time, it reflects the expanding tastes of a diversifying nation, borrowing flavors from all over the world.It’s not just that the Cheesecake Factory’s wonton chips and chicken shawarma appeal to a different crowd than the chicken-and-gravy offerings at Cracker Barrel. The distinction is a sign of the way that middle America is moving on in general from the rigidly white, rural and suburban conformity so valorized by the Trump administration. The president and his acolytes, particularly during his second term, have been explicit about narrowing their view of what a “great” America should look like. The administration puts out a steady stream of propaganda envisioning a country composed solely of Aryan-looking nuclear families dressed in old-fashioned clothes. But it’s not clear if this has much appeal beyond some elderly white conservatives at Trump rallies, nostalgic for childhoods spent watching “Leave It To Beaver,” or the small number of bitter young men who let social media tell them it was easier to get a wife in the bygone days.After his narrow win in 2024, Trump and his aides like Stephen Miller convinced themselves that the result was a resounding victory for his fascist fantasy. The president’s rapidly plummeting approval ratings, though, tell a different story: He mostly won because swing voters have short memories and thought he might make good on his promise to bring down prices. Instead, they got more inflation. Likewise, Trump and Miller thought they won on a “no more tamales” platform. But as it turns out, Americans just want those tamales to be a little more affordable. In fact, Trump’s policies are now even threatening to take away free chips and salsa. In the process, we’re learning that, for most Americans in 2026, this traditional Tex-Mex appetizer is considered as all-American as, well, cheesecake.During the 2024 campaign, Trump’s love of kitsch mostly endeared him to his voters, who saw themselves in his corny preferences for the musical “Cats” or faux-baroque interior design. The president may be rich, but he connected with his fans in their shared resentment of smarter tastes, which require the very curiosity and intellectual engagement that the president fears. Instead, as Sam Adler-Bell wrote in New York magazine at the time, they craved the “As the popularity of Bad Bunny at the Super Bowl reminded us, the escapist fantasies of authoritarians don’t appeal to most Americans. It was just easier for some to look the other way when there wasn’t a war in Iran, rapidly rising gas prices and paramilitary troops grabbing grandmothers off the street. In good times, kitsch feels like harmless fluff, making its long history of being used for fascist propaganda easier to ignore. But when the president is more worried about redecorating the White House in his schmaltzy self-image than he is about the real struggles of Americans, the kitsch stops being so funny.Love it or hate it, the Cheesecake Factory cannot save the MAGA movement — no matter how many Cabinet officials get photographed in front of it.

He wouldn't say. Instead, Falvey called it "a matter of public and political controversy."It isn't. Joe Biden won, and Falvey knows it. But saying so would mean failing Trump's loyalty test, and Falvey wants this job. Now take a look at his resume:He finished law school in 2017 and has about six years of real legal practice outside his clerkships. In 2020, he worked for Senate Republicans as they rushed ultra-conservative Amy Coney Barrett onto the Supreme Court. After a federal court ruled South Carolina's congressional map racially discriminatory, Falvey helped defend it at the Supreme Court. He represented Douglass Mackey, the influencer behind a scheme to trick Clinton voters into "voting" by text. He has spent years inside Leonard Leo's network and the Federalist Society machine. Here's what that tells you about Trump's criteria for these nominees: Qualifications? Independence? Proven loyalty? If Falvey will duck a basic fact under oath to win Trump's approval, imagine what he'll do when a case Trump cares about lands on his docket.We're not having it. Demand Justice PAC is fighting for courts that protect the people, and that means exposing every one of Trump's cronies before they get anywhere near a lifetime seat on the bench.

item.title: We Must Always Remain Thankful For The Dallas Cowboys
item.author: Tom Ley
item.content:encoded: This year's slate of Thanksgiving games couldn't have unfolded much better from the perspective of a neutral fan. It was hard not to feel stuffed after just the first game, a 39-35 Bears win over the Lions that featured some of the season's most entertaining football, being played by two of the league's most entertaining teams. How could a game like that possibly be topped? Perhaps with a game that was just as thrilling, featured a 21-point comeback, provided a healthy dose of schadenfreude. That is what the Eagles and Cowboys delivered in the second game of the day: a purely delightful viewing experience.I am always left with a slight sickly feeling at the end of a game like Bears-Lions, only because it feels unfair for a game so good to have to produce a loser. It just doesn't seem right that Jahmyr Gibbs can carry the ball 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns, and not get to spend today as the biggest story in the NFL. This is why the Cowboys are such a valuable presence in the league: They could come out on the losing end of the greatest game of all time, and not one person, save for some number of degenerates, would be forced to feel an ounce of sympathy for them. Reasons to delight in the suffering of this franchise are so myriad that everyone can find their own for doing so (I choose this one).The Dallas Cowboys of recent vintage have become especially adept at delivering the goods to their true constituents, the nation's haters. A team with this purpose must maintain a delicate balance. They can't be so bad as to make all of their games unwatchable, but they can't be good enough to find steady competence. They have to be both an entertaining watch and a squad of self-sabotaging dopes. For a while there, we all had to wait until the playoffs for the Cowboys to make their face-first landing, but now the team has been fine-tuned to meet their true purpose. We can watch the Cowboys eat shit in inventive, entertaining ways just about every week now.

item.title: Here’s how a colicky piss-baby ‘celebrates’ Thanksgiving
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Kids today just don’t realize how easy they have it.It used to be that if you wanted some batshit crazy in your life, you had to work at it. You had to get dressed, go down to the park and find . You know who I mean: the sweaty, unshaven one, with the dirty hair and the bloodshot eyes. He’d stand too close to you as he pressed a badly mimeographed manifesto into your hand, while going on about how space aliens had turned his uncle into a Buick Skylark, and how the government had documents that proved this, but were refusing to release them.Ah, the good old days, am I right?Oh come on, you joyless sack of shit, how deranged are you? It’s a holiday, and we’re all just trying to enjoy ourselves. Nobody wants to read this tiresome litany of bellyaching. Certainly not today. Life is too fucking short.On a national holiday that’s all about getting together with friends, family and loved ones, and celebrating that time that the Original Americans chose willingly to help a bunch of struggling immigrants — — survive in a strange land, this vile, crabby old man, alone, no friends or family in sight, sits in his room in his vulgar golf motel, hunched over his phone, and does a racism. “Most importantly, thank you to the murderers, drug dealers, and criminals of all shapes, sizes, and colors, who illegally entered our Country from other countries’ jails, prisons, mental institutions, and places unknown, to rape, plunder, and kill American Citizens in record numbers. They are mostly gone now, brought back to their point of origin.”Way to truly learn the lesson of Thanksgiving, jackass.If the Wampanoag tribe who helped the Pilgrims survive had their own Nosferatu McGoebbels, going ‘no! No immigrants! Send them back where they came from,’ he got outvoted. He’s been lost to history.Wouldn’t it be great if our Nosferatu McGoebbels also got lost to history?Donny continues to be the opposite of who we need leading us right now. Throughout America’s history, we’ve gotten it wrong so many times — slavery, anyone? Japanese internment camps? The Trail of Tears? Jim Crow? — but Thanksgiving is one of the instances we pretty much (almost) got it right. We need a leader who can celebrate that — not one who continues to divide us.Unfortunately, being a racist asshole isn’t a high crime or a misdemeanor — but could the incoming Democratic Congress please please impeach the shit out of this clown, as soon as possible? You’ve already got more than enough reasons to.Couchfuck McGee and his cabinet confederates are probably never going to 25th Amendment this fuckstick back to oblivion, so once again, it’s up to Democrats to make things right.“It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE, and a correction was issued yesterday by the people in the Government Agency that does these numbers.”Goddammit, they’re not numbers, they’re numbers. That’s how it works. That’s how it’s always worked. The government collects data, put out numbers, and, as more data comes in, the number are revised, up or down. Twas ever thus, there’s nothing devious or diabolical about it.Donny should know this already. He’s been head of the federal government for six out of the last ten years. You would imagine that at some point he would — at least accidentally, by osmosis — gain some understanding of how his own federal government works, but no. Anything bad that happens, it’s just more proof that the whole system is rigged against him. It’s all so eternally exhausting. Donny raving and ranting about how the Commerce Department — headed by his own granny-starving oligarch, Howard Nutlick — is plotting against him is truly Red-Queen-off-with-their-heads territory.Is there no way we can get that guy in the park — the one with the manifesto about the uncle who got turned into a Buick to run the country for the next two years? How could he do a worse job than Preznit Fuckwit?Later in the day, Donny and his contractually-obligated Slovenian green-card rent-a-wife made calls to members of the military.Service Member: “What are you most thankful for?”Trump: “We have the highest stock markets in history.”There were so many possible answers to the question Donny had been asked. He could said he was most thankful for the beautiful rent-a-wife sitting right next to him. He could have mentioned his children. He could have spoke of being thankful for living in a country where a privileged, pampered white male moron such as himself could be allowed to fail eternally upwards until finally falling ass-backwards into a presidency he neither earned nor deserved. But no, he made it about the . What a sad, tiny, unimaginative idiot.We really need some palate cleansing right now, so let’s check in on the Obamas, and see how a real First Family spends the holiday season.“Thanksgiving is a time to gather with family and friends in gratitude for all the blessings in our lives,” Michelle Obama wrote. “It’s also an important time to give back.”The Obamas did what they always do — they . They didn’t hole up in a golf motel and bitch and moan about every fucking thing. They got out there and did good in the world. They’re an inspiration for the rest of us. “Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa is spending Thanksgiving morning giving back right here in Central Texas. She’s teaming up with Meals on Wheels Central Texas and HUB’s Feast of Sharing to help deliver 2,000 meals this Thanksgiving to homebound neighbors across Travis, Hays, Bastrop and Williamson counties.”Oh, and speaking of helping: two days ago I posted a link to a go-fund-me to assist the family of a woman who had been kidnapped by ICE to Mexico. As I sit here typing this on Friday morning, 64 of you have kicked in $2,619.You people fucking rule. Thank you so much for helping to make a difference. Let’s further palate-cleanse with some Daily Claudia.Here’s Ms Spouse, three years ago today, on November 27, 2023, enjoying the brand new couch she’d found for us. Decorating truly was one of her superpowers. Here’s another shot of Ms Spouse on her couch, keeping warm in the living room on a cold winter’s night, January 15, 2024.Now let’s switch it up completely. Here she is on the beach in Narragansett, Rhode Island, on September 15, 2021.Have a great Friday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Why I Don't Like Rom-Coms
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: One reason I never really liked rom-coms is that there is rarely any comedy in them. And even more so, the fact that the lead character's "happy ending" is so often ending up with the guy who ruined her life, or at least treated her terribly. Oh, I liked those stories when I was young and desired the bad boy. A few bad boys later, I understand that these romantic victories are altogether a horrible idea for lasting happiness. I agree with this host's insight, at least in the movies here that I've seen, which is a minority of them.

item.title: The Nazca Booby
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: The Galápagos Islands are a unique places for animals. Most of the area is a national park, fiercely protected, and the creatures who live there never had to worry about a threat from humans. So those who are lucky enough to visit can get up close and personal with seals, reptiles, tortoises, and birds such a boobies. Nazca booby is one such bird that nests in the Galápagos. They are great swimmers, but a bit awkward on land with their big feet. In this video, we see how they court and set up nests, although they can get confused as to which nest is theirs, and which mate is theirs. This can cause a bit of problem. But even stranger is their "heir and a spare" system of raising chicks. With limited resources, they can only successfully raise one chick. Yet they lay two eggs at a time. The chicks themselves will have to decide who is the favorite.

item.title: The Myths About Disneyland's Feral Cats
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: You've heard that Disneyland has a huge colony of cats who roam the park at night, hunting mice and other rodents who come in to get a meal from the trash people leave behind. The company doesn't talk about it because, after all, their mascot is a mouse. And specifically because Disney doesn't talk about those cats (much), internet legends have grown up around them.The cats moved in on their own because they found shelter where they wouldn't be bothered by people. Yes, they are managed by the park's administration now, but that was a gradual shift over time, and doesn't happen in the way you've been told. Cats don't follow instructions, especially feral cats. The Imagination Files dug into the history of these cats and busts some myths. The one thing he doesn't tell us is who gets to clean the litter boxes.

item.title: From LaTeX to Typst
item.author: Jack Baty
item.content:encoded: I've been using LaTeX to generate PDF documents for a long time. I like the way LaTeX does typography and layout. Its output looks "correct" to me. That's probably because LaTeX tries hard to do the right thing. I've never seen output from a word processor that looks nearly as good.I don't write raw LaTeX. I use it as a device for converting Org mode or Markdown files to PDF, usually via Pandoc.. I've built a complex workflow around it. Scripts, templates, boilerplate, etc. It works well. It's also wildly complicated. And so, enter Typst.People have been mentioning Typst as a modern LaTeX alternative. I ignored it because I'd already solved the problem. It turns out that dismissing Typst as "LaTeX for Losers" was a mistake. I finally gave it a go, and found that it's similar to LaTeX, but without the steep learning curve, complexity, or multi-gigabyte download. The output is slightly different, but still looks great.I've updated my scripts and various utilities to use Typst. It's open source, distributed as a single binary. And it's so fast!There's some residual guilt for leaving LaTeX after so many years. I think it'll be OK without me.

item.title: Rivalry Week Is Here To Ruin Some Postseason Plans
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: It's seeds-and-stems time in the college football season, and if that only means something for you older stoners, a glimpse at the schedule should tell you just how desirable that is. It's Rivalry Week for those schools that have a natural rival, and plain old Week The Last for everyone else. But even the rivalry games don't burn the way they used to. Indiana is now light years ahead of Purdue, Michigan vs. Ohio State feels unusually trivial and bleak this season, and South Carolina-Clemson is just a meaningless referendum on Dabo Swinney you didn't need or ask for.In other news, the NCAA is running a test on the 24-team playoff on Sunday with the announcement of the FCS playoff bracket, which is to say the Dakotas/Montanas Range War. The FCS champion in 12 of the past 15 years has been absorbed by those FBS ghouls, and since most of those champions have been North Dakota State (now an FBS operation; they won 10 of those titles), South Dakota State, and most recently Montana State, it seems safe to say the FCS trophy route runs roughly in parallel to I-90. But that's tomorrow's apocalypse. Saturday's opening round includes Harvard at Monmouth at noon ET, Idaho State at North Dakota at 1 p.m., and Incarnate Word at Montana at 8 p.m. The first two are on ESPN+, and UIW-Montana is on ESPNU, which is good news for you small-school psychos.

item.title: Things to be thankful for in these dark times
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: I spend 364 days of the year bitching and moaning about how everything is. Today, I want to talk about what I’m thankful for. I only wish it could have been more — but 46 is a pretty good run, isn’t it? because she’s very easy to brag about, and no parent could ask for more.I’m thankful for my family, because they’ve been putting up with my crap for almost seventy years.I’m thankful for my friends, because , I found a bunch of kindred spirits who are as weird as I am.I’m thankful to be surrounded by an amazing, supportive communityof readers and commenters. I’m thankful for my readers, because without you, I’d be shouting into the wind. And I’m thankful for my commenters, because you’re smart and witty, and you keep me on my toes — any mistakes or ill-conceived ideas on my part, and you’re right there to school me.I’m thankful that we live in this weird, fucked-up world where a cranky loudmouth like me, with no real plan beyond ‘Donald Trump is an asshole, and I’m going to troll him mercilessly on social media,’ can turn it into [gestures all around] .I’m thankful that 2027 is bound to better than 2026. I’m thankful for the massive tsunami that turned so many formerly red states and districts blue. Look at these homies. I’m thankful for them.I’m thankful that Preznit Fuckwit and his party shit their beds with such gusto that even this Democratic candidate, who lost by 43 points two years ago, and who didn’t have any money for TV ads, won her race this year.The morning after the election, Victoria Broderick, a tech support worker in Fayetteville, Tenn., told her boss she needed the day off because she might just have been elected to Congress.Ace job, Republicans — you built that! That’s Rep. Robert Garcia, the Democrat who is now the incoming chairman of the House Oversight Committee. He can’t wait for January 3, 2027. A federal judge in D.C. on Wednesday halted the Federal Communications Commission’s decision to call in ABC’s eight broadcast station licenses for early renewal proceedings, saying it was probably retaliation for speech critical of the Trump administration and therefore violated the First Amendment’s guarantee of a free press.(From 2025) “Donald Trump and the cynics want us to believe that he is all-powerful, and that if you fight back you will lose. He wants you to believe that if you fight back you may face danger. And he wants you to believe that it won’t matter, because he is in control of everything — and it is not true. It is time for us to build not a resistance but an opposition — something that is durable, something that will last for four years, and beyond. And we need to build that opposition now, and we need to all gird ourselves for the long run.”(From 2024) “I was not invited to my mother’s house for Thanksgiving. Apparently there wasn’t enough room. she said it was a ‘scheduling situation.’”Oh, I see. a ‘scheduling situation.’ How fucking pathetic.Imagine getting mad at because they allegedly prevent you from being an unstoppable fetus factory.“I was at the bottom of my class. I started doing heroin, I went to the top of my class. suddenly, I could sit still.” (From 2025) “Think about turkey. who really likes — be honest with yourself, Who really likes Turkey? You are all full of shit, everybody who raised your hands … turkey doesn’t actually taste that good. Chicken is good all the time.”Who disses turkey in a speech to the troops the day before Thanksgiving? Way to shit all over hallowed American iconography, dumb-ass. What’s next? A soliloquy about how George Washington was actually kind of an asshole?Hey, JD — is this your handiwork?I’m thankful I’m not a ketamine-addled Nazi who fucked his own brand straight into the shitter.And where’s Donny? He’s holed up in his unspeakably tacky Florida golf motel. He has no public appearances on his schedule for the rest of the week. What a man of the people!I’m thankful that I’m not in a cult.I’m thankful that I’m not stupid enough to believe the asinine “war on Thanksgiving” drivel that Fox News trots out at this time.From 2019: “Trump vows Thanksgiving name won’t be changed.” Holy shit. Was anybody seriously worried about Thanksgiving being renamed Communist Martyrs Remembrance Day? I swear, Fox viewers are the most gullible fucking rubes in the universe.From 2020: “They also turn their neighbors in, in China, in the Soviet Union. This is so un-American, and right now, just keeping your family’s Thanksgiving traditions is an act of civil disobedience. The home is sacred. what we do inside of our homes is our business, and I want the government out of it. And believe me, big government — Marxism — this is the one space they’ve been trying to penetrate for a long time.”Covid protocols, that’s what they were whining about — in the middle of a pandemic that killed over a million Americans. Damn those Marxists for trying to keep you safe.And, lastly, I’m thankful that I’m not a fragile fucktangle of insecurities who needs to be constantly ‘proving’ my masculinity via a series of inane stunts, only to have it all blow up in my face — or crotch, if you will.Let’s do some Daily Claudia.As I searched through my photo archive just now, I very surprised to learn that I never took a photo of Ms Spouse on Thanksgiving — at least not since the advent of digital cameras and phones. But I do have this, from our living room, nine years ago today, on November 26, 2017.And I do have a shitload of photos from the vacations we took in Plymouth, MA, back when Katie was a wee lass. That kind of sort of counts, doesn’t it?Here’s two-year-old Katie with her mom on August 24, 1993, on the beach in Plymouth Bay.This one’s undated, also on the beach in Plymouth Bay.Have a great Thanksgiving, everyone!here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Grand Thanksgiving Autumn
item.author: Jason Koebler
item.content:encoded: Happy Thanksgiving everyone! In the spirit of sharing and togetherness, we have a story from Megan Farokhmanesh about how couples and families are figuring out how to play without killing each other. The screenshot you see above is indeed a real screenshot from , which ran a segment called "Grand Theft Auto stealing Thanksgiving's thunder?" In this newsletter, today, it is! 25% OFF is 2026’s breakout entertainment event. By the numbers, it made roughly $3.79 billion in revenue at launch, outpacing the lifetime earnings for megahit films like , , and . PlayStation called it their biggest launch of all time with over 39 million players on the platform alone. It’s the center of the current cultural zeitgeist, whether it’s because of the game’s , , , , or its .Entire households are playing GTA VI with one slight hitch: unlike movies, TV shows, or even books you can read side by side, a single-player, 40+ hour experience is tough to enjoy when you live together. For some couples, the solution has been using more than one console or even multiple copies of the game. Married couple Meagan Kelley and Kyle Prahl typically switch between playing different games in the same room, or the same platforms in different parts of the house. The two are parents who find time to game after putting their son to bed. “The nice thing about having really young kids is they do go to bed super early,” Kelley told me. “Usually [my son] goes down and is asleep before eight, so then that's kind of like our prime gaming time.” The couple often plays different games in the same room, but for GTA VI “we're playing separately, so that kind of sucks because it's like we don't get a lot of time for each other,” Kelley said. Although some men online have whined about central romance, complaining about doing favors for their in-game girlfriend Lucia (“cuck simulator” being one common refrain), Kelley says the benefits to her real-life relationship are only positive. “It's funny that there's so much online discourse about GTA splitting up relationships and stuff when it's like something that can bring Kyle and I closer,” Kelley said. “Especially as we become parents and need to have more perspective on making sure that we're making time for ourselves.” Dividing up time to play and sharing their experiences, she said, adds a new dimension to their mutual hobby. “When we are together taking care of our kid or having conversations, it's almost like book club,” Kelley said. “We share the different ways that we're experiencing the game with choices and stuff like that.” Justin Massongill, another GTA VI player, and his wife recently had their second child. “She's taken on a lot,” he said. He bought the game for her, giving her priority to play so she could de-stress. is a true . Every news channel is covering it, anyone with a passing interest in video games is playing it, and it’s in less than a week. Desperate to connect with constituents, governments around the world have tried to capitalize on GTA’s popularity by releasing some of the worst AI-generated memes I’ve ever seen. The pictures of politicians in the hyper-real cartoon pink-tinted style of GTA 6 are so awful they even caused a minor political scandal in Scotland.Instead of links today, you’re going to get rantsgiving, a thing I just made up. Please know that my overwhelming feeling on this day is of gratitude to my friends, family, and, of course, our subscribers and readers. But also, in the spirit of consumerism and, vaguely, Black Friday, I feel it’s time for a semi-periodical rant about how absolutely insane the price of “computing,” broadly defined, has gotten in the wake of component manufacturers reconfiguring everything for industrial scale AI and data center buyers at the expense of the consumer market. We’ve touched on this before, but the problem has only gotten worse over the last few months, according to my recent forays in trying to figure out how to buy various SSDs and computer parts without making myself nauseous. It’s not that the price storage has gotten worse (it’s been horrendous all year, and has sort of stabilized in recent months), it’s that the need for the average person to have more storage that they actually own has become more acute.The recent outages we’ve seen have made clear that for very important things (priceless documents, photos, whatever), you cannot rely exclusively on cloud storage. I’m also not remotely a prepper, but the recent string of hacks, AI agents operated by reckless people and companies, and just general feeling of instability has me thinking that I should, at least, make sure that I have a few storage devices that are not connected to the internet in any way and that I can store, say, under my bed or in a drawer rather than on some company’s servers. It’s also not my cup of tea, but I think that if you are using AI to do anything even remotely interesting, it makes sense to try to run local, open-source LLMs because AI companies have been locking down the capabilities of their flagship models to prevent things like “Reverse Engineer Anything.” Prepare to take out various loans if you want to buy, say, a graphics card or a lot of RAM; the situation for those components is far worse than the SSD crisis. This has been argued before, but I think it’s very, very concerning that it is becoming more difficult and more expensive to have, say, a “personal computer.” Immediately after Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia, the company is reportedly going to cut consumer supply of GPUs. Anyways, this state of affairs where most computer and computer component manufacturers serve enterprise customers and data centers almost exclusively is leading us to a dark place, I think. Rantsgiving over!Have a great and restful day and weekend, everyone.

item.title: All the Worst Government GTA Memes from Around the World
item.author: Matthew Gault
item.content:encoded: is a true . Every news channel is covering it, anyone with a passing interest in video games is playing it, and it’s in less than a week. Desperate to connect with constituents, governments around the world have tried to capitalize on GTA’s popularity by releasing some of the worst AI-generated memes I’ve ever seen. The pictures of politicians in the hyper-real cartoon pink-tinted style of GTA 6 are so awful they even caused a minor political scandal in Scotland.Let’s begin in the United States, where Vice President JD Vance, the White House, and several other government-run X accounts attempted to capture the cultural zeitgeist by quickly churning out AI-generated meme garbage. GTA has long been popular with Trump 2.0 officials. In March, the official X account of the White House published a compilation of strikes on Iranian targets overlaid with the “WASTED” game over screen from GTA. In one of the more embarrassing exchanges, the X account for House Republicans posted an AI-generated picture of Hakeem Jefferies, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and Abdul El-Sayed above the words “Grand Theft Taxpayer.” A Democrat-linked account then replied with its own picture of Trump and the words “Grand Theft Autocrat.” Embarrassing for all involved.Israel also got in on the action. On the Friday after the game’s release, U.S. ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee shared a “Shabbot Shalom” meme in the GTA style. The Israel Defense Force’s Farsi X account posted several pictures of dead Iranian officials captioned as “WASTED.”“We saw all this killing before GTA6,” the post said in Persian, referring to the now retired meme we got something before GTA 6. This account posts in Farsi and meant for “direct dialogue between us and you,” meaning Israel and Iran, according to its bio on X.In India, Prime Minister Narenda Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) posted GTA memes repeatedly on November 19, the day the game was released.Indian politician and frequent Modi critic Jairam Ramesh mocked Modi for the posts on social media. “The PM in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media,” Ramesh . “Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate.”On Instagram, Singapore’s Land Transport Authority made fun of people who can’t navigate the country’s rail system. “If he can memorize the entire GTA6 map, he can memorize the Singapore MRT System Map,” . “Bro knows every corner of Leonida but still saves the SG MRT System Map on his phone to get to Orchard. 💀”NATO posted its attempt at being part of the cultural conversation on Instagram. “Wanted level: NATO,” the post said above the pink-hued cross cut collage of military images in the GTA style. “The final boss of wanted levels. Think you could fend off the most successful Alliance in history? NATO isn’t part of GTA6 of course, but if it was, we think even the best gamers would have a challenge with this one.”In Scotland, the Scottish National Party (SNP) posted GTA 6 memes so cringe that they talked about it on the floor of parliament. On November 19, the SNP social media accounts posted AI-generated pictures of Boris Johnson and Margaret Thatcher in the GTA style. “When the loading screen so long you start seeing characters you’ve never seen before,” one image said over a picture of Thatcher pouring a bag of “Scottish oil money” into the UK treasury.Scotland’s Green Party didn’t find the memes funny. Rockstar is originally Scottish, was founded in Edinburgh, and still maintains a significant studio there. In parliament, Green co-leader Gillian Mackay said she was proud of what all of Rockstar’s workers had done to stand up against bad working conditions and produce a work of art like GTA 6. Then she made comments about SNP leader and Scottish First Minister John Swiney. “Last night the SNP angered anti-AI campaigners by posting AI-generated GTA memes on its social media despite huge concerns about the impact of AI and AI data centers on artists, workers, and the environment,” Mackay said in the parliament . “Does the first minister understand why people are concerned about his government’s approach to AI and the big companies behind it.”The SNP deleted the memes and Swiney apologized. “First of all, let me say that I don’t want to offend anyone by anything that we get up to, so if I’ve offended anyone about that, I’m sorry about that. It was not my intention,” Swiney said in the Scottish parliament. Then he said he shared concerns about AI but defended the technology’s use for healthcare.There will be more bad posts like this. hasn’t been out for even a week and the memetic landscape around it will shift and change. We don’t even know what the dominant memes for the game are yet, let alone the innovative ways posters will iterate on them. Rest assured, however, that the governments of the world are watching and waiting to post their own variations and make it all cringe.

item.title: Pass the Controller: How Single Console Households Split 'GTA VI'
item.author: Megan Farokhmanesh
item.content:encoded: is 2026’s breakout entertainment event. By the numbers, it made roughly $3.79 billion in revenue at launch, outpacing the lifetime earnings for megahit films like , , and . PlayStation called it their biggest launch of all time with over 39 million players on the platform alone. It’s the center of the current cultural zeitgeist, whether it’s because of the game’s , , , , or its .Entire households are playing GTA VI with one slight hitch: unlike movies, TV shows, or even books you can read side by side, a single-player, 40+ hour experience is tough to enjoy when you live together. For some couples, the solution has been using more than one console or even multiple copies of the game. Married couple Meagan Kelley and Kyle Prahl typically switch between playing different games in the same room, or the same platforms in different parts of the house. The two are parents who find time to game after putting their son to bed. “The nice thing about having really young kids is they do go to bed super early,” Kelley told me. “Usually [my son] goes down and is asleep before eight, so then that's kind of like our prime gaming time.” The couple often plays different games in the same room, but for GTA VI “we're playing separately, so that kind of sucks because it's like we don't get a lot of time for each other,” Kelley said. Although some men online have whined about central romance, complaining about doing favors for their in-game girlfriend Lucia (“cuck simulator” being one common refrain), Kelley says the benefits to her real-life relationship are only positive. “It's funny that there's so much online discourse about GTA splitting up relationships and stuff when it's like something that can bring Kyle and I closer,” Kelley said. “Especially as we become parents and need to have more perspective on making sure that we're making time for ourselves.” Dividing up time to play and sharing their experiences, she said, adds a new dimension to their mutual hobby. “When we are together taking care of our kid or having conversations, it's almost like book club,” Kelley said. “We share the different ways that we're experiencing the game with choices and stuff like that.” Justin Massongill, another GTA VI player, and his wife recently had their second child. “She's taken on a lot,” he said. He bought the game for her, giving her priority to play so she could de-stress.Massongill watched his wife play the first hour of the game; the next morning, he started his own. “We're kind of trying not to look too much at the other player's screen,” he said. “I don't want to, you know, get spoiled on things. But it's also such a massive game that what are the chances that we're going to see the same thing in the first place?”Madeline Blondeau and her fiancée decided to buy their copy of together. The $80 price tag wasn’t so bad between the two of them; they downloaded the game, knowing that even with a PlayStation 5 and a PlayStation 5 Pro, they’d have to divvy up time between their single copy. “We have been alternating our schedules,” Blondeau said. Her fiancée wakes up at 5 a.m. to start her IT job. Blondeau’s shift starts around 10 a.m. “We've sort of worked this out—me playing while she is working, and then her playing while I am finishing up my shift, trying to tiptoe around spoilers.” Even as a queer couple, there’s an equality and care for each other in the experience Blondeau finds reassuring. “I think there's these very gendered expectations in relationships in terms of who games, who is the gamer of the household,” Blondeau said. You even see it in , she adds, where Jason, the game’s male protagonist, will be the one with a controller in his hand. “Breaking down the gendered expectations of who is the gamer in the relationship really opens up a whole avenue for not getting into fights with your partner over video games,” Blondeau said. “It feels like two people who figure their shit out, working out equitable time to experience something they've liked their whole lives, and talk about it.”This past weekend, Blondeau’s fiancé left to grab groceries. She came back with something extra: the trilogy for Nintendo Switch, a consolation prize for whoever wasn’t playing their shared copy of GTA VI. “I was in the mood to play Vice City,” her partner said. “We can trade off."

item.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025. It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics.Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO. In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy!It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync:The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers Nukes Mike McCarthy, Then His Own Career
item.author: Samer Kalaf
item.content:encoded: To provide further detail on the Pittsburgh Steelers' late-night benching of Aaron Rodgers, the quarterback himself appeared on Wednesday's edition of . Essentially, Rodgers said that he would never play for the team again, and he described head coach Mike McCarthy as inattentive, sleepy, and "unhealthy." In response to this TV appearance, the team has waived Rodgers.The Steelers' benching of Rodgers came after his dismal performance in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, and there's some logic behind it for purely football reasons. But the way the news was delivered was the strange part: Tuesday at 11 p.m. ET, through a team spokesperson. At the time, it wasn't even clear if Rodgers himself knew he was being benched for the team's game this Friday against Denver.

item.title: Quentin Tarantino goes back to his bad old habits in his new sequel
item.content:encoded: If you’re an American man of a certain age, the pedigree behind “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” (which opens theatrically this week before streaming on Netflix in late December) had you downing Big Kahuna Burgers in celebration before the trailer had even dropped. Here’s a movie directed by the legendary David Fincher, who was also behind the camera for “Fight Club,” one of the defining bro movies of my generation. Better yet, this movie was scripted by Quentin Tarantino, who wrote and directed every other defining bro movie of my generation: “Reservoir Dogs,” “Pulp Fiction,” the “Kill Bill” saga, and on and on. Tarantino rarely lets other directors shoot his credited scripts. One previous example, 1993’s “True Romance,” just happens to be one of my favorite movies of all time. So you understand why I was foaming at the mouth for this first official QT/Fincher joint effort to be unleashed upon the world.What I ended up getting was a movie that let me down in the same way that the majority of Tarantino’s work this century has.A lot of fanboys will disagree with me here (as will Tarantino himself), but I believe that man established a standard with “Pulp Fiction,” released in 1994, that he has failed to match ever since. That film not only instantly established the Tarantino aesthetic — rat-a-tat dialogue, B-movie tropes of yore remixed and elevated, scenes punctuated with jarring spurts of violence — but also . Every seemingly tangential piece of dialogue fit perfectly into the greater story. It’s not necessarily fair to expect Tarantino, with or without collaboration, to consistently put out movies as good as one of the best films ever made. But I don’t care about fairness. I expect greatness from Tarantino and Fincher, and I know “Cliff Booth” straight up fails to achieve it.Article continues below this adI’ve kept you in the dark with regard to this film’s plot for too long, but don’t worry: The movie itself will keep its plot from you for even longer. “Booth” serves as a loose sequel to 2019’s “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” which Tarantino wrote and directed. Brad Pitt, who won the Academy Award for best supporting actor for his work in that movie, returns as the lead this time around. Pitt plays Cliff Booth, a World War II vet-turned-laconic Hollywood stuntman, who still lives with his pawn shop owner of a dad (Peter Weller! RoboCop!). Cliff makes extra money by doing a number of side jobs around the LA area, some of which require him to kill people. One day, Cliff gets tasked with one such job when a statuesque talent agent (Elizabeth Debicki) hooks him up with nutjob actor Charlie Peters (Scott Caan, in easily the best performance he’s ever given), who needs Cliff to help undo a big ol’ mess he’s gotten himself into.That sounds like a tidy enough plot, but true to the film’s title, the audience has to sit through well over an hour and a half of scene-setting before that plot really kicks in. Thanks to Fincher and his scribe, those establishing scenes are all beautifully written and photographed. The actors are beautiful, the vintage cars are beautiful, and Los Angeles itself is beautiful. It’s easy to get lost in the vibe of it all, which is precisely what our filmmakers end up doing.Article continues below this adTo use the classic editor’s dig, there’s a lot of good stuff in here. The chemistry between Pitt and Debicki is palpable, and the chemistry between Pitt and Weller is even better. The movie and vintage TV clips in this movie are, as they were in “Hollywood,” as well thought out as everything else (although some clips, including one featuring the late Johnny Carson interacting with Caan’s character, may have been AI-generated). One of Pitt’s side jobs is revealed in a way that had me howling with laughter. There’s also a truly fantastic scene I won’t spoil where Pitt tells Caan about the best way to feel like you’ve killed a man without actually killing a man. As always, Tarantino is the best in the business at building up your anticipation just with dialogue.But it takes all of this movie’s 140-minute runtime for that anticipation to pay off. There is a pair of extremely violent antagonists in this movie (Matt Groove and JB Tadena, both excellent), but I damn near forgot they were in it before the story had finally circled back to them. Once it does, the audience is treated to one last set piece where Cliff Booth has to either talk or shoot his way out of a jam, and you’re never quite sure which one it’ll be until the very end. It’s a fantastic scene, and one that’ll probably net Tarantino his zillionth screenwriting Oscar nomination.However, none of it feels . With “Hollywood,” Tarantino could have used its Manson Family plot to make the scariest movie of all time. Instead, he punted and just made the same alternate history caper he’d already made a few films prior (the WWII-themed “Inglourious Basterds”). Every QT script over the past 20 years has played out like a handful of brilliant punch lines that each require an extensive setup. All of these films have suffered from logy pacing. I thought that Fincher behind the camera might have served to speed things up a little bit more, but the director is too deferential to Tarantino’s script to rectify what has become his peer’s worst filmmaking habit. At one point midway through “Cliff Booth,” Pitt says to Caan, “I’m a little confused about what we’re doing here.” Under my breath, I said, “So am I.”Article continues below this adTarantino has already said the next movie he writes and directs will be his last. That last film was originally supposed to be “The Movie Critic,” until Tarantino nixed the idea. You can tell he used portions of that movie’s unfilmed script in “Cliff Booth,” because Debicki’s agent character is also a former movie critic herself, and a harsh one. So whatever project Tarantino takes on as his final statement will be, in theory, something completely different than whatever fanboys like me might have been anticipating. Maybe it’ll be another crime movie. Maybe it’ll be some other tale of old Hollywood. Maybe it’ll be another alternate history story that doubles as a 14-year-old boy’s daydream. The speculation about Tarantino’s next move is always its own enjoyable spectator sport.After watching the man’s work remain in neutral ever since “Kill Bill,” I’m now certain Tarantino’s last movie will be something. Like “Hollywood” and “Basterds,” “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is a good movie, but it’s not a good movie. I went in expecting something revolutionary. Instead, I ended up getting another QT flick that had way too much fat on it. Tarantino has always said he wants to end his directing career on a high note. He’s 30 years too late for that.

item.title: MAGA attacks on women voters are no joke
item.content:encoded: If the polls are correct, Republicans are set for a shellacking in the Nov. 3 midterms, losing the House and quite possibly the Senate, and likely some prominent governorships across the country. If that happens, there’s a good chance that online chatter about repealing the 19th Amendment will heat up once again.For a decade now, MAGA social media users have been aggrieved at the way women vote for Democrats at higher rates then men, such as in 2024, when 53% of women voted for Kamala Harris over Donald Trump, who received 55% of the male vote. Their solution to this imbalance began in 2016 as a trolling hashtag on what was then called Twitter: #RepealThe19th, a reference to the constitutional amendment, ratified in 1920, that extended suffrage to all women in theory, but mostly white women in practice. The hashtag has faded since then, but not because of a lack of interest. The idea has morphed from a joke into a serious proposal that is making its way from fringe Christian right circles into the mainstream of the Republican Party.Douglas Wilson, a prominent Christian nationalist who lead the church Pete Hegseth belongs to, has grown increasingly loud in his calls to replace individual voting with “household voting,” where only heads of households, who are presumably male, would be able to vote. The defense secretary has praised Wilson for a CNN interview he gave in which he outlined his vision of a Christian theocracy that disenfranchises women. Ending women’s suffrage is a hot topic among the right’s youngest leaders. Earlier this year, “Conversation over whether women should vote used to be limited to some of the most extreme and patriarchal churches,” said Sarah Stankorb, a journalist, expert in women and religion, and author of “Damned If She Does: Why Women Quit Church and What It Means for the Future of Religion.” She told Salon that it’s “no coincidence” that ideas once on the fringes of the Christian right “keep popping up in public discourse.”Stankorb noted that Christian nationalists are taking “partisan polarization” to a place where “denying the basic rights of half the population not only comes off as a debatable point, but one with theological backing.” “All at once, patriarchal men share think-pieces on walking back the 19th, while perched casually in leather chairs, normalizing the conversation as if it’s simply academic, reasonable even,” she said. Stankorb is worried that the constant social media repetition means the shock has “dulled over time,” putting the once unthinkable “in the realm of ‘normal.'”To be certain, it’s extremely unlikely that Christian nationalists will be able to repeal the 19th Amendment, which would require passing and ratifying a new amendment. There is precedent for this; after the 18th Amendment, which banned the sale of alcohol, was ratified, it took another amendment, the 21st, to overturn Prohibition. The process would require a joint resolution approved by two-thirds of the House and Senate or a constitutional convention, followed by approval of three-fourths, or 38 out of 50, statesAs extreme as the GOP has gotten, it’s hard to imagine that the party — which has 11 sitting female Senators — would go that far, or be able to win big enough majorities in Congress, if they even considered it. After all, it took a century of feminist organizing to get male leaders to even let women vote, and it would be a lot harder to take the right away since over half the electorate is female. The larger goal here is to normalize the idea that women’s citizenship isn’t legitimate and to instill the idea that women should feel lucky to be “allowed” even the few rights they have.In all likelihood, most of the MAGA pundits and pastors who are pushing to end women’s suffrage know full well it will never happen. But their musings shouldn’t be dismissed as nothing more than attention-seeking behavior. The larger goal here is to normalize the idea that women’s citizenship isn’t legitimate and to instill the idea that women should feel lucky to be “allowed” even the few rights they have. In fact, this notion is similar to the way that leaders like Vice President JD Vance insist people of color should be “grateful” for having rights at all, words which carry the implication that the way to prove their gratitude is by not demanding full equality. Wilson made the underlying threat explicit in April. “Women have to appeal to men for the rights,” he told Konstantin Kisin, a right-wing British political commentator. “Anytime men want to take rights away from women, they can, like that. And there’s not a damn thing women can do about it.” Wilson continued to argue that there will no end to male dominance, because if women push their luck too far, it will be the end of male “benevolence” in letting women have any rights at all. His diatribe shows the goal of the anti-suffrage argument: to scare women off seeking full equality, or even trying to claw back rights they do have.While the 19th Amendment is unlikely to be repealed, it’s important to note that other rights that were long assumed to be safe have been stripped from women in the MAGA era. The right to abortion, which was for decades widely assumed to be untouchable, was overturned by a far-right Supreme Court in 2022. Because of women’s outrage — and suffrage — many red states restored abortion rights through ballot measures, which angered the right and amplified calls to take away women’s votes.The assumption that the justice system will protect women and children from sexual violence has also been under assault in recent years with actions that range from the Trump administration blocking the release of the Epstein files to the attacks on the Cornell student whose only “crime” was reporting an alleged gang rape. Then there is the recent ad run by Ohio’s Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, which features the estranged mother of Dr. Amy Acton, his Democratic opponent. In 1978, after Acton reported that she had been raped by her stepfather, her mother sided with her husband, and the pair fled the state following his arrest and before he could stand trial.All these incursions on women’s rights are easier to sell to a public that has normalized the idea that women aren’t full citizens — that their ability to vote is a privilege that can be snatched away, and suffrage is only a right for men. The voting rights issue is used as a rhetorical cudgel against women, designed to delegitimize their opinions by suggesting they aren’t even real citizens. It’s about scaring women into thinking that if they “abuse” their vote by demanding full equality, they will be left with no rights at all.
