item.title: Captured Federal Court Approves Iowa Toxic Lead Detonation Sought by Trump
item.author: Lisa Graves
item.content:encoded: Today, the Trump administration plans to detonate 9,500 pounds of lead azide, a weapons-grade compound of lead and nitrogen used in bombs. The Army’s destruction of 68 barrels of this toxic substance is expected to release a 100-mile plume of dust that could deposit lead in communities across Iowa and neighboring states, contaminating water, farmland, and more. Lead is a neurotoxin that can cause brain damage. There is no safe level of exposure, and it does not break down in soil.Earlier this week, Trump absurdly tried to blame Iowa’s incoming Democratic governor, Rob Sand, for any harm caused by the lead-filled barrels, even though he has not even taken office yet. Governor-elect Sand has urged the federal government to give Iowans more information about the planned detonation.The situation began earlier this year, in March, when the Army found signs that some of the barrels it had stored for decades at a munitions plant in Middletown, Iowa, had degraded into a crystalline form that could result in spontaneous detonation.In response, the government issued a contract this spring to MuniRem Environmental, a company specializing in chemical mitigation, to help neutralize the lead azide barrels, a process it has successfully done before. Despite the lower cost and much smaller risk of explosive consequences, the government reportedly canceled that contract in May–abruptly–opting instead to proceed with its own plan of blowing up the barrels. When MuniRem raised concerns with the EPA about the potential dangers of detonating the lead, it received no reply.The Trump administration is invoking an emergency exception to environmental rules to justify the detonation, while planning to filter the resulting plume of gas and dousing it with water. The government asserts that temperature changes, like the coming winter season, could result in unmitigated explosions of the lead barrels if it does not blow them up first.Local and national environmental groups sued to stop Trump’s plan, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit temporarily halted the detonation a few days ago. On Monday night, however, a three-judge panel approved the plans, ruling that the administration could detonate the barrels, a procedure it asserted was safer than allowing them to continue to degrade.On the surface, this is a unanimous ruling, which makes it seems as though the law compelled the result. But we’re talking about the most captured federal court in the country, rivaling even the U.S. Supreme Court. Ten of the eleven judges on the court, which covers the Dakotas and Minnesota straight down to Arkansas, were appointed by Republican presidents.Only one judge on the entire court was appointed by a Democratic president: Jane Kelly of Iowa, who was nominated by President Obama in 2013. Due to the random process for judges getting assigned to three-judge panels, she was not selected to hear this appeal. We do not know how she would have ruled, but the packing of this circuit court means that there is zero chance of any party drawing a panel with a majority of Democrat-appointed judges.Statistically, the chance of drawing an all Republican-appointed panel on that circuit is nearly 75%. The chance of having a majority of Republican-appointed judges hear your appeal is 100%, just like with the U.S. Supreme Court, where six of the nine justices are Republican appointees.The Circuit’s lead detonation ruling is unsigned, leaving its author anonymous. Two of the judges siding with Trump, however, were hand-picked by him for their positions of power.Justin Smith was confirmed in June by Senate Republicans 48-43, with all Democrats voting no. Smith, who was born in 1985, could remain on the federal bench for another 40 years or more.Before becoming a judge, he was a partner at the law firm founded by John Sauer. Sauer argued for immunity from criminal prosecution for Trump while he and Smith were partners and co-owners at the James Otis Law Group. Trump praised Smith’s role in that litigation, in which the Supreme Court, led by John Roberts, invented presidential immunity from criminal prosecution. Trump said Justin “played a BIG role in securing a Supreme Court Landmark Victory on Presidential Immunity.”Sauer was named Solicitor General and Smith got rewarded with a federal judgeship.Numerous civil rights groups opposed Smith’s confirmation. He has actively attacked abortion access and trans rights. He is also part of what I call Leonard Leo’s Missouri Posse: a group of lawyers tied to the right-wing agenda and money directed by Leo, to whom Trump delegated the selection of Supreme Court candidates during his first term.I don’t think there was any chance that environmental groups and Iowa community members suing to stop or further delay the lead detonation would get a fair hearing from Smith.Another Trump appointee on the panel was Steven Grasz. When he was nominated to become a federal judge, the American Bar Association gave him the worst possible rating: unanimously Not Qualified (NQ). The ABA concluded that Grasz could not be trusted with a judgeship “because of judicial temperament concerns, specifically ‘lack of open-mindedness and freedom from bias.’”Grasz is a long-time activist against abortion access and the separation of church and state. He has repeatedly attacked LGBTQ rights and supported conversion therapy, a cruel practice that has been condemned by mainstream psychologists.The Republican-controlled Senate confirmed him in 2017 anyway, by a 50-48 vote, with every Democrat voting against his confirmation.The third judge on the panel was Bobby Shepherd, who was appointed to the Eighth Circuit by George W. Bush in 2006. Shepherd has since joined numerous controversial rulings, including blocking President Biden’s student loan debt relief plan. Unfortunately, the Roberts Court sided with Schmitt, despite Missouri’s obvious lack of standing to challenge the Democratic plan to give debt relief to Missourians and other Americans.Earlier this year, the Eighth Circuit also sided with the Trump administration against Minnesota as the state tried to stop Trump’s violent siege of Minneapolis. That federal operation resulted in deaths and injuries, including what I consider to be the murders of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by ICE agents, and the seizure of numerous immigrants who committed no crimes.This is a circuit court where Republican appointees have routinely chosen to retire when a Republican is president, locking in Republican control. Meanwhile, Democratic appointees–like the first woman and first Black man on the court–stayed on as they aged only for Republicans to flip their seats, as happened with Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg.The Eighth Circuit is a cautionary tale of court capture by right-wing special interests, resulting in a court predisposed to side with Trump and against ordinary people.It is one of the reasons why I support term limits across the federal judiciary, not just for the Supreme Court, among other needed reforms.The right-wing court capture scheme has already broken so many of our rights, and now it seems its appointees are willing to let Iowa and surrounding areas be poisoned, too.The EPA’s description of .The Constitution’s , which empowers Congress to create lower federal courts and specify their jurisdiction.Get the full receipts every Monday in The Cover-UpAccountability starts with the record. COURIER’s new Contradictions Tracker compares testimony to the Epstein files, with every source linked. Follow along every Monday in The Cover-Up.

item.title: trurl
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: trurl is a command-line tool for parsing, constructing and modifying URLs in shell scripts.It extracts individual components such as the hostname or path, replaces their values and resolves relative references. Query operations append parameters, remove matching keys and sort key-value pairs, with URL encoding handled by the parser.It's URL handling is based on libcurl's parser, matching the interpretation used by curl. It reads batches of URLs from files or standard input and emits formatted components or JSON for further processing use cases.For developers who are used to curl and writing shell scripts that prepare HTTP requests or clean URL lists, trurl provides structured operations for changing addresses and parsing URLs.

item.title: rustic
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: rustic is a backup tool with a command-line interface for creating encrypted, deduplicated snapshots in the terminal.It stores snapshots in local or cloud repositories using the same repository format as restic. Subsequent backups reuse existing data and record complete snapshots, while in-place restoration updates only changed files.The interactive browser lists snapshots and their directory trees, with controls to edit tags and start restores. Configuration profiles define backup settings and retention policies for repeated runs.For anyone that is interested in backups such as system administrators maintaining workstation or server backups, rustic works best for scheduled snapshots and interactive recovery from existing repositories.

item.title: rmpc
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: rmpc is a terminal music client for Music Player Daemon (mpd) that browses music libraries locally and controls playback in your terminal.It shows a three-column library browser which you can navigate the queue and supports choosing tracks, arranging the playback queue and managing saved playlists. If a track has the correct album metadata attached, rmpc will show the cover album artwork in terminals with compatible image protocols on the left hand side with the title and the artist name.Whilst playing, rmpc will show the visualizer at the bottom and you can cycle through different visualizers as you navigate the queue. Synchronized lyrics are an extra addition and the panes can be configured to customize the view positions entirely such as optionally using cava for audio visualizations within the same interface.For those who are listeners with an mpd setup, or looking for alternative local music players such as cmus or kew, rmpc can be useful as a feature rich media player for playing tracks and displaying album art and managing listening queues in the terminal.

item.title: tokui
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: tokui is an interactive terminal viewer for exploring a codebase's size, language composition and complexity.By default it runs tokei for line counts or uses an scc backend for complexity estimates from either code analysis tool. This tool comes with sortable tables and directory trees and treemaps of file attributes, such as line count, language and whitespace with a breakdown of how they are used or distributed in the code base.tokui can be used as a command-line tool and integrates with Git to measure code churn, compare statistics between revisions and browse historical snapshots with side-by-side file diffs. Additionally, you can compose tokui to accept piped JSON as input and it can run an analysis on the codebase, which is useful for code reviews, CI automations and it gives helpful information of the total language use in a project.For developers or software engineers who need to review and audit a project repositories code growth or learning a project's structure, tokui can be used for locating large directories and examining which folders have the most code distribution.

item.title: slackdump
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: slackdump is a command-line archiving tool that saves Slack conversations and attachments without requiring admin-level privileges.Using the interactive wizard in the terminal, it guides you to authenticate and export a given Slack workspace with SQLite archives and Slack-compatible ZIP exports available for accessible conversations. This tool can also view the exported archive inside which you can search the results afterwards.It is possible to add newer messages through incremental updates in an existing archive and then open it in the built-in browser viewer or even convert it to static HTML. This tool comes with an MCP server which can gives AI tools and agents access to parsing the archived messages, conversations and threads for local analysis.This tool is useful for team members who need to preserve project discussions or who are preparing for migration from chat platforms such as Mattermost or to another Slack workspace who need to. If you need other platforms, slackdump can also be used to migrate conversations to Discord.

item.title: sipnab
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: sipnab is an advanced terminal tool for capturing and analyzing SIP signaling and RTP media to investigate VoIP calls at the packet level.It reads live interfaces, packet capture files or HEP (Homer Encapsulation Protocol) feeds from SIP proxies, then it organizes messages into searchable dialogs and call-flow ladders. A split view places the decoded SIP message beside the sequence with a visual flow of each package type and the timeline in milliseconds.sipnab does a low level RTP analysis that can reveal jittering in calls, packet loss and estimated voice quality for individual streams. HEP feeds carry signalling rather than call audio, so media analysis requires capturing the RTP traffic. Headless mode can export JSON and can be used for reports for automation.Intended for VoIP engineers, system administrators or network engineers specialized in VoIP infrastructure, sipnab supports diagnosing failed call setups and one-way audio from captures on Linux and macOS.

item.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: I gave a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months.Here's the video of the talk. In this post I'm going to pull out the major inflection point theme and interrogate it more deeply.Coding agents in November 2025Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of Claude Opus 4.5. With hindsight, this was a consequential model.In the Opus 4.5 announcement, Anthropic said:Testers noted that Claude Opus 4.5 handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding. They told us that, when pointed at a complex, multi-system bug, Opus 4.5 figures out the fix. They said that tasks that were near-impossible for Sonnet 4.5 just a few weeks ago are now within reach.Opus 4.5 was the first model I had used with Claude Code where the default result was generally the right thing. I hadn't been using Claude Code as a daily driver because it didn't feel reliable enough - I had to correct it often enough that it didn't feel like a clear accelerant.The new Opus changed that. For most of the coding problems I faced on a daily basis, Opus would . It was clearly faster than working through the problems myself.Also in November, OpenAI released GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, GPT-5.1-Codex, and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max. These had a similar effect on their Codex coding agent: it became reliably useful for many of my coding tasks.The timing was convenient, because the December holidays were upon us. A lot of people, myself included, spent December tinkering with these new tools to see what they could do. By January we were ready to use them for our actual work.Fable class models in June/JulyWe got our first hint of Claude Fable in April, when Anthropic announced Claude Mythos and said that it was to release, due to its improved cybersecurity capabilities. Mythos was a model that could not just find security vulnerabilities, it could also figure out how to exploit them.In June we got to see how good that model was for ourselves, with the release of Claude Fable 5 - a defanged Mythos, that would solve most problems but would actively block you from using it for security work.After three glorious days... the US government took it away from us. Fable 5 was placed under export controls that effectively banned the model. We wouldn't get it back until July 1st.For me, Fable was an inflection point because it introduced us to what I now think of as . My definition of these: In June I wrote about how Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive, after I asked it to help fix a display glitch in Safari and it spun up its own screenshot mechanism and a CORS-enabled localhost logging server to help resolve the bug.A more recent example of the power of Fable class models is my mysterious beep finder from a couple of weeks ago. I gave Opus 5.5 and then Fable 5.2 access to five WebAudio microphones in a room full of boxes and it was able to triangulate the source of an infuriating mysterious beep to within about 40cm.Give it a goal, give it the right tools, and watch it cook.I'd currently class Claude Fable 5, 5.1, 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 as Fable class (I think of Opus 5.5 as "cheap Fable"). GPT-6 Astra got there for me too, and I think the new Gemini 4 Neon may count as well.These now represent the baseline for what I expect from a frontier model.3D modeling and game development in September/OctoberSomething interesting happened with frontier LLMs over just the past four months: they got at 3D modeling. Set them up with Blender or ask them to write Three.js code and they'll produce credible models of almost anything you ask for.I first noticed this with Claude Fable 5, but it really kicked into gear with Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and most recently the Gemini 4 family. Here's Gemini 4 Neon's attempt at "Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data", for example.3D spatial awareness is crucial if you want to use vision LLMs for robotics. I don't know if 3D modeling capabilities are a side-effect of the labs focusing on that or vice-versa.I was somewhat relieved that designing a game that was appeared to remain a uniquely human pursuit. I even used that in a talk in September to reassure people that us humans still had a role to play!Then, I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 "This game isn't fun enough yet. Make it a LOT more fun." And it worked. My Command & Conquer-style RTS went from boring to deeply entertaining overnight, after Opus spent 12 hours playtesting new features and rebalancing the gameplay.Opus 5.5 was the first model I'd used that appeared to understand fun. I've since worked on several little game projects where prompts like "Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful" produced results that kept me engaged for significant amounts of time.Opus 5.5 came out on September 22nd, 2026. I've been to two different conferences since then where people showed me game projects they'd been working on that really did feel like proper, worthwhile games.It feels like another inflection point to me.Is Fable 5.2 an inflection point too?I'm still trying to decide if Fable 5.2 represents a new inflection point, or just another incremental improvement.I'm getting done with that model right now!It seems to have taste that almost exactly matches my own. I have been burning through all sorts of gnarly problems that I've been thinking about (or procrastinating on) for several years now. The release notes for Datasette 1.0a42, 1.0a43, and 1.0a44 - plus LLM 0.37, 0.37.1, 0.37.2, 0.37.3, and 0.38 - all in the last three weeks, represent a flood of fixes, features and improvements.If this does represent an inflection point, the key feature seems to be that if you can imagine and then clearly describe a piece of software, Fable can build it. That's a wild thing to say, but it matches my experience over the past few weeks.Software development has transformed beyond recognition in the last year. I don't think I'll ever go back to typing most of my code by hand.

item.title: Michigan Pulls Offer On Incoming Athletic Director, Still Owes Him Money
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: The Protect College Sports Act is a bad idea that seems stalled in Congress, and now we're finding out that the things most endangering college sports are coming from inside the house. In this case, the house in question is in Ann Arbor, Michigan, where ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Trev Alberts, who was hired last week as the University of Michigan's athletic director, has now been un-hired for that role.Yes, Alberts has apparently been fired before being hired as the Michigan AD, which may not quite be unprecedented but is inarguably damned weird. What made Michigan reverse course was that Alberts was the AD at Nebraska when Ashley Scoggin, a women's basketball player, sued the school in 2024 after being kicked off the team because of an alleged sexual relationship with assistant coach Chuck Love. Alberts was specifically named in the lawsuit for supporting the head coach's decision, not adequately addressing the assistant's misconduct, and, in a meeting with Scoggin's parents, supporting the decision to kick Scoggin off the team for dishonesty rather than dealing with the allegation of Love's misconduct. Alberts has denied those allegations in a court filing opposing the suit, but the baggage he would have brought to his new job, so soon after Michigan's issues with former football coach Sherrone Moore, seems to have given the school's administrators enough pause to bail on Alberts.The sidebar here is that Alberts already signed a memorandum of understanding that he would be paid $17.2 million over the next five years. According to ESPN, Alberts' lawyer Tom Mars claimed that Alberts, who pronounced himself "shocked and disheartened" at the news, has not been given a reason for the school pulling out. Mars also maintained that there was no reference in the MOU to a background check. In other words, the fight isn't over the job but the money. Nothing says college sports quite like that last sentence.

item.title: Solving The Olivia Rodrigo–Taylor Swift Songwriting Credit Debate Once And For All
item.author: Patrick Redford
item.content:encoded: All of pop music can be thought of as existing on a temporal and stylistic continuum. Every up-and-coming artist is influenced to make music by the people they grew up listening to, and the truest marker of success is making music that's beloved enough to influence the next generation of musicians. In one sense, this is a straightforward description of the passage of time, but it's also the foundation of a complicated, fascinating legal space, where something like a particular yell can be thought of as proprietary. Which is all to say, I find the Taylor Swift–Olivia Rodrigo songwriting credit debate, the subject of this week's episode of , extremely fascinating. Three songs on Rodrigo's 2021 debut album , all of which was written by Rodrigo and her collaborator Dan Nigro, were the subjects of post-facto songwriting credit adjustments. Swift and her collaborators are now listed as the writers of two tracks, while two members of Paramore are listed as writers on one, despite none of them actually writing any of the material. How did something that strange happen? What does it say about the way intellectual property functions in music? Can someone own elements of a song?We got into all that and more with the great Nate Sloan and Charlie Harding of . This week's episode is the first in a three-episode, season-ending mini arc that we are calling Who Owns An Idea? The next episode is about IP theft in fashion, while the season finale is about AI.

item.title: Unmasking The International Man Of Mystery And Nets Twitter, With James Herbert And Ock Sportello
item.author: Patrick Redford
item.content:encoded: This week's episode of marks the second straight week of interviewing the author of a landmark piece of sportswriting. This time, we were joined by James Herbert, who wrote a profile of longtime NBC investigative reporter and prolific NetsDaily blogger Bob Windrem for The Ringer, as well as longtime favorite Ock Sportello, Nets fan and NetsDaily scholar. The descriptors "NBC investigative reporter" and "prolific NetsDaily blogger" both undersell Windrem. He was the first reporter to learn of Al Qaeda's role in 9/11; spent decades breaking extremely important, thorny international news stories; and also possesses perhaps the greatest corpus of knowledge on Nets of minor import, such as Sundiata Gaines, Cui Yongxi, and Milton Doyle. We spent a long time digging into the story.

Obviously, today’s single-day fall is no more definitive than yesterday’s surge. At a minimum, though, it reflects second-day realizations that there were reasons Jensen Huang was booted in the first place: the multiple investigations noted here yesterday and all the unknowns that go with them. It will take some time to see how this gambit shakes out in terms of NVIDIA’s stock price. But everything we’ve seen so far points in the direction of an extraordinary, brute-force use of presidential power to engineer a result with decidedly short-term and evanescent gains.

item.title: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries:With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library. It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians.Astra found a diary reference reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot dated five days before a date mentioned in the sketchbook at a nearby river, and suggested that Chabot's journal of his travels (only available by order from Cleveland State University) might confirm that the sketchbook was his work.Are historians due for a round of Deep Blue? Mark thinks it will be mild:But if the experience of mathematics is any guide, we can also anticipate that sometime next spring or summer we’ll face a sort of crisis of confidence as we struggle to understand how to respond to agentic systems that can do things human historians cannot. To be fair, that crisis will almost certainly be less profound for us than it is for math. The problem in mathematics, of course, is that solving hard math problems was the whole game. Historians, on the other hand, constantly reinterpret the past in light of an evolving present; we don’t chase a single universal truth. We also (in the ideal at least) write books and articles that are closer to works of philosophy and literature than they are to scientific tracts. Humanity is thus something of a requirement for the production of historical literature.

item.title: Jayden Daniels Has The Juice Again
item.author: Lauren Theisen
item.content:encoded: With under a minute to go, it looked like Washington had let the game slip through their fingers. The Cincinnati Bengals were behind 19-17 late, but they quickly got into kicking range. On second down, however, Joe Burrow lofted a pass right over the middle, and Commanders DB Rasul Douglas was in perfect position to make a clutch interception. Instead, the ball bounced off his hand, twice. To make matters worse, Douglas laid face-down on the ground in frustration after the near-pick, and the officials charged Washington with an injury timeout, their final one. They couldn't stop the clock after their third-down sack, which meant Evan McPherson's go-ahead kick passed through the uprights with only 46 seconds remaining.That was all the time that Jayden Daniels needed. Coming off a game where he threw the winning touchdown in the final minute, the Commanders QB took advantage of a prevent defense to complete two long passes over the middle, setting up Drew Stevens for the winning 26-yard kick. For the first time since the 2024 playoffs, Washington has won back-to-back games.

item.title: A Culture of Impunity Unites Trump and Tech Oligarchs
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: Blanche Reportedly Cleared HuangBut it manages to be all of those things and also a new and stunning example of the culture of impunity for the techno-authoritarian oligarchy that was heralded by President Trump’s re-election. Trump and the tech billionaires sustain and reinforce each other’s predilections for an accountability free-zone in which they can operate freely, avoid legal consequences, pay low taxes, enjoy dalliances with subordinates, and cosplay as masters of the universe.President Trump’s direct involvement in the restoration of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia is simply without precedent. Trump not only called into the meeting of the Nvidia board and all but demanded (on what terms we do not know yet) that it reinstate Huang despite his serial lying to his own directors, but he essentially leaked the news yesterday to Liz Landers of PBS before the markets opened. The opportunities for corruption around that one bit of insider information could be a whole scandal of its own.But Trump did not proceed — and may not have proceeded — without the clean bill of health that Huang received from Attorney General Todd Blanche, according to the WSJ:Over the weekend, Attorney General Todd Blanche presented an opening. The nation’s top law enforcement officer informed Trump and Vice President JD Vance on Saturday that Huang wasn’t the target or the subject of any Justice Department investigation, adding that the department had no evidence to suggest that he had broken laws or was a national security risk, according to U.S. officials.That by itself is an astounding position for the attorney general to take, given the reported intelligence concerns around Huang’s honeypot vulnerability, the national security concerns around the alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips to China in violation of export restrictions, and the attorney general’s dual role in law enforcement and counterintelligence.We may never know if what Blanche told Trump and Vance was literally true or what he thought they wanted to hear or what they told him they wanted to hear — or was made true by Trump ordering it to be so. It was not apparently the first time Trump has come to the rescue of a tech billionaire.Even as the news of Huang’s reinstatement was breaking, Trump was bragging on national TV about previously protecting Elon Musk during Trump I from unspecified accountability. It is similarly unclear whether this is a truthful recounting of an actual episode or something Trump needed or wanted to be true:I often think back to the Solyndra “scandal.” If you don’t remember, Republicans tried to made the collapse of the solar panel maker (which had received loan guarantees from the Obama administration) the signature scandal of Obama’s first term and derail his 2012 re-election. It was a byword for scandal before Benghazi. For a while, it injected “crony capitalism” into the political vernacular. It was, in Republican’s telling, everything wrong with the intersection of government and industry. And it was all bullshit.Like so much else about modern Republicanism, Solyndra was a projection. It presaged the Trump con of accusing Democrats of the precise corrupt thing he was already doing or would later go on to do. Even if everything about the made-up Solyndra scandal had turned out to be true (and, again, it wasn’t), it would be massively dwarfed by the Nvidia scandal — and a few dozen other similar Trump II depredations which has the WSJ warning about “state capitalism.”Coming into Trump II, one of the big unknowns was whether corporate America would hold the line or be coopted by the regime. We now know how quickly some companies capitulated, and how far-reaching Trump’s effort would go to cement his political power by interweaving it with direct economic control over companies and industries.I was hopeful that the midterm election shellacking marked the high water mark for Trump’s crony capitalism. But now Jensen Huang is back, and we’re in for at least another two years of this.Was Alice Huang Really a ‘Spy’?Interviews with current and former U.S. intelligence officials, lawmakers and China analysts suggest the spy-or-not-a-spy question misses a broader point. The greater challenge, they say, is that China’s intelligence services have grown so expansive and opportunistic under Xi that the line between a recruited agent and an unwitting asset has blurred—making it harder to assess the damage and easier to dismiss the threat.Raskin Targets Don Jr.’s Biz InterestsRep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD), the incoming chair of the House Judiciary Committee, is demanding information from four companies that reportedly saw big investments from Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital Management, and experienced favorable federal government actions.The companies and the actions that Raskin is interested in:: The “nascent” defense contractor received almost a billion dollars in military contracts under Trump II.: The vape company benefited from FDA authorization and approval for e-cigarette products.: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and DOJ closed investigations of the prediction market company last year, and CFTC cleared the way for it to acquire a derivatives exchange.: The online gun retailer benefitted from an ATF proposed rule that would make online firearm purchasing easier.Polygraphs for Trump Appointees at DOJ?Attorney General Todd Blanche’s chief of staff warned top DOJ political appointees that they may be polygraphed to determine who’s been leaking to the press, Bloomberg reports.Omar Hung Out To Dry by House CounselU.S. District Judge James Boasberg of D.C. ordered the unsealing of heavily redacted court filings surrounding the FBI search of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s D.C. home. Among the revelations in the unsealed filing (which did not include the search warrant itself):Prosecutors are reaching all the way back to 1980 in search of evidence that Omar, 44, has “committed [redacted] crimes over decades—beginning long before she was ever in Congress.”Ahead of the search, U.S. Magistrate Judge Matthew J. Sharbaugh ordered prosecutors to institute safeguards to prevent her legislative work from being swept up in the search, in violation of the Constitution’s Speech or Debate Clause, and expressed frustration that they didn’t initially take his concerns seriously.Sharbaugh apparently ordered prosecutors to notify House General Counsel Matthew Berry before conducting the search, but prosecutors reported that he “refused to be involved” and took the position that Speech or Debate Clause protections “do not extend to a Member’s private residence.”The House general counsel seemingly failing to come to Omar’s defense is a startling departure under Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) from the House’s usual reflexive defense of its institutional interests.

item.title: Donny’s corruption is happening right out in the open — because fuck you, that’s why
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: The thing about the Nvidia scandal is that it really has something for everyone. Do you adore crony capitalism? Are you charmed by tales of a horny CEO who can’t keep his dick in his pants? How about a Chinese spy running a honeypot operation, does that float your boat? What about a greedy, insider-trading president who gives the horny CEO a free pass to sell restricted technology to China, in return for the horny CEO ‘donating’ a twenty-five million dollars, ostensibly to pay for the vulgar Epstein Dance Hall? That shit’s cool, isn’t it?But wait, there’s more. We also have that same president shamelessly thumbing his nose in our faces about how openly corrupt he is, because .CNBC: Without your intervention, do you think Huang would've been put back in his post by the board? TRUMP: The answer is no. I believe my intervention was very important.So there we all were, yesterday morning, just hoping to make it though the day in one piece, when , we got blindsided by a shit-blizzard of fuckery. In rapid order, we first learned that Nvidia had rehired Jensen Huang to be their horny CEO. Next, we found out that it was none other than Preznit Fuckwit who had personally phoned up the board of Nvidia and strong-armed them into re-hiring Huang. Third, we learned that Donny is even more of a national security nightmare than we ever imagined.“He’s in the business of selling chips. As far as the woman is concerned, every time you have a Chinese woman that’s good-looking or beautiful, they say she’s a spy. Now with Swalwell, she probably was a spy. But with Jensen, I don’t believe that’s true. But if he sold, I don’t even know what they sold. If they sold to the company she’s with, that’s standard.”Before the scandal broke into public view, advisers to Mr. Trump told him on at least two occasions that U.S. intelligence had uncovered Ms. Huang’s links to the Chinese spy agency and that she was in a close relationship with Mr. Huang while he was still running Nvidia, according to U.S. officials with direct knowledge of the briefings.Holy shit, those are some serious allegations. I’ll bet when Donny was clued in, he sprang right into action, taking steps to tighten up national security, to keep US tech from falling into Chinese hands, like few thought possible.Spoiler alert: oh please, Dear Leader didn’t do shit.Both times, including when his national security adviser discussed it with him, the president downplayed the concerns and made clear he did not want to intervene in the matter. The officials said Mr. Trump regarded Mr. Huang as a valuable ally and Nvidia as essential to the health of the American economy and stock market.Donny let the spy allegations slide because the horny CEO was his .I have a question: why do Donny’s friends always ?Remember, the horny CEO had done Donny a solid, by ‘donating’ $25 million for the construction of the vulgar Epstein Dance Hall. And so Donny did the horny CEO a solid in return, by keeping his mouth shut about the Chinese spy allegations, and by allowing the horny CEO to go through with his plan to sell restricted chip technology to China.The company won a huge victory late Monday afternoon, when Mr. Trump declared on his social media account that he was freeing Nvidia to sell its second most powerful chip, known as the H200, to China.Isn’t it great how these oligarchs are always doing cool favors for each other, while We the People get cordially invited to go fuck ourselves, if we dare to ask for affordable healthcare? It really warms the cockles of one’s heart, let me tell you.Oh, and then there’s this: Donny’s personally invested in Nvidia, and rakes in a shitload every time their stock spikes. In fact, Donny enriched himself to the tune of fifteen mil yesterday, by getting the board of Nvidia to announce the re-hiring of Jensen Huang as their CEO You would imagine that there would be laws to prevent a president from manipulating the markets for his own personal gain, am I right? Well, of course, there — but there I go again, nattering on about stupid little things like , when Donny is A Very Special Boy Who Gets To Do Whatever The Fuck He Wants.This piece of shit rat bastard cares more about his own greedy self than he does about the national security of the country he’s somehow managed to sleaze his way back into presiding over.I can’t fucking even. I’m going to burst a blood vessel over this.Excuse me while I go scream into a pillow for about five minutes. Here’s a cute kitten gif to stare at until I get back.Wouldn’t it be great it we had a president who at least had the decency to pull this shameful skullduggery in the shadows, where it belongs? Of course, we don’t. We have a shithole president who thinks he just did an amazing thing, and so he showed up on CNBC, to take a victory lap. This corrupt fuckhead thinks he’s earned a cookie.“I’ve seen some unbelievably talented CEOs get thrown out because they were kissing somebody inappropriately at a game or something. They never got somebody back who was at good.”Listen to Jabba the Fuckface, casually dismissing predatory behavior as if it were just another day at the office. ‘When you’re a CEO, they let you.’Oh sure, who among us hasn’t been honeypotted by a Chinese agent? It happens too many times to count, am I right? Even Jimi Hendrix had that memorable line in Purple Haze, ‘scuse me while I fuck this spy.’Tell me, allowing a crony to pal around with a possible spy, because doing so is a thing you’ll personally profit off of — is that a high crime, or a misdemeanor? Or has Donny invented some new kind of offense? I guess it will be up to the next Democratic Congress to suss that out, at Donny’s upcoming impeachment trial.Oh, and then there’s this — yesterday’s Crowning Moment of What In The Actual Fuck. Is this supposed to be funny? Inspirational? Donny’s brain is fried. I don’t even think he knows why he’s mocking his own Miracle of the Magical Ear Nicking.Everything fucking sucks right now, but at least we can enjoy Fox News found object Jesse Watters being a fucking idiot.“If Oppenheimer was caught sleeping with a beautiful Japanese woman, and she was secretly passing secrets to the emperor, should Truman have fired him?”Oppenheimer WAS caught sleeping with Communist Jean Tatlock. His security clearance was pulled and he was put on trial, essentially “fired”. Waters hypothetical basically happened.That’s right, Oppenheimer get caught pulling a scuse-me-while-I-fuck-this-commie — and they yanked his security clearance and sent him packing.That’s enough for one day. Let’s Daily Claudia ourselves the hell out of here, what do you say?Here’s Ms Spouse at the Peekskill waterfront on September 5, 2016.And here’s some patio cocktail hour on June 2, 2025.Have a great Tuesday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: The Man Under the City
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: The strongest man in the world has given all for his queen. There is definitely some kind of relationship there, so they trade wishes. The queen wishes for the man to bear the burden of her city on his back. And so he does. He takes the brunt of attacks from rival armies and mythical monsters, through all kinds of weather, while she and her court enjoy the high ground. There is strategy in the upper reaches, and we even see a contrasting style to illustrate how disconnected the top is with the bottom. We know what the queen's wish is, but what is our hero's wish? We aren't going to find out, because this story does not end the way you expect it to.The animated story of The Man Under the City has layers of morality that go deeper the more you think about them. But creator DoodletmeGO tells us this is only one chapter in the legend of the strongest man in the world. (via the Awesomer)

The new chess generation’s two most exciting superstars are set to do battle in what could be the start of a rivalry that defines the next era of our beautiful game.We’ll be covering the match right here on Defector. Let’s go!

item.title: Google's Customized AI TV Channel, Starring You
item.author: Jason Koebler
item.content:encoded: We promise 404 Media will never constantly generate customized AI newsletters for you. You'll get our flawed human tastes! And like it! (Hopefully)Google has filed for a patent that would use the information it knows about you to create an AI-generated TV channel full of personalized “shows” starring you and featuring customized advertisements. The patent is the latest signal of the AI video endgame: endless highly specific, customized content that is automatically generated based on the wealth of data companies and advertisers collect about you.Tech companies regularly file for patents that they don’t end up actually putting into real products, but this one, called “creating a channel of video experiences tailored to a user,” describes a system that many AI companies have been clearly trying to build. It imagines something called “My Channel,” which would be filled with AI content generated based on demographic data, their video watch history (presumably from YouTube), and other information it knows about the user. It would then make “the user as the protagonist for the whole video.” The patent was first noticed by Patentlyze, a news site that tracks tech company patents, who shared it with 404 Media.“You are a customized video generating model. Generate a customized video for a user where the user will play the protagonist,” a hypothetical LLM prompt in the patent reads. “The generated customized video includes characteristics based on the <user_profile>. The generated customized video follows the style and format of the <top_ watches> of the user. The generated customized video sticks to the <preferred_genres> of the user but the narrative for the generated customized video is customized. The <top watches> and <preferred _genres> parameters are ordered from more preferred to less preferred.”It suggests that the channel would be connected to an “advertising server,” and that advertisements would be inserted into the customized AI content: “an advertising stitcher included in the advertising server generates an updated customized media content item by inserting at least one advertisement into the customized media content item,” it says. The patent imagines, for example, “a crime/comedy caper,” “a fun romantic comedy,” “a sci-fi adventure,” and “an action/thriller experience” with a viewer named “John” as the protagonist. Another prompt included in the patent suggests that someone who had recently watched cricket highlights of a “Player 1” might then be served a similar video “that incorporates elements of the Cricket World Cup and Player 1’s recent performance. Perhaps [user_name] could be cheering for India in the stands or interacting with Player 1 in some way.” The notable thing about this patent is that it is barely an evolution of what is already happening on social media and what is beginning to happen on streaming free TV channels on services like Samsung TV Plus and TCLtv+. The people generating AI slop on social media are making incredibly specific content because they know that social media algorithms will be highly effective at filtering people there. Meta is already allowing advertisers to use AI to generate many slightly different versions of an advertisement; its targeting AI then automatically shows them to users who are most likely to react to a specific version of an ad. As I’ve previously reported, TCL has been experimenting with AI-generated content on its streaming free TV channels, and, even without AI-generated content, free streaming TV channels have gotten incredibly specific. It is now possible, for example, to watch reruns of individual shows 24/7/365. AI boosters have long been saying the future of entertainment is allowing anyone to generate their own TV shows, or to generate “new” episodes of existing properties. An always-on, autogenerating, customized AI TV channel isn’t far off from that idea. As I’ve previously argued, the future that tech companies envision is one in which we are somehow even more siloed than we are now. They imagine a world in which everyone lives in their own reality and watches their own, customized content, which is a world in which big, unifying pieces of media are harder to make and are few and far between. The Google patent comes on the heels of a Microsoft patent that describes a system that alters spoken words (and the person’s lips) in live video, thereby distorting reality.University Approves Nuclear Weapons Data Center, Township Vows to Fight OnLast week, the University of Michigan’s board of regents approved the construction of a $1.25 billion data center that will power American nuclear weapons research. The regents voted 7 - 1 in a public meeting on November 19 to move forward with the project despite widespread opposition from faculty, staff, and the residents of Ypsilanti Township, Michigan where the data center will operate. A few hours after the vote, the leaders and citizens of the Township gathered to discuss how to stop it.University of Michigan Mailer Promises Its Data Center Isn’t Really a Data Center:And, related, over the past month, the University of Michigan sent postcards and pamphlets to people in Michigan telling them its new data center is “NOT a commercial data center” and is, instead, a “research computing center.” According to one of the postcards viewed by 404 Media, the University’s data center will “advance breakthrough research in medicine, clean energy, cybersecurity, and engineering,” and "accelerate discoveries like new drug therapies and cancer treatments that improve people’s lives.” The University's postcard also promised to create 300 “high-quality union jobs during development” and “preserve approximately 80% of the 124-acre property as green space.”The biggest story in the tech world is, once again, Nvidia and the Jensen Huang scandal. Outside of mentioning it in this newsletter, we haven’t really been covering this. The main reason is that these are one of the few types of stories that we’re not really set up to do. Nvidia is technically the most valuable company on the planet, and so other bigger news outlets have a bunch of reporters who are dedicated to covering just Nvidia. When a scandal like this breaks, they throw entire news teams at it. It just doesn’t really make sense for us to try to compete with our smaller team. The New York Times, Bloomberg, The Information, and the Wall Street Journal (and lots of other outlets) are all over this. It does feel bad to more or less sit out such a big news story, and it’s not that we don’t think this scandal is important. It’s just that we are usually trying to break new ground, and it’s hard to do that when hundreds of other reporters are laser focused on the same scandal. We reserve the right to jump in at any time, especially with a reported take or something like this. I do think it’s depressing that this has become a culture war thing, and an opportunity for Silicon Valley VCs and billionaires to do class solidarity and try to show that there should be no consequences whatsoever for bad behaving CEOs. I think the Trump and essentially stock market by blackmail aspect of it all is quite worrisome, too. Huang’s return raises all sorts of national security concerns, corruption concerns, and questions about how (much more) subservient Huang will be to Trump now that he’s done him a massive favor. I also found this exchange to be upsetting on many levels. Also, this post from Balaji, one of the worst to ever do it, is wildly deranged and will probably make your blood boil. Anyways, that’s enough of that for the moment. Here’s what else is going on.In a move that should probably surprise no one, Facebook has suspended the largest DeFlock account, called DeFlock America. It had more than 800,000 members. I’m trying to report out how this happened, so if you know more please let me know. I figured it was only a matter of time until Flock tried to get the social media platforms to prevent Flock content from circulating widely.Greg Otto, my old colleague, friend, and fellow security reporter, tried an experiment. Could he, a guy who writes about cybersecurity but who doesn’t know how to do cybersecurity, use AI to find and report a real vulnerability? The answer is yes. I thought his experiment was really interesting and well done, and raises questions about just how bad the AI-powered hacking scene is going to get. I found this Reddit thread about the best film camera to take on an ultramarathon through the Sahara desert to be useless to me as someone who is not going to be running an ultramarathon in the Sahara desert but also fascinating in a living vicariously kinda way.Gratuitous Mamdani content: I don’t live in New York City anymore but my extremely specific beef since I moved is how insanely expensive Citi Bike bikeshare has become. It makes me unreasonably angry every time I go back and visit. And so of course Mamdani is capping the prices of Citi Bike rides. I think someday at 404 we’ll have more public transit/housing/urban design content. This is a few days old and has already caused a big kerfuffle, but shout out to our friends at US PIRG for their Trouble in Toyland report, which led to several AI-enabled toys being pulled from the shelves for being dangerous and/or doing sexually explicit chats.This guy hacked an iPod Nano 5G from 2009: No AI appears to have been used here and it’s a fun little writeup, so figured I’d flag.

item.title: University of Michigan Mailer Promises Its Data Center Isn’t Really a Data Center
item.author: Matthew Gault
item.content:encoded: Over the past month, the University of Michigan sent postcards and pamphlets to people in Michigan telling them its new data center is “NOT a commercial data center” and is, instead, a “research computing center.”According to one of the postcards viewed by 404 Media, the University’s data center will “advance breakthrough research in medicine, clean energy, cybersecurity, and engineering,” and "accelerate discoveries like new drug therapies and cancer treatments that improve people’s lives.” The University's postcard also promised to create 300 “high-quality union jobs during development” and “preserve approximately 80% of the 124-acre property as green space.”One of U of M’s mailers said the building will not operate as a commercial data center. “This facility will not support streaming, entertainment, social media, or e-commerce,” it said. It also said the facility will not “burden the local community with the cost of its energy or water use, drain resources from the local community or raise utility rates,” or “create smoke, odors, or significant noise.”The University it’s not sure how much water the data center will use but that it could be as much as 650,000 gallons a day. It also said it’s “evaluating several cooling techniques to identify the most efficient approach,” a process that “includes continued evaluation of reclaimed wastewater for cooling, which would significantly reduce demand on municipal potable water supply systems.”In April, the Township’s utilities authority on delivering water to data center projects while it studied how they might impact the community’s water supply. In response, U of M sent a letter to the Township utility board . Concerned Township residents have spent the past year strategizing with community leaders about how to delay or stop construction. The Township’s anger caught U of M off guard and it attempted to address community concerns in . It hasn’t gone well.The pamphlet attempted to contextualize the data center’s place in America’s nuclear weapons research. “It would not involve nuclear weapons manufacturing, physical weapons testing, or the storage of hazardous nuclear materials,” the pamphlet said. But it would help “improve cybersecurity practices to safely manage existing nuclear material out of state.” In January, LANL confirmed its portion of the data center would be used for nuclear weapons research.U of M did not return 404 Media’s request for comment.On November 19, the board of regents of development for the data center in a . The same night, Ypsilanti Township hosted a panel discussion about the data center where its leaders promised to continue to fight. “We have a number of strategies right now that we’re going to be pursuing,” Township attorney Douglas Winters said at the panel. “We believe that U of M has gone far afield when it comes to the constitutional autonomy which they have enjoyed by virtue of being a university.”

item.title: 8Ball & MJG – On Top Of The World (October 31,1995)
item.author: deedub77
item.content:encoded: Once upon a time in a land called Memphis lived two greasy-headed street hustlers named Premro Smith and Marlon Jermaine Goodwin. They were small-time pimps and petty crime perpetrators, aimlessly moving through life looking for their next scheme. Until that fateful day, they discovered hip-hop and microphones in their Orange Mound neighborhood. With these microphones came the gift of gab over beats, and their lives would never be the same. Premro would become 8Ball, and Marlon would transform into MJG, known collectively as…8Ball & MJG, of course. The dynamic duo would begin their quest, spewing raw pimp poetry over hard beats. A few years later, they would embark on their next adventure, making their metamorphosis from hoe-smackin’ flesh-peddlers to players with a purpose, providing a pimpology course so that the blacks can one day rule the nation. That leads us to their third musical excursion, .Their junior odyssey would become more successful than their previous two escapades, receiving an abundance of adoration from fans and, in turn, being showered with gold from the music gods. Today, I’ll go back to 1995 and revisit 8Ball & MJG’s third musical mission as I continue my trip through two-thirds of the Sesshead Funk Brothers hip-hop journey. – MJG returns with the distorted Grim Reaper voice he used for the intro and welcomes us to the album over ghoulishly cinematic music. Now, on with the show. – T-Mix unleashes a pristine and sexy G-Funk banger that the self-proclaimed “Break-A-Bitch scholars” use to talk shit, but mostly to spew their slick Memphis pimpology. This was complete fire. – Well, you can start by putting a question mark at the end of the song title. 8 and M rap from the perspective of conflicted drug dealers looking for a legit hustle but are still enticed by the fast money that comes in the streets. It’s a compelling cautionary tale backed by a muscular T-Mix beat. – T-Mix’s instrumental has a smooth R&B aura that I’m sure Mary J. Blige would have made magic with. Instead, 8 and M get a hold of it and make their own Memphis voodoo. MJG sounds good over the creamy instrumental, but 8Ball sounds spectacular. – Our hosts spit a PSA on the dangers of using cocaine/crack over a semi-solemn, partially bluesy musical bed. They sound a little preachy and hypocritical (MJG admits to once trying “fry” (which I’m assuming is slang for crack), and 8Ball shows understanding for the crack dealer. Yet neither shows empathy for the user). But they avoid sounding corny, and I agree with the message. The Pookie from clip was a nice addition to close the record and introduce the next track. – This amazing T-Mix production sounds like it could be the father of OutKast’s “SpottieOttieDopaliscious” instrumental. And the emcees for the night proceed to do what the song title suggests. – 8 and M question whether the people in their circle are loyal or modern-day Judases. Ironically, they invite a few so-called friends to join in on the commentary: E-40 (who mistakes being molested at 5 years old by his babysitter as getting “vicious head”), Mac Mall, and Big Mike, while Rodney Ellis sings the hook. 8 and M deliver the best verses, which made me wonder why 8Ball didn’t take his own advice and “trust few” to join him on this record. Then I wouldn’t have had to listen to an annoying rubber-mouth verse from one of my least favorite rappers on the planet. – Both of our hosts dive deep into their criminal bags and blame Lucifer for their violent actions (at least 8Ball does some self-analysis, briefly questioning why he’s compelled to do the evil things he does). The duo’s devious deeds are scored by demented, devilish laughter and a deep mid-tempo funk groove suitable for midnight marauding, and apparently, robbing and murdering. – The title track finds 8Ball & MJG in celebratory mode as they revel in their rise to the top of the game. The breezy backdrop feels as warm as a summer day, and the simple talkbox hook brings everything together like the zipper on a butter leather (shoutout to Black Thought). – The first thing I saw was the missing question mark at the end of the song title. 8Ball & MJG are joined by the female duo Nuckle Heads (Lez Mone and RacQuel Gemini), and they make quite the first impression with their self-proclaimed “Tomboyish ass flow.” As dope as the ladies sound on the mic, 8Ball cuts the head off of T-Mix’s rugged instrumental, rapping on a completely different plane than his counterparts. – Some topics in hip-hop are evergreen. Racist cops mistreating black men in America is one of them. Our hosts voice their frustration on the matter, spewing verbal venom at the perpetrating pigs. T-Mix builds the tension with a menacing instrumental that uses electric, howling synth chords on the hook that scream brutality. – Someone must have laced 8 and M’s weed with PCP, as it’s got 8Ball talking about squarin’ up with Paul Bunyan and being pussy whipped by Medusa. Meanwhile, MJG’s having illusions of being served breakfast and anything else he desires by a bikini-clad woman who looks like Jeannie (the character Barbara Eden, a slept-on sixties baddie, played in ), and making pimp anthems with Quincy Jones. South Circle (Mr. Mike and Thorough, the latter of whom appeared on “Lay It Down”) join in on the fun. But it sounds like they got the memo about the song’s concept a little late (they both get two cracks at the mic, and only Thorough plays along with the fantasy idea on his second verse; Mike completely missed the mark with the song idea, but his cadence and swag sound great). The instrumentation on this record was incredible: a bop with West Coast sensibilities, splashes of jazzy keys, and a killer rock guitar solo to close things out. – 8 and M reflect on their journey from starving artists to bonafied rap stars. Their bars are scored by a fitting instrumental that captures the essence of survival and triumph. – I loved what 8Ball and MJG did on “Middle Of The Night” from MJG’s solo debut . This breezy pimp ballad may have been the blueprint for the former. Except for the last minute of the record, which features a cringe vocal solo from the track’s featured guest (Nina Creque), it was smooth and pleasant.– Our hosts wrap by blessing one more T-Mix heater with their Memphis slang. Correction: MJG blesses it. 8Ball murders it.In 1991, 8Ball & MJG came out hard, spitting raw and edgy pimp poetry over Tony Draper’s fiscally responsible but effective production. Two years later, they returned to give us a glimpse into their world from the outside looking in as they slowly began to blossom into critical-thinking militant pimps with something to say. Both albums were solid in their own right, but like a white girl’s legs in Minnesota winters, they pale in comparison to .T-Mix puts his foot in the production on relying heavily on a West Coast G-Funk sound. It’s all fire, and similar to , the heat comes in different levels, and it’s all edible. A handful come with Reaper heat and are absolute bangers.While T-Mix is busy concocting the perfect production package for the album, 8Ball & MJG fine-tune their chemistry and get it running at optimal performance. They continue to shed the “bitch smackin’” pimp personas they came out hard with, spending a minimal amount of bars on chicks and misogyny. Their focus is meaty verses, balanced with straight emcee spit. I mentioned during my review that 8Ball began widening the gap between his and MJG’s rhyming ability. On , the self-proclaimed Southern Funkadelic Preacher rhymes in a completely different stratosphere than his partner. Yet, I enjoyed their synergy because every Batman needs a Robin.-DeedubFollow me on Instagram @damontimeisillmatic

item.title: I knew this moment was coming
item.author: 1axcb35wxctebypdn4e7blzn87nqqghm9pzroj@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: It is not always easy to understand what Donald Trump intends to do, but it is always easy to tell when he is worried. Right now, he is terrified of congressional oversight, and he is keeping every option open to block it.Trump's second term has been the most corrupt in American history. Barely a week goes by without news of another scheme to enrich him, his family or his advisers.Corporate leaders have showered him and his causes with gifts. Foreign governments and their leaders have poured money into his family's crypto venture, provided a $400 million luxury jet for his use, and invested alongside his relatives.Then there are the Epstein files. Congress passed bipartisan legislation requiring their release, only to see the Justice Department answer with heavy redactions and millions of withheld pages, in a file that mentions Trump thousands of times.It is no wonder that Trump is worried. He has good reason to be.His administration has been preparing for this moment for months.

item.title: Drawing fish scale tiles with Python
item.author: Alex Chan
item.content:encoded: My friend Madeline has some kitchen tiles that look a bit like fish scales. The pattern is multiple rows of overlapping circles, every other row offset by half a circle, where the top half of one circle overlaps the bottom quarters of two circles in the row above. It adds a pop of colour to the backsplash:I really like this pattern, and I’ve considered getting it in my own kitchen – but until I can redecorate, I wanted to recreate the effect digitally. I got close a few years ago, when experimenting with circle-based art for the header of this website, but the scales were diagonal rather than horizontal.I was able to draw the horizontal rows with a small tweak to the original script, adjusting the centres of where the circles get drawn.Like my previous art in this vein, I’m using varied shades of a single tint colour rather than a discrete palette. This loses the shape of some of the individual tiles, because they blend into a similar shade in the next tile.I ran another experiment where I used the tint colour as “grout” to add a border between tiles. I like this effect in the lighter tiles, but darker tiles can still blur the edges between shapes:I think you could make this pattern work, possibly by using an edge colour that doesn’t appear on any of the tiles, but I didn’t pursue the idea further.Alternatively, I could switch to a discrete palette. If you have more than a handful of colours, the four colour theorem tells us that it’s always possible to find a colouring where adjacent tiles never have the same colour. Notice that’s how Madeline’s tiles behave – she has five different colours, and the same colour never touches itself.I’ve never tried to use that approach in generative art. The theorem only states that it’s always to find a colouring, but you can’t just pick colours at random and expect it to work. Maybe that will be my next project.If you’d like to try to play with these designs yourself, you can download my code.

item.title: The Guest Room
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Excuse me, I'm a grandma, and have hardly any of these things in my guest rooms. They are basically my kids' rooms, with mostly their stuff in them. Well, okay, I have the classic books, but it's because I can only carry so many books to the dump every year. The loud ticking clock was left over from when I had elderly foreign visitors once, and it was recently removed. Any dolls were the kids', not mine. Same with the artworks. The heat is the guests' problem; there is a separate system and thermostat upstairs. I guess a lot of this stuff in Matt Shirley's floor plan are things grandma wants to keep, but doesn't want to look at, so it goes in the guest room. I don't do much of that since I'd have to haul it upstairs.

item.title: datasette-charts 0.2a0
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: I introduced this new charting plugin for Datasette yesterday. Today it's gained integration with Datasette Agent, so now you can ask chat for a chart and it will create one for you using the same underlying chart suggestion and generation tools.Here's a demo video, recorded on agent.datasette.io where you can sign in with GitHub to try the plugin yourself: I prompt Datasette Agent to "Use #stats to show sqlite-utils downloads over time as a chart" - where typing "#stats" opens a table search box. It shows me a chart inline in the chat, and when I click "Open in the chart builder" it opens the chart in a panel along with the table page. I use the table page to switch to a chart of "datasette", then when I ask the agent "what does the chart show?" it notices that I changed the content in the panel and describes the new Datasette chart to me.

This version improves navigation by fragment hashes, for deeper integration with other Datasette plugins that update fragment hashes when the user interacts with the plugin in a way that changes state.

item.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this:In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count.This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said:Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality.GLM 5.4 is not yet available as open weights:We plan to open-source the model weights responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening.I tried it out using the Z.ai API, for which I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API.It turns out both coding plan and regular API share the same OpenAI-compatible Responses API (at ), and the API key for the coding plan worked with that and gave me access to the new model.I built a llm-glm plugin, then realized that llm-zai by Tommy Hughes already exists! I've shipped mine purely because doesn't yet support the new model, but I'll likely retire mine once that plugin catches up.I realized I never ran pelicans for GLM-5.3, so here those are for the same effort levels. They look similar in quality to 5.4.It's interesting how GLM 5.1 and GLM 5.2 produced radically different pelicans from other models. The pelicans for 5.3 and 5.4 are much more comparable to those I get from OpenAI or Anthropic models - the previous generations had their own distinctive look.I made a comparison grid showing the four generations of GLM pelicans all in one place. The style transition between 5.2 and 5.3 is pretty stark.

item.title: Trump’s stacking the courts. We’re fighting back.

item.content:encoded: Too often, the courts are an afterthought. item.title: Ladybird's first alpha release
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird's even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS.I've been trying it out today, and it's very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I've tried to load in it have worked as they should. It looks like this (showing my video-compressor tool):Here's the process tree after I opened six tabs in one window and another tab in a second window (generated by this script, thanks Claude):Ladybird (72925) [240 MB] └── Hub (72926) [61 MB] ├── RequestServer (72927) [29 MB] ├── ProcessReaper (72928) [1 MB] ├── Compositor (72930) [123 MB] ├── RequestServer (72953) [36 MB] ├── WebContent (72984) [819 MB] ├── MediaServer (73006) [118 MB] ├── VideoDecoderServer (73007) [20 MB] ├── WebContent (73052) [144 MB] ├── WebContent (73057) [73 MB] ├── WebContent (73073) [166 MB] ├── WebContent (73094) [70 MB] ├── WebContent (73112) [116 MB] ├── RequestServer (73113) [27 MB] └── WebContent (73185) [60 MB]Ladybird runs different tabs in different processes, an isolation mechanism used by most browsers (well, technically Chrome uses a process-per-site).I tried Ladybird against several of my more advanced tool examples - like the video-compressor shown above, which runs ffmpeg compiled to WebAssembly. I had it resize its own screenshot using my image-resize tool. It happily runs my Pyodide REPL (Python compiled to WebAssembly) too.The one thing I tried that didn't work was Datasette Lite, which runs Pyodide in a complicated arrangement of service workers and web workers. Attempting to start Datasette Lite displays this error:undefined is not a function (evaluated from 'navigator.serviceWorker.startMessages')The project has been leaning heavily into coding agents this year. On February 23, 2026 Andreas Kling published Ladybird adopts Rust, with help from AI, describing how they ported parts of their LibJS JavaScript engine from C++ to 25,000 lines of Rust in two weeks using Claude Code and Codex.That uptick in October corresponds to the landing of a wealth of big improvements.How did they do that? Coding agents:Most of that gain came in five days, from about 2.12 million on October 22 to about 2.18 million on October 27. We pointed AI coding agents at WPT and asked them to fill in missing functionality. They made lots of small fixes, and those added up. Our biggest gains for the month were about 30,000 in and 10,000 in .I'm interested in what models they are using here - I know Andreas uses Codex and Claude Code, but I haven't seen him talk about specific model versions. Claude Opus 5.5 came out on September 22, 2026 and Claude Fable 5.2 on November 9, 2026 (after that window). I'd love to know what they were using for that huge leap in the last week of October.Here's what Andreas says about Ladybird's suitability for use as a daily browser:This is an alpha, so some websites won’t work, and it will crash sometimes. When that happens, tell us! You can report a broken site from inside the browser. After a crash, you can read the crash report and decide whether to send it. Our privacy policy has the details.We want security nerds to hack it! A new browser gets hacked, over and over, and that’s part of the process, so we make no promises about security today. When you pwn us, please tell us how so we can harden Ladybird!Given how hard it is to secure a web browser, and the hostility of the environment they operate in, I won't be using Ladybird to sign into GitHub or Gmail or any of my other sensitive accounts.I'm going to keep it around for anonymous browsing though, partly to participate in the testing efforts but mainly because it gives me a glimmer of optimism to see a promising new entrant in the stagnant browser engine market start to grow its wings.

item.title: NWSL Players Association Has Concerns About Bay FC’s Treatment Of Players Who Have Taken Maternity Leave
item.author: Abigail Segel
item.content:encoded: The NWSL Players Association is concerned that Bay FC violated two different sections of the league’s collective bargaining agreement related to parental rights, according to PA Executive Director Meghann Burke. One of the sections is about non-discrimination, and one is about parental leave in the case that it overlaps with an expiring contract. The union is evaluating if there is enough information to file a grievance.On Nov. 13, Bay announced its end-of-season roster updates. Three players who are new mothers—Caprice Dydasco, Abby Dahlkemper, and Emily Menges—were out of contract with the club and would not be re-signed. “On its face, we’re concerned there were three moms under contract with Bay who gave birth and were on maternity leave, and none of them are returning next season,” Burke told Defector. “Right away, that sort of raises an index of suspicion, where you try and understand what’s going on.”

item.title: The Directing Genius of Akira Kurosawa Explained

item.content:encoded: This video from StudioBinder looks at how Akira Kurosawa made his films.In this video essay, we break down Kurosawa’s filmmaking techniques across Seven Samurai, High and Low, Rashomon, Ikiru, Yojimbo, and more. From dynamic blocking and layered composition to bold movement and weather-driven cinematography, Kurosawa didn’t just direct scenes — he engineered visual storytelling with precision.
