item.title: Award: Here for It, #368
item.author: SRS0=2yBh=JM=m.ghost.io=bounce+3cffae.7bdc18-misc=muneer.top@eforward.registrar-servers.com
item.content:encoded: Hi! It's R. Eric Thomas. From the internet?Hi!I feel sure that I've written about my deep love of awards shows in this newsletter before but I cannot find it and so maybe I dreamt it. Maybe I've dreamt this entire newsletter! (It's truly amazing how much useless stuff I get done in my dreams. Last week, I attended an entire conference in my dream. My schedule included plenaries and an award dinner. A man next to me at the award dinner repeatedly told me that he was playing "John Travolta in He seemed very proud of it. I was not and am not sure if he was playing John Travolta in a movie about the making of or if he was just playing the John Travolta role in the 1999 stage adaptation of said film. What's crazy about dreams is that there is no way for me to find the answers to this question because it all came from inside my head, objectively a confusing and chaotic environment!)Anyway, my favorite award show is the Barrymores, the regional theater awards for the Philadelphia community. I've gone to the Barrymores since 2013 and it's consistently one of the highlights of my year. (And I include the year I won a Barrymore and also the year I ate something I was allergic to at the afterparty, went into anaphylactic shock and had to go to the emergency room. It's called having range!)In 2013, I was a marketing assistant at a local theater company and I somehow got to go to the Theatre Prom, and I had a transformational experience. I'd spent the previous 7 years in Philadelphia trying to make in-roads into the community and often feeling like I was failing at it. What I realized that night was that being a part of the community wasn't about one particular place or accomplishment or career milestone. It was on-going and ever-changing and, at that moment, was centered around wearing my one (1) suit and devouring the mac and cheese buffet.Three years later, I'd win a Barrymore Award for Best New Play. That was a great night, but--no shade--there was no mac and cheese bar and so the overall experience was a mixed bag.I've since been nominated six more times but never won again. (Yes, the authorities are looking into it. We're expecting charges from the Justice Department any day.) But I go back every year because I think of the "Theatre Prom" more as a wedding. You go to a wedding to celebrate the couple, sure, but at the best weddings you're also reminded of the beauty of your own life and your own love and your own joy and the privilege of being with people you love and strangers who love the same thing you love. And you get a free meal and an open bar if you want it and you're wearing fancy clothes and you get to hear the Cha-Cha Slide which, shockingly, one does not encounter in everyday life. And that's what you're really there for. I love enthusiasm. And I love the improbable idea that that which you love can somehow love you back.And so it was improbable and lovely in equal measure that my friend Robi Hager texted me and told me that he was directing this year's Barrymore Awards and that he had a big, ambitious vision and part of that vision was me hosting. He said, "I want you to be Neil Patrick Harris at the Tonys." The Barrymores were last week and, beloved, let me tell you--this was the hardest thing I've ever done professionally and I once had an emotionally ruinous Zoom call with Lee Daniels, director of It was also one of the highlights of my life (the Barrymores. Not that Zoom. Sheesh!)Robi wanted me to co-write an opening number in addition to doing a comic monologue to start the show. I said, "I don't sing and dance." He said, "I believe in you," and, alas, people believing in me is my Kryptonite.I co-wrote an opening song with Jake Collins and then rehearsed a performance choreographed by Devon Sinclair. Y'all, they had ya boy out here doing time steps! (And if you don't know what a time step is, you and I are the same! I have neither a formal theater education nor significant lung capacity. Ya boy was on life support!)Erik Larson immediately saw the vision and decided to design and hand-make six different outfits for me to wear. Every time I hit the stage, I was in a different look.Erik quipped that I was Neil Patrick Hairless. And our friend Alex followed up with Neil Black-trick Harris. And I've spent the entire weekend trying to come up with a third play on words. The best I can do is Key and Peele Patrick Harris but I want you to know that I'm not proud of it and I'm not happy about it.Every single moment was simultaneously so hard and so revelatory. Robi and Erik and Devon and Jake saw something in me that I didn't. I have no problem hosting something. It doesn't feel haughty to say I'm good at holding a mic and telling jokes and occasionally running a live auction. If I'm doing a book event, we're going to have a great time. But singing, dancing, starting a kick-line on the correct foot, doing a quick change, doing six quick changes--all of that felt ambitious.I'm an ambitious person but I'm also lazy. But I like being around people who have large ambitions, because it makes your ambitions seem right-sized. It makes you want to expand, to do and dream and achieve more. And that feels like magic. If I'm challenged by people who have my back and can guide me when I don't know where to go, the challenge can elevate me as opposed to stymieing me.There's nothing wrong with a challenge, but you need support, mentorship, and other people who get the idea. I love to be around people whose ambitions outpace mine because then I think, "why am I dreaming so small? It's my life. How dare I put a limit on any part of it?"It's important to make a fuss; it's important to put a marker in time and say "I was here and it was hard or it was easy or it was fun or there was free mac and cheese." It's important to care. And sometimes that means just showing up and enjoying yourself and sometimes that means putting a gigantic bow on your butt and joining a kick-line. Congratulations to everyone who is trying, including the random guy from my dream. Can't wait to see , whatever that means.Tickets for Variety Pack: Volume 4 are now on sale! Four days, twelve shows, all comedy! Come check us out January 14-18, 2027!alas, people believing in me is my Kryptonite,Eric

item.title: datasette-charts 0.1a0
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: I've been thinking about this problem for over a year now, but on Sunday I finally fired up Claude Fable 5.2 to build an initial prototype. The prototype went so well that this is now a full plugin.The new charts plugin works against any table or arbitrary SQL query in Datasette. It defines several different chart types (using vendored D3, Observable Plot, and topojson-client), each with a set of heuristics for identifying when they might be a good match for a specific set of rows.Those suggestion thumbnails at the top are actual visualizations driven by the data, and selecting one pulls up the full chart along with tools for modifying it. You can also manually construct a chart from scratch.As with other Datasette visualization plugins, the current state of your chart is persisted in a in the URL - so you can bookmark charts or share them with others.The most important feature is that the charts take . Previous charting plugins like datasette-vega would only show charts for the current page of results, generally up to 100 rows.The new plugin compiles each chart to a SQL query that aggregates across the entire result set (potentially millions of rows) using GROUP BY, time bucketing, and window functions. Each query returns a result capped at 5,000 rows, suitable for display on the chart. The plugin uses sampling to help suggest charts for larger tables without evaluating the full result set.I'm really happy with this initial release of the plugin. It's still very much an alpha, but it's the closest I've got to the dream of Datasette helping visualize data with as little required direction from the user as possible.

item.title: Kansas City Broke Through The Noise
item.author: Abigail Segel
item.content:encoded: Kansas City wanted blood. Knowing the Washington Spirit would look to dazzle home fans with pretty football, and knowing those fans—desperate for a championship after two consecutive final defeats—would be loud and temperamental, the Current set out to disrupt, disrupt, disrupt. Laney Rouse, the Current’s only starting rookie, took the first kill. Washington was coming off an early attacking sequence when the ball bounced over toward the sideline. Trinity Rodman set herself up for the trap, but Rouse had already gathered her momentum and crashed into Rodman’s back like a wrecking ball. The face of the Washington Spirit tumbled, hard. Rouse got away without seeing a card, and the home fans were apoplectic. Rodman didn’t get up for minutes. Rodman’s health was key to the Spirit’s success this year. In 2025, she missed months while struggling with a back injury and only appeared for 35 total minutes in the postseason. But after an offseason in which she chose Washington and the power of her stardom changed the league itself, she found her groove. A deserving MVP nominee, Rodman notched 13 goals and eight assists in the regular season and didn’t miss a match. The sight of Rodman floundering about on the ground was nightmarish for fans at Audi Field.

item.title: 63 years ago today...
item.author: Minnesotastan
item.content:encoded: I remember exactly where I was. I was on my high school's debate team and we were off at a tournament. For practical reasons, our coach always drove us to tournaments; he would then serve as a judge on some of the debates not involving us, and we would all gather after the last debate of the day in some barren classroom to hear the results announced and get feedback on our performances. On that day, after the last afternoon debate, he didn't meet us. After a brief search, we found him in his car, listening to the news on the car radio, in tears. The news itself was startling, but the sight of encountering one of the pillars of the school faculty, our history teacher, unabashedly crying made the moment surreal for me. As I was writing this, I decided to look up the National Forensic League's official debate topic for that year. I remembered speaking as Second Affirmative, but didn't remember the topic. Here it is: 1963-1964Resolved: That Social Security benefits should be extended to include complete medical care. Wow. How's that for a relevance stretching half a century into the future. I wish I still had my file box of 3x5 cards. Readers who have sharp memories of 11/22/63 are welcome to offer them in the Comments. from 2013 to invite additional reflections and memories.

item.title: Are The Knicks Back?
item.author: Rachelle Hampton
item.content:encoded: Within the first three minutes of playing time in Saturday night’s game against the Portland Trail Blazers, I found myself wondering (and maybe even hoping): Are the Knicks back? My suspicions had started to rise only sometime in the last week, somewhere between the reigning champs' back-to-back victories against the Raptors and their hard-fought win against the Timberwolves. It was in the second game against the Raptors that I started to see glimmers of what could make this current New York roster so magical to watch; that was the same game where Karl-Anthony Towns declared that his team, after a sleepy start to the season, was finally playing “like the Knicks again … with that physicality and that energy that made us so special last year.”So when I saw that KAT, one of the few bright spots of consistency in this season so far, along with the steadfast, laconic OG Anunoby, were both out for Saturday night’s game against Portland, my first thought was lol, we’re 100 percent going to lose. Then I saw that Deni Avdija was cleared to return to the Blazers after missing the last two games, and I thought, Oh, so we’re 1,000 percent going to lose. Even without Avdija, the Blazers had been surprisingly competitive, led offensively by a newly returned Damian Lillard.

item.title: Ramaswamy’s ad exposes MAGA’s obsession with parental estrangement
item.content:encoded: As soon as Vivek Ramaswamy released an ad celebrating a woman accused of backing a fugitive rapist, the widespread assumption among the pundit class was that it would backfire on him. Ohio’s Republican gubernatorial candidate is falling behind in the polls against his Democratic opponent, Dr. Amy Acton, in a race that threatens to turn long-red Ohio blue.In a move reeking of desperation, Ramaswamy’s campaign ran a spot featuring Acton’s elderly mother, Donna Arthur, calling her daughter a “liar” and suggesting she suffers from severe mental illness. But it took almost no time at all before the record was widely corrected, with extensive media reports showing the facts in black-and-white: In 1978, Arthur sided with her husband, Cledith, when he was charged with raping his 12-year-old stepdaughter Amy. Acton has not seen her mother since the Arthurs fled Ohio in an effort to evade justice nearly five decades ago. Her brother confirmed what both Acton and court records show, calling the Ramaswamy campaign “despicable.” The news that the GOP nominee was championing an abusive mother over her daughter quickly became the media narrative, leading to multiple predictions that the ad would backfire on Ramaswamy.And yet MAGA leaders, including President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, are doubling down on the ad. At a Wednesday campaign event in Cincinnati, Vance praised Ramaswamy for his “audacity to run a TV commercial which calls it out like it is,” despite there being no evidence that Acton lied about her rape and ample evidence — such as fleeing the state — that the Arthurs did. On Wednesday, Trump defended the ad, saying, “It’s very unusual for a mother to hate her daughter, but I don’t think that has anything to do with Vivek.”The president escalated his rhetoric on Thursday, posting on Truth Social, “let everyone listen to the mother of a defective, dishonest, and incapable Candidate.” In Iowa on Thursday, Trump went further, calling Ramaswamy “lucky” to have this situation to exploit, and that he should thank “God” for the favor. The reason is grim political strategy. With Trump’s approval ratings hitting record new lows by the day, Republicans feel their only hope to eke out victories in close midterm races is to juice MAGA turnout. Demonizing an adolescent rape victim is a likely two-fold play; it could energize the same people who are currently attacking Jane Doe, the Cornell gang rape accuser.But the framing of Ramaswamy’s ad also suggests there is another audience his campaign has in mind: aging MAGA voters who are obsessively angry about the phenomenon of parental estrangement. As I documented in an extensive 2024 report, right-wing media frequently runs scare stories about adult children who cut off their parents, a phenomenon that gets blamed on therapists, progressive ideology and social decay supposedly producing selfish children — but never the parents themselves. Just this year alone, Fox News has run multiple stories blaming “cutoff culture,” “social contagion,” “social media” and “ungrateful” children for parental estrangement. Earlier this month, the conservative National Review castigated children who go no-contact for being too poisoned by left-wing ideology to return their parents’ allegedly unconditional love. In September, the Wall Street Journal called it an “epidemic” and quoted supposed experts who claim children suffer from “self-delusion,” “diminished skill for tough conversations” and ““No one is reckoning with the question of what is happening in a lot of families that makes kids feel like they would be better off going low- or no-contact,” explained Joshua Stein, a political researcher who has spent years tracking parental estrangement forums. Instead, there’s an “online ecosystem of estrangement experts,” who often work through right-wing media, “selling services and stories appeal to that audience by first assuring them that it’s not their fault.”“This is the same underlying politics of grievance at the heart of the American right,” he told me, noting that the Acton situation, while an extreme example, is not unusual. “Donna Arthur is a symptom of the moral psychology of right-wing reactionary politics,” Stein said, noting that for the “reactionary right,” the concept of respect “is one-directional.”“Donna Arthur is a symptom of the moral psychology of right-wing reactionary politics,” Stein said, noting that for the “reactionary right,” the concept of respect “is one-directional.” In this view, “authority figures are entitled to respect, regardless of conduct,” and that “respect includes deferring to the authority,” which all too often results in making excuses for child abuse. While none of the estranged adult children who spoke to Salon in 2024 had endured sexual violence, many described how right-wing politics were deeply intertwined with parents being controlling, cruel and abusive. Some spoke of being severely beaten. Others had parents who wanted to dictate their romantic lives. One woman was pushed into a bad marriage at an early age. Another man described how his parents ran off girlfriends for being the “wrong” race or religion. A woman reported being denied medical care for religious reasons. Another woman, who is biracial, said her white mother made racist comments to her. In online forums for estranged parents, which tend to lean conservative, Stein found that children’s stories of mistreatment were regularly dismissed. “The driving narrative of children exaggerating trauma is central to reactionary politics of estrangement,” he explained, noting that Ramaswamy’s ad featuring Acton’s mother is “a manifestation” of this “reasoning under its worst conditions.” Ramaswamy, Trump, Vance and their advisers are all notorious for being constantly online, and they are almost certainly aware that the topic of parental estrangement is a driving concern with many MAGA voters, some of whom have experienced estrangement or distancing from their own children, family members or friends, and are outraged at the thought of facing social consequences for their reactionary views. Much of the online response in right-wing spaces suggests this read on the GOP base is accurate enough. On social media, plenty of GOP voters have defended Arthur and denounced Acton. Many of them appear to be elderly.“Because of the estrangement factor,” one Daily Wire commenter wrote, “I believe the mom.” Many concurred.“So telling the truth is a horrible thing. Mothers know their kids better than anybody,” one person posted on Facebook in response to a local news post about the ad. “NOT all daughters are good daughters EITHER,” agreed one. “Our mothers know us best!!” added another. To be clear, these attitudes are not the norm among Americans generally, and pollsters haven’t had a chance to gauge if Ramaswamy’s ad has boomeranged. But if the goal is to energize Republican voters who may feel demoralized this cycle, the strategy makes more sense. There’s a widespread sense of grievance on the right over feeling rejected for their political views, which manifests in everything from Republicans complaining that liberals won’t date them to a woman at a rally for Byron Donalds, Florida’s GOP nominee for governor, demanding that the law force her “petty” daughter to stay in contact.The Donna Arthur ad was designed to stoke that very sense of entitlement and persuade conservatives to use their vote to punish liberal family members and neighbors for shunning them. It may not be enough to overcome the disgust that Ramaswamy stirred up in voters who have a healthier attitude about family and boundaries. Still, from the party that gave us “Haitians eat pets” and “LGBTQ kids poop in litter boxes,” there really is no move too morally depraved, if they think they can get votes with it.

item.title: Oh No, I Can’t Stop Watching People Play ‘GTA VI’
item.author: Brandy Jensen
item.content:encoded: I did not imagine that the release of would have any meaningful impact on my life, for the simple reason that I am not a gamer. I know and even respect a few people for whom video games are important, but I mainly regard this in the same way I do friends who really like square dancing, or go to church: nice for them, but not really my business.While I have, in the past, dated gamers and even come to occasionally enjoy watching them play video games, that was mainly because I'm bossy and liked telling them , or Open that box, I bet there's something inside. Backseat driving a video game can be fun, but only insofar as I can manipulate what's happening. The appeal of Twitch, where you are simply one of dozens or hundreds of spectators watching someone else play a game, has always been totally, utterly alien to me. This would be true even without the dangers of encountering slurs in a chat or being confronted by the ever-present sight of anything that could be reasonably called "a gaming rig." No thank you.And yet, I have found my conviction wavering recently as I find myself strangely compelled to click on clip after clip of people playing . It started innocently enough, as people kept insisting that this game was teaching men to be thoughtful partners. I watched clips of people doing things Lucia will appreciate: buying groceries, taking her shopping, picking up flowers. I watched a guy make thoughtful decisions about how she might like to wear her hair. Soon I'd moved on to following along as people make Jason lovingly turn their house into a home, or invite Lucia to take the driver's seat on an aquatic adventure.

item.title: Tell Congress to protect funding for those unhoused.
item.author: SRS0=zgbh=JL=mail135.sea51.mcsv.net=bounce-mc.us19_228507186.17295082-8782042e9f@eforward.registrar-servers.com
item.content:encoded: Late Thursday night, the Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, by a vote of 62-33 (Native News Online). The bill would speed up federal permits for data centers, pipelines, wind and solar farms, and mines (Utah Public Radio). More than 70 Tribal Nations came out against it, because its third section would weaken the law that gives them agency when a project threatens their sacred places (NCAI). The legislation passed in the Senate on Thursday, and will be considered by the House when it returns from Thanksgiving recess (Native News Online).The law at stake is Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, passed in 1966. It requires federal agencies to consider how their projects affect historic places, and to invite tribes into the process when those places carry religious and cultural meaning for them (ACHP). To be clear, it's a modest protection. The final decision still rests with the federal agency, not the tribe (ACHP). But it's often the only seat tribes get at the table, especially since many sacred sites sit outside reservation boundaries (Native News Online).The bill would narrow which projects need that review in the first place, decrease touch points for tribal input, and make it harder for tribes to get a court to pause a project before the damage is done (NARF). "This is such an existential threat to Indian Country," National Congress of American Indians President Mark Macarro said at a press conference earlier this month (Native News Online). The bill was introduced in September with no public hearings and no tribal consultation (Native News Online).The legislation also deems natural features like mountains, bodies of water and landscapes ineligible as historic property (Turtle Talk). For many tribes, those are the types of places that are sacred. Beyond that, it expands the scope of the federal government to misuse these natural resources, potentially covering even more resources from the communities that need them most.Native people have fought for generations for the right to pray on their own land. Congress passed the American Indian Religious Freedom Act in 1978, after finding that federal and state laws often disrupted Native religious practices (The Conversation). But ten years later, the Supreme Court ruled that the Forest Service could build a road through the Chimney Rock area of Northern California, land sacred to the Yurok, Karuk and Tolowa peoples (Oyez). The Court called the harm to their religion "incidental" and treated the 1978 law as a policy without real legal protection (Oyez, The Conversation). In his dissent, Justice William Brennan wrote that "Native American faith is inextricably bound to the use of land" (The Conversation).Oak Flat, or Chi'chil Biłdagoteel, in Arizona, is used for religious and coming-of-age ceremonies by The San Carlos Apache and other tribes. The land was protected from mining by a 1955 order from President Eisenhower (Cronkite News). In 2014, the late Sen. John McCain slipped a provision into a defense bill to trade 2,422 acres of it to Resolution Copper (Cronkite News). The Supreme Court declined to hear Apache Stronghold's appeal last year, and the Forest Service handed over the land on March 16 (Cronkite News). The mine would leave a crater more than 1,000 feet deep and up to two miles across (Cronkite). Legislation like BAAJA will make it even harder for tribes to be heard and respected in these decisions.This week, many of us will sit down for a holiday that misconstrues how colonizers disrespected Native communities and their land. That practice — of expulsion and displacement, of extraction and suppression — is still happening today. Use this week to help write a new story, and support contemporary Native issues with the gratitude and reverence they deserve.

item.title: Preznit Fuckwit has really shitty taste in friends
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Friends. They can be a mixed bag. We’ve all been there, right? I mean, who among us doesn’t have that one bud who can be a little bit — oh, shall we say, ?Or maybe you’ll be shooting the shit, when all of a sudden he starts a war of choice against Ukraine, one that’s now been dragging on for five years, with no end in sight.Sure, these kinds of pals can be a handful — some days you just want to go ‘’ — but we keep giving them mulligans, because they’re such irrepressible funsters.There we all were, once again unwilling participants in the shittiest timeline ever, simply hoping against hope that maybe — — we could go an entire Saturday without having to bear eternal witness to Preznit Fuckwit humiliating himself, and embarrassing our entire country.No such luck. It’s so exhausting to have to reset this counter every single goddamned day of our lives.This is so childish. So needy. Imagine having to work this hard to convince the world that not hates your guts.You know what? It occurs to me that Donny has . Donny really needs some new buddies — ones who aren’t pedophiles, or war-criming psychopath bastards. Can’t anyone help hook Donny up? What about the diaper nurse? Doesn’t she know anyone who’d be a good hang for him? Nah, the bunny boiler wants Dear Leader all to her own. She’s not the sharing type. Look at them, yesterday — golfing together, on the taxpayer dime.Trump departing the White House this morning for another round of golf. Natalie Harp, in spandex, is tagging along.When they weren’t canoodling on the 13th green, Donny and Natty were very busy on their crappy app, farting out dozens of posts in the span of an hour or so — most of them variations on the same theme: .For heaven’s sake, Stalin, Churchill and Roosevelt met in Yalta so they could fight Hitler and the Nazis. Do you think Donny even knows that? I doubt it. All his putrefying pudding-brain can dredge up is ‘famous photo, me want some too.’Pro tip for Donny: actual leaders don’t have to work this hard to convince the world that they’re leaders. Their accomplishments are all the convincing anyone needs.But Donny doesn’t have an actual accomplishments to show off. Accomplishments require hard work, and Donny’s too fucking lazy for any of that shit. Getting your photo taken with your despot besties is its own reward.Donny’s a cheap grifter and carnival barker. Life to him is just a series of photo ops, so he can be the center of attention, and give the of having gotten shit done. But nobody but the brain-deadest of his cultists are fooled. Of course we all know the truth. Putin and Xi aren’t Donny’s friends — and they never will be. They’re taking advantage of a demented old moron, sweet-talking him and then robbing him blind. Donny’s a mark. He’s getting his pockets picked by two old pros working in cahoots, and he’s too fucking dumb to realize it.Here’s the other fucked-up thing that happened yesterday, and this one has the diabolical undead hand of Acting President Nosferatu McGoebbels all over it. Donny just ain’t Machiavellian enough to come up with this shit. President Trump has issued an executive order ordering federal contractors to inform the White House about any congressional requests for information about their work with the government, and withhold any information the government considers confidential.Basically, this is how Nosferatu imagines he’ll do an end-run around Democrats looking into malfeasance and corruption — by having Donny sign this patently illegal executive order. The idea being that when next year’s Democratic-led House Oversight Committee asks Donny’s cronies to account for the money spent clownfucking the vulgar Epstein Dance Hall, the cronies will go ‘nuh-uh, we don’t have to tell you. It’s executive privilege.’ Oh, you want to know how the Epstein Reflecting Pool turned into such an over-budget debacle? Fuck you, that shit’s a state secret.Never mind that executive orders don’t cover contractors. Never mind that it’s Congress’ Constitutionally-mandated to investigate how taxpayer dollars are spent. Nosferatu’s scheme is to tie it all up in courts, for the foreseeable forever. Come on, do you fuckers really have to pull this shit on a ? Can’t we ever have some peace and quiet around here?Wouldn’t it be great if it stayed that way? ‘Wouldn’t it be amazing if he went twenty-four whole hours without being a thermonuclear fuckwad? Imagine if my post for tomorrow were simply ‘nothing happened, here’s some Daily Claudia.’That would fucking rule, wouldn’t it?Don’t get your hopes up. That ain’t how shitty timelines roll.And speaking of our Daily Claudia, let’s have some.Please don’t ask me to explain why Ms Spouse has that garland on her head, because I don’t remember. Just know that it was relevant to whatever event was going on down at our lake on September 12, 2020 — and that Ms Spouse very patiently perched it on her head after a child wandered up and handed it to her.I think she looks cute as fuck, don’t you?Have a great Sunday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Thank you for supporting the League!
item.author: SRS0=h6rD=JL=enbounce.lwv.org=ma_us-bounces@eforward.registrar-servers.com
item.content:encoded: We are a century-strong grassroots movement working to empower voters and defend democracy. Originally referred to as a “mighty political experiment,” the League has paved the way for women’s suffrage, launched an ongoing fight for equal rights — and changed our democracy forever.We’re the League of Women Voters. And we’re so glad to have you with us. We’re grateful for your involvement in our mission to ensure every voter has the tools and opportunity to make their voice heard. Your support ensures that every eligible voter has free and fair access to the ballot box, that voters pick our leaders instead of the other way around, and that the people hold our elected officials accountable.The work of the League of Women Voters does not stop between elections. League members are on the ground 365 days a year, working to register, educate, mobilize, and protect voters so we can build a more inclusive, representative democracy. Today, you’re embracing the League's mission at an especially critical time. Attacks on voting rights have been coming to us from all directions. And we are fighting back. The League is defending democracy at every level of government: federal, state, and local. With Leagues in every Congressional jurisdiction, we have the widespread reach and people power to create change on a national level. And we're proud to be a source of trusted, nonpartisan election information for millions of voters. Together, we are protecting voters and building civic power in every corner of the country — including yours.Thank you again for your commitment to empowering voters and defending our democracy — ensuring our electorate reflects the wonderfully diverse communities across our country. We’re glad you’re with us!

item.title: Muru
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since.Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production.As he did with wrapture, he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process.Here's everything he's published so far, all in the last three weeks:The AI may be doing a lot of the work on the surface, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still down to me, and twenty years of getting things wrong with mod_wsgi turns out to be useful for that. I am prepared to put in the hard work to keep polishing Muru until it is something I would trust, and something you would too.

item.title: The 'best Mexican restaurant in the world' is in SF. It only cost me $500.
item.content:encoded: There is exactly one three-starred Michelin-rated Mexican restaurant in the world, and somewhat rudely, it’s not in Mexico. It’s Californios, a $450 prix fixe gastronomic temple tucked away on 11th Street in the SoMa neighborhood of San Francisco. You already know this kind of restaurant simply from the price point (which rose $50 since my visit, from $325 to $375 before tax/tip/drinks), and from the fact that it got the notice of the fabled Michelin judges this year, who went so far as to declare it the best Mexican restaurant in the world. Is this the kind of place custom made for its patrons to boast about having dined there? Of course. Does the 12-course tasting menu include fantasy novel ingredients such as “chickweed”? You bet it does. Do certain dishes come with tweezers? Bitch, you KNOW there are gonna be some tweezers coming your way. As long as epicureanism exists, there will always be establishments like this one: ones that are equal parts thrilling, exhausting and ultra-expensive.But, knowing what you and I know about the post-COVID world, about the darker side of Michelin-starred kitchens, and about America’s ever-worsening income gap, is the kind of restaurant that dollops caviar onto multiple courses still ? That’s where I come in. Because tonight, I’ll be dining at Californios for the very first time …Article continues below this adI’m not lying when I tell you this restaurant is tucked away. As with so many restaurants of its caliber, Californios, open since 2015, hangs no shingle by its entrance. You have to know it’s there to it’s there, and even then, you can still miss it. I know because I just walked right by Californios’ front door without realizing it, then had to double back as I stared at the pin on Google Maps, then double back again when I walked right by it a second time. This is fine dining as speakeasy: No walk-ins allowed, and the only way in is by securing a reservation months in advance. Again, you and I know this kind of place.Then I saunter through the main entrance and am instantly transported. I’m standing inside a stone courtyard dotted with luxe wicker patio furniture and potted palm trees. Every muscle in my body slackens. A few steps farther, and now I’m inside a flawlessly lit dining room with walls painted a deep, rich blue and adorned with vibrant paintings that I’d probably pay a separate entrance fee just to stare at. I wish I lived here.Article continues below this adThe host escorts me to my table, and I feel a touch sad to be dining alone. This is the kind of place you take her after she’s said yes, you know what I mean? Californios offers romantic ambience in endless abundance. Now I miss my wife. I better stuff myself with 900 pounds of quail mole and black cod tacos to help dull the heartache.Then I get the menu, and it looks exactly like a wedding program. There’s even a tasteful photograph of a flower affixed to the cover. I half expect to open it and see that my meal will begin with a procession to Vivaldi, followed by a reading from Corinthians. There’s also an autographed welcome card on the table addressed to a “Brodie,” which is not my name but the name of the person who booked my reservation. My server apologizes and promises to get me a new envelope with my actual name on it. I tell them it’s OK. On this night, I’d rather be Brodie. Makes me feel stealthy.That’s enough prelude. Let’s get to the good stuff, shall we? My evening begins with a flight of aguas frescas: strawberry hibiscus soda, canary melon horchata, and guava/kiwi soda. I also order a separate, a la carte mocktail: a coca noza, Mexican Coke with cherry. All of it is delicious. I love fancy sodas. My appetite has now been sufficiently whetted. I could eat a whole bull right now.Article continues below this adI’ll have to settle for a series of arty small plates instead. As with many other high-end omakase restaurants, dinner at Californios is an overextended affair in which you, the diner, must endure an hourslong procession of courses, each of which includes a little guest lecture from your server before you feel allowed to partake. That waiting can prove a bit torturous, but the tease is part of the burlesque. So I can’t help but groan with pleasure when I finally get to take my first bite: an Anasazi bean sope, or beancake, topped with caviar. I’m a sucker for caviar, and pairing it with this cake, which has been stuffed with a gigante bean mousse, is exactly the stroke of genius I’d expect from chef-owner Val Cantu, who’s originally from Texas and mastered the craft of Mexican cooking during a stint working at Mexico City’s Pujol. I hear another diner say, “This tastes like a memory,” which was surely Cantu’s goal. In this mission, he is fabulously successful. This is food that makes you think, and that makes you to think.But all that thinking tends to make one hungry. Here comes more modestly sized appetizers — a bluefin tuna tostada that’s been topped with serrano coins and finishes hot on the palate. It’s a slow burn that I hope lingers a good long while. Then comes a single Dungeness crab flauta. I’m a sucker for flautas, too. This is Mexican food all right: instantly recognizable and yet new all at the same time. I want more.Article continues below this adI get it. While sucking down the rest of my coca noza, I’m greeted with a disc of lobster ceviche sitting in a pool of “spicy water,” the latter of which is far tastier than its name implies. The server tells me that I’m free to slurp this aguachile, and I happily take him up on the entreaty. Now here’s abalone on the shell, which I take down in seconds. Every bite here only makes me hungry for more. I suspect that, even after all of these bravura small bites, the Californios kitchen is holding back on the big flavors for the later courses. My patience, admittedly, is wearing a touch thin. The quail mole and rib-eye tacos are still many courses away, and I’m wanting to go to there.When on my table what should appear but a grilled banana flan topped with serrano ham, date jus, translucently thin plantain chips and, natch, more caviar. I have never tasted anything like this, and likely never will again. In the pre-COVID times, experiential dining like this was revered to the point of absurdity. It feels a bit more crass to enjoy it in a broken 2026 America. But man, eat that flan and tell me if it’s a moral abdication or not. I’m sorry that not everyone gets to try this, but I’m not sorry that get to.After I lay waste to that savory flan, my server tells me, “Now we’re moving on to tacos.” F—k yeah, we are.Article continues below this adAnother showstopper follows: a single fish taco. But this is no ordinary fish taco. Cantu and his staff have battered a rectangle of black cod (aka sable, aka butterfish), placed it atop a sourdough tortilla, and then topped the fish with a corn smut crema and multi-pepper salsa. Frying black cod is a very evil and awesome thing to do. This is the best fish taco I’ve ever eaten, in part because of the aforementioned cod,but also thanks to the sourdough tortilla. I hope sourdough tortillas make it off the runway and down into the retail dining sector sooner rather than later.It has taken literal hours for me to get through these opening acts, and my back is a touch sore. I get back up to enjoy the courtyard, plus a bathroom that features a toilet with a seat that opens and closes automatically. Makes me feel like a heavy hitter.Article continues below this ad the kitchen brings out the big guns. First up is the aforementioned quail mole, which is presented so artfully that I want to hang it on the dining room wall: a diamond-shaped piece of quail breast covered in a mole that surely contains 936 separate ingredients and required 47 hours to make. The mole coats the breast entirely, leaving only a clean matte finish that reflects the light fixtures hanging overhead. To one side of that plate is the leg quarter of that same quail smoked, its lower portion wrapped in twine for easy gripping. To the other side, a bowl of fresh tortillas (not sourdough) crusted in sesame seeds. At certain points during this meal, I kept expecting a burrito to arrive, because I am long conditioned for a specific kind of Mexican food, which, to be clear, kicks major ass. At other points, I’ve wondered if I’d be left so hungry by all these small plates that I would have to go purchase said burrito at another restaurant after dinner was over. The mole makes all of those cravings and worries disappear. I am being both blown away and sated all in one go.Ah, but we’re not done yet. Because after the mole comes a final taco, this one stuffed with ribbons of sliced rib-eye that are so tender, they never catch on my teeth. Even better, the kitchen has paired this steak taco with a glass of beet juice (as part of the N/A drink pairings I ordered to go with my tasting menu, at a supplemental cost of $95, now $125) that’s so deep in color and texture that it behaves like red wine. As someone who no longer drinks alcohol and has found all dealcoholized red wines to be rotgut, I’m downright grateful for this glass of beet juice to go with my final taco. I don’t even normally like beets, man. Then again, I am not me tonight. I am Brodie. Brodie will f—k up some beet juice.Now for dessert. Do they crumb your table before serving you dessert here? You needn’t ask. The main dessert is a chocolate alegría — a kind of traditional Mexican candy — topped with strawberries, lightly toasted amaranth and solidified honey bits. Its satellite desserts include a blueberry empanada and a scoop of almond ice cream, which, when eaten in tandem, is the kind of dessert I would like to eat every night until I’m dead. They spoil you with desserts at Californios, right down to the candied mandarin segments that come with my check. It’s late now, far too late, but I, the mysterious Brodie, will be heading back to my hotel room more than satisfied.Article continues below this adIf not conflicted. Again, this is an extremely pricey restaurant. An one. So while I had myself a grand ol’ time at Californios, even without a proper date sitting across from me, I’m still left to wonder if this sort of restaurant can exist in the 21st century, and if it even should. Does the world still need restaurants where the starting price is about the same as a fancy hotel room, where every course comes with its own special set of utensils, and where any question you ask about your food will get you a crisp paragraph in reply? Isn’t this all a bit ostentatious? Do we really want a place like this to still have cultural purchase?After thinking about it, my answer remains an unequivocal yes. Yes, sitting for an hourslong dinner is kind of an ordeal, and the money spent by customers here would be better spent on helping the destitute, and maybe not every restaurant should have a menu that literally includes pages’ worth of end credits. Would I have preferred to eat all of Californios’ dishes from an a la carte menu, over successive (and much more brief) visits? Of course. But then Cantu’s restaurant might not have gotten quite as much notice from Michelin, which still represents the vanguard of the fine dining establishment. It may not have been recognized as three-star runway food. Article continues below this adAnd runway food, of the highest Michelin rating, still needs to exist for the same reason that all high art needs to exist. The world, no matter what condition it’s in, will always need people who feverishly labor to give others something they’ve never experienced before; people who act as credible tastemakers in the greater culture for the coming years, if not decades. That’s especially true in the case of Californios, because it has given Mexican food long-overdue representation in the highest stratosphere of culinary gatekeeping. It’s the first three-star Mexican restaurant in the world, but it will not be the last.

item.title: This Week in Stupid: November 21 edition
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: As another stupid week comes to a close here in America, let’s look back at the dumbest fucking shit that happened.Monday: exposing imaginary election fraud, for fun and zero profitHey, has anyone seen the chopped foam pillow salesman lately? It’s been a while. Should we be sending someone to do a wellness check?“They were so blatant in what they just did in these midterms. Take all of Texas, all of Kansas, all hundred and five counties. All of Iowa. All across our country. They went overboard. Evil is greedy. And this is where we are gonna win. As you know, the president declassified information that the government was holding from us, about foreign interference in our elections. We need your help.”Yes, I know. Choppy McPillowface’s elevator no longer goes to the top floor. It hasn’t for a good long while. The deranged Christmas elf inside his head has been leaning on again.But let’s set that aside for a moment, because there’s something I really want to know:Where in the hallowed name of Cut-Rate Lodging Jesus is Mike Lindell broadcasting from? Look at his surroundings. Some shitty floor lamp. A nondescript chair, next to a simple table and a bed. The worst drapes ever. Holy fuck, Mike’s been reduced to staying in cheap motels, hasn’t he?Didn’t this jamoke used to be some kind of millionaire CEO? Why is he now holed up in Four Seasons Total Motelling, across the street from the topless joint with the all-you-can-eat buffet, on the outskirts of town?Bro, it’s time to pick a better grift. Begging MAGA for their spare change so you can prove imaginary election fraud ain’t floating the boat.Here’s Rachel Campos-Duffy, spouse of the Secretary In Charge Of Making Sure Planes Don’t Fucking Fall Out Of The Sky, with some super-reassuring news. “If anything happens, we all go up to Wisconsin, where we have fresh water, we have guns and lots of ammo.”Wait a second, the Duffys are ?Excuse me, but that’s not how it’s supposed to work. When shit goes sideways, the moron whose incompetence that shit go sideways isn’t supposed to have a place to hide from all the sideways shit. He’s supposed to stay at his desk, straightening that shit out.These nitwits are stockpiling guns and ammo out in the middle of nowhere? Great, what could go wrong?Oh, by the way, here’s some footage of Sean Duffy, up there in Wisconsin, doing his doomsday prepping.I swear, these MAGA shitwits have no shame. I can’t wait for Duff’s final press conference — the one where he goes ‘sorry we broke everything. Sucks to be you,’ as he closes the hatch to his shelter.Thanks for nothing, asshole.Wednesday: just another mystery from the dawn of time“When is the last time you saw a conservative riot? Conservatives really don’t know how to riot. We lack the blueprint for it.”Hmm. I’m trying to jog my memory about the last time conservatives rioted. It’s right there on the tip of my tongue. Maybedudes know. Hey guys, can I ask you a question? When was the last time conservatives rioted? Have they ever? Guys? Ah, they seem too preoccupied by whatever hijinks they’re doing to reply. Oh well.Hey, can we get Josh Hawley in here? Maybe he knows the answer. Apparently no, we can’t get Josh in here. He seems to be in a real hurry to get somewhere. What about Markwayne Mullin? Hey, Mark? It looks like Marky Two-names is too busy looking for whatever he dropped to answer. I wonder why he looks so terrified. Huh.Oh well, I guess we’ll never find out if conservatives have ever rioted. It’s just going to be one of those unsolved mysteries for the ages.Thursday: just fuck off, Florida GOP Rep Randy Fine: “Look, if Americans want to elect a former bartender as their president, then that’s up to them, but I think we need people who have had to be successful in the real world, who have gone out and done things and understand how you start, build, and grow a family. How you start, build and grow a business.”Fuck straight off into the sea, Randy — if that even is your real name.Folks, get ready to hear this every goddamned day for the next two years. ‘AOC was a bartenders. Girl bartenders can’t be president. They don’t know how to run a business.’After her father’s death, AOC tended bar to help prevent foreclosure on her parent’s house. Bartenders encounter a wide variety of people with a wide variety of perspectives. AOC earned a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree, double-majoring in international relations and economics. So why is Fine sneering at AOC?.Oh, and speaking of some fucking idiot—Friday: the further adventures of Some Fucking Idiot™On Friday, instead of hiding in shame after his traitorous escapade in China, some fucking idiot actually had the temerity to take a victory lap. Flanked by his Emotional Support Flunkies, Couchfuck McGee and Liddle Marco Big-Shoes, the fucking idiot actually bragged about not giving a shit about America.COLLINS: You said Putin is your friend. Russia is Iran’s biggest ally. Do you believe Putin is a friend to America? TRUMP: I can't speak to AmericaThe fucking idiot can’t speak to America? Does the fucking idiot remember which country he’s supposed to be president of? Oh my god, the fucking idiot wants a cookie. He thinks he deserves a cookie, after shitting the bed and then rolling around in the mess. Fuck off, you don’t get a cookie.as Marco Rubio squirms behind him, Trump whines about not getting a Nobel PrizeTrump: “Before I was here, I had a plane — I had a very nice life — and my pilot would use the air traffic control from a totally different country ... I don’t want to say the country.”What the fuck? That’s not how air traffic control works. There’s no concierge service where you get to pick and choose which one you want. The pilots communicate with the tower that’s closest to their plane at any given moment. Does the fucking idiot even know what planet he’s on right now?Trump says not to worry about all the tech outages lately because he has a very good understanding of what’s going on with the technology because of his uncle and it probably passed on to him genetically, too.Now, could the diaper nurse please take the fucking idiot to the dentist and get his dentures adjusted? Because the fucking idiot kept making gross slurping noises the entire time. Listen to this.Yeah, the fucking idiot slurped his way through the entire presser. Ew.And, of course, it wouldn’t be a White House press conference if the fucking idiot wasm’t rude to some reporter.TRUMP: Come on. Who are you with? REPORTER: I’m with NBC, sir TRUMP: You're really a rude person. I’m not talking to you. You shouldn’t be in the front row. You should be in the back row.And, as always, even though the fucking idiot had just treated them like shit, right to their faces, not one reporter stood up to ask, ‘what the fuck is wrong with you?’How fucking idiotic is that?And now, let’s put a close to This Week in Stupid and reward ourselves with some Daily Claudia.Here’s Katie and her mom, in some undated photos that were taken at our old house in Hastings. Katie looks, what, 7 or 8 years old? That would make these photos from 1998 or 1999.Oh my god, Have a non-stupid Saturday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future:practice self-care. do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: A hospital slashed costs. Then a patient froze to death on its roof.
item.author: bounce-mc.us1_388705.10709053-d186966748@mail194.suw241.rsgsv.net
item.content:encoded: When a new healthcare company took over a struggling hospital in Waukegan, Illinois, residents hoped it would finally revitalize the facility. Vista Medical Center East had already been bought and sold four times—but maybe this time would be different. The new owner was American Healthcare Systems, a for-profit company pitching itself as a turnaround specialist for distressed hospitals. Rick Harris, a local pastor and businessman on the hospital’s board, had never heard of it. And his research turned up a troubling example of its work: A year before, AHS took over a struggling hospital in St. Louis. When financial troubles there got worse instead of better, AHS closed it in less than a year. “I’m just thinking to myself, if I’ve got good intentions, if I can’t pay for this hospital, if I owe all of this money…then where am I getting the money to buy Vista?” he said. Soon, AHS was stiffing vendors, not paying doctors, and leaving millions in taxes unpaid. It asked the state of Illinois for money and got $30 million in loans. AHS promised this money would allow it to pay staff and keep Vista running smoothly. But what happened instead would shine a spotlight on the hospital, AHS, and the for-profit playbook in American healthcare. A 28-year-old woman who came to the ER was found on the roof of the hospital in a gown and socks, frozen to death. , in an investigation produced in collaboration with the McGraw Center for Business Journalism at CUNY's Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism, we find out how her death happened and the financial chaos that laid the groundwork.

item.author: SRS0=MMio=JK=bh1234.vbnewsletters.votebeat.org=bounces+misc=muneer.top@eforward.registrar-servers.com
item.content:encoded: Prather: One of the things that our survey reveals is what happens in between these elections. What you can see is a decline over time. So, much of the loss in trust among Republicans happened in the intervening years, not as a result of the election itself. So if you just looked at where Republican trust was post-2024 and then looked at it post-2026, you'd see this huge, massive decline. Most of that decline happened across January and then January to September, and really we only see a 6-percentage-point decline in trust from September to November. So that suggests to us there's something going on that's different.

item.title: Scientists Discover New and Horrible Eagle-Based Way Our Ancestors Died
item.author: Becky Ferreira
item.content:encoded: Welcome back to the Abstract! Here are the studies this week that dive-bombed our ancestors, brightened the sky, recalled an old tune, and got hosed by marine mucus.First, scientists discover that eagles are hunting large baboons, hinting that early human relatives once sated ancient avian appetites. Then: star-on-star contact, a musical memory lane, and the secrets of cetacean snot. Eagle-eyeing you…for dinner!Death came from the sky for early humans, according to a new study that suggests giant eagles preyed on our ancestors far more recently than was previously known. Birds of prey (raptors) have hunted primates for at least 20 million years, including early human relatives, known as hominins. For example, a hominin toddler known as the “Taung child” shows signs of being killed by a raptor roughly 2.5 million years ago. But scientists have assumed that hominins outgrew their status as bird bites since that time, and there are no reports of raptors preying on primates that weigh over 28 pounds on record—until now. In 2025, scientists discovered that Verreaux’s eagles—one of the largest eagle species in the world—at Ennedi Plateau in Chad are likely hunting adult olive baboons weighing up to 57 pounds. The team found baboon remains among the region’s sandstone cliffs that show signature marks of eagle predation, such as talon punctures on the skull and scrapes to the shoulder bones.“We cannot definitively rule out scavenging activity, but the severity of punctures is suggestive of lethal interactions through a killing grip,” said researchers led by Catherine Hobaiter of the University of St. Andrews. The team also observed the baboons rapidly retreat when eagles approached, suggesting that they feared aerial attacks.Some researchers have argued against the “raptor-mediated predation” of the Taung child on the grounds that the hominin would have been too heavy for a bird. The study’s authors get extra points for including a quote from the comedy Monty Python and the Holy Grail on this point: “It is a simple question of weight ratios. A five-ounce bird could not carry a 1-pound coconut.” IYKYK. However, the laughs stop there, as the team refutes this idea by recounting the grisly “low flight with sustained grip attack” that eagles perform on ungulates, such as antelopes or cattle, which reveal that raptors can kill animals that are many times their own weight with the right approach. “Briefly, an eagle will land on the back or neck of a moderately large ungulate, gripping it firmly with its talons. If the prey withstands knocking to the ground, the eagle will ride it with wings outstretched and flapping to maintain balance until the quarry collapses, either from exhaustion, shock, or internal injury. A similar tactic is described in the of a Harpy eagle ( attacking a 52-kg adult woman.”Wow, new fear unlocked! Imagine being an early hominin, minding your own business banging rocks together or something, when suddenly a giant bird of prey either pushes you off a cliff or rides you to death. For everyone preparing to eat a huge bird for Thanksgiving next week, be grateful that it’s no longer the other way around.Speaking of unwieldy meals, scientists have captured an unprecedented glimpse of a star eating another star, thereby forming a new mega-star. Over the past few years, scientists noticed that something weird has been unfolding in a binary star system called AT 2025abao—nicknamed “Bao” (yum!)—in the outskirts of the Andromeda galaxy, which is about 2.5 million light years away from the Milky Way. One of the stars, “Big Bao,” was expanding into its dying red giant phase, which pulled its companion, “Little Bao,” into a deadly spiral. Last year, the system rapidly brightened, signaling that Big Bao had swallowed Little Bao.“In October 2025, the star underwent a dramatic eruption” and exhibited “a sudden increase in its photospheric temperature to about 8,000 K,” said researchers led by Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University. The system “shows the defining hallmarks of luminous red novae,a class of transients established to arise from impulsive energy injection…during the merger of a star with its companion.”“This inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly,” the team noted. Congratulations to the newly-fed couple! Long may Bao shine.Girl, put your records on / but don’t think you own that songWe’ve all had that feeling of hearing a familiar song and being transported to a specific time and place in our lives. But as it turns out, the recollections stirred by those cherished songs are probably not all that special, according to a new study that surveyed 233 undergraduate students about these so-called “music-evoked autobiographical memories.”The students (aged 18-23) listened to clips of grouped into two categories: “new” songs released from 2014 to 2019, during their adolescence, and “old” songs released from 1985 to 1995, before they were born. When asked to reminisce about the songs, students with similar backgrounds were remarkably aligned in their answers.“Memories evoked by country songs were more strongly associated with very recent time periods (college) and themes relating to family, driving, summertime, romantic partners, and listening to music (particularly music selected by someone else),” said researchers led by Cara Turnbull of Texas Tech University. “Alternatively, memories evoked by hip-hop songs were most often associated with friends, acquaintances (such as classmates, coworkers, and teammates), dancing, and being at school, while those evoked by pop songs were most associated with middle school, listening at home or by oneself, and singing along,” the team added. As an elder millennial, it was humbling to realize what counts as an “oldie” these days. I also felt my generation’s soundtrack was done dirty by offerings like “Achy Breaky Heart” by Billy Ray Cyrus or “Whoomp! There it is” by Tag Team. No Stevie Nicks? Madonna? Wu Tang? All I ask of future generations is that you do not judge us solely by the croonings of C+C Music Factory and Bryan Adams, I beg you. Join hands, dear friends, for we are about to run directly through majestic fountains of whale snot. Scientists who flew drones through whale “blow”—the mucus-filled vapor exhaled by whales through their blowholes—have successfully sequenced whole genomes from the snotty samples, representing “a major step towards non-invasive cetacean sampling,” according to a new study.“Preserving biodiversity requires the genetic monitoring of wild populations, which is traditionally done through invasive sampling techniques for DNA collection,” said researchers led by Éadin O’Mahony of the University of St. Andrews. “However, this approach can impact animal welfare or be impossible to implement due to behavioural responses to anthropogenic factors or national/international legislation.” Indeed, I think that we can all agree that humans have stressed whales out enough as it is. Instead of invasive biopsies of skin and flesh with darts or scrapers, O’Mahony and his colleagues equipped drones with petri dishes and flew them through a total of 58 blows from 26 Northeast Pacific humpback whales in the Gitga'at First Nation territory of northern British Columbia. The team “established that a whole humpback whale genome can be recovered from exhaled respiratory vapour (‘blow’), marking a significant methodological advancement in non-invasive cetacean genomics.”While it’s not the kind of blow most people associate with breathing orifices, it just might be what we need to study whales without hassling them.Thanks for reading! See you next week. Corrected: A previous version of this story erroneously used "miles" in place of "light years."

item.title: We built our own platform for this moment
item.author: 1axbtwoq239im3vds5bhycqyj7inh0vraysn9v@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: Shortly after the election, I came to you with a bold prediction: once all the ballots were counted and the results certified, Democrats would hold 56 Senate seats. I can now report that my prediction came true.Throughout the post-election period, I have worn two hats. I am the chairman of Elias Law Group, the law firm that helped secure the final victories. I am also the founder of Democracy Docket, an outlet that had reporters on the ground.During that time, Democracy Docket provided you with in-depth reporting, analysis and commentary on what was happening and what to expect next. There was no hedging, no false equivalence and no both-sides journalism.When Mississippi’s secretary of state tried to blame third-party vendors for high rates of ballots flagged for further review, rather than counted outright, Democracy Docket covered it. When the Department of Justice threatened, and then abandoned, a legal effort to block Alaska’s certification, Democracy Docket cut through the spin and told you what was really at stake.Throughout it all, I offered my analysis in writing and on video podcasts. Thanks to support from its premium members, Democracy Docket dropped its paywall from Election Day until the Alaska race was called.During that period, one of the most visited parts of the Democracy Docket website was its live blog, which kept you updated on the remaining races to be called. It featured a mix of short and long written pieces, along with video reports from the states.Democracy Docket could provide this feature for free because it built its own technology platform. That may seem minor, but think about what it meant in practice.If we had relied on a corporate platform that decided, under political pressure, to restrict or remove us, you could have lost access to that live blog in the middle of the Alaska fight, precisely when accurate information mattered most.That is why Democracy Docket built its own custom technology stack: to ensure it is never beholden to venture capital firms, tech CEOs or corporations whose interests and alliances shift with the wind. Honestly, this makes operating Democracy Docket harder, more expensive and often a headache.But managing our own platform is another way we ensure Democracy Docket stays fiercely independent and unapologetically pro-democracy. It makes it far harder for any one company to be pressured by Donald Trump into cutting us off, and far harder for any one vendor to cripple us.There are other benefits as well.It is never sold or traded, and you won’t receive emails urging you to sign up for some other site or product.There are no Nazis on Democracy Docket, no right-wing propaganda and no one promoting crypto schemes., our subscribers and members, including by hosting a live blog in the middle of a critical election.Across the country, we’ve watched media owners and executives curry favor with Trump, trading tough coverage for access or bowing to the fear of lawsuits, investigations and prosecution. Democracy Docket is built to withstand those pressures.Democracy Docket is powered by premium members who pay $120 a year, just $10 a month, for access to all of its content. It simply cannot do its work without them. If you are able, please consider joining the more than 70,000 members who make this work possible.We have fought long and hard for this victory, but this is not the end of the road. Donald Trump is still in the White House. The weaponization of government against Trump’s political opponents is escalating.Democracy Docket will be there every step of the way. I am proud to have you on our team.

item.title: It’s Golden Dukes Time of Year – Golden Stefaniks?

item.title: JD Vance is America’s worst insult comedian
item.content:encoded: Theories abound as to why JD Vance, once a promising Yale Law graduate with a best-selling memoir, went MAGA. Some argue that it was always a mistake to confuse the vice president’s cosmopolitanism for intellectual sophistication, pointing out that “Hillbilly Elegy” is a bad book that panders to ugly right-wing stereotypes about his working class family of origin. Others suggest he is an empty shell who will become whatever it takes to gain money and power, as evidenced by his constantly shifting attitudes about race and religion. The truth likely falls in the “why not both?” arena. After all, empty and insecure people have often been drawn to far-right ideologies. But there is one under-appreciated possibility for the MAGA turn of a man who once called Donald Trump “America’s Hitler”: that he finally found an audience willing to laugh at his unfunny jokes.Vance is clearly embroiled in a lifelong struggle with a common ailment of self-serious men who consider themselves profound geniuses. He longs to be the funniest guy in the room, but he is unable to understand how humor works. But the vice president has discovered what second-rate talents that end up as the “comic” relief on Fox News learned long ago: The right-wing crowd doesn’t care if you’re not funny just as long as you’re cruel. Vance is taking full advantage of MAGA’s lack of discernment in the last weeks of the midterm campaign. During a stop in Texas supporting the Republican Senate candidate, state Attorney General Ken Paxton, Vance responded to a fan by saying, “I love you, too, sir. And in a totally platonic way, to be clear. I’m the vice president, not James Talarico.” The audience roared with laughter, apparently unable to realize that calling Paxton’s Democratic opponent “gay” is less witty than if Vance had made fart noises with his armpit. The vice president can’t stop with tedious jokes about Talarico, who is leading in statewide polls. On his way to Texas, Vance falsely accused Talarico of having “a weird focus on transgender kids and drag queens,” topics that he and Trump bring up every chance they get. Vance added, “typically people who say stuff like that tend to have some pretty unusual search histories.” But Vance isn’t content to simply dabble in homophobia and transphobia. Racism is also his forte. During a North Carolina rally on Monday, he called non-white congresswomen “crazies” and mispronounced the name of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn. When a protester jumped up to demand that the Trump administration release the Epstein files, Vance suggested, apparently taking note of the young man’s darker skin, that the protester was in the U.S. because of “illegal border crossings.” At another event, Vance called Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan’s Democratic candidate for Senate, a “little weasel” who should “shut his mouth and show a little gratitude.” This was not out of character; the vice president often demands that people of color bow and scrape before white people for graciously allowing them to exist. But this time he got rebuked by the far funnier El-Sayed, who responded that Vance “had a cute little rally” with the “five people who like him.”But the vice president’s lack of wit was perhaps best illustrated at an Ohio rally in support of GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, when he suggested that Dr. Amy Acton, the Democratic nominee, has a substance abuse problem. “Vance’s implication can be traced to a Republican ad that paints Acton as an alcoholic after a 2019 incident in which the police were called during a loud fight with her husband. The call was reported not violent by officers, and her campaign claims the situation is being blown out of proportion. (Acton has also been hit with ads featuring insults from her mother, Donna Arthur, with whom she has been estranged since 1978 after Arthur refused to support her when she accused her stepfather of molesting and raping her between the ages of nine and 12. According to the New York Times, Acton’s stepfather entered a not-guilty plea and was indicted by a grand jury, then went on the run from Ohio before standing trial.) Vance’s stream of insults ring particularly noxious when considering that he spent the summer portraying himself as a heartfelt Catholic convert whose salvation has imbued him with a newfound sense of Christian grace.Vance’s stream of insults ring particularly noxious when considering that he spent the summer portraying himself as a heartfelt Catholic convert whose salvation has imbued him with a newfound sense of Christian grace. In an obvious effort to soft-launch a 2028 presidential campaign, the vice president published “Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith” in June, and strived mightily to convince interviewers they were beholding a humble servant of Jesus Christ. Vance told USA Today that “my faith tells me to fight against” the blind pursuit of ambition and instead “focus on the good” and “make wise decisions and moral decisions.” In an excerpt published in the Wall Street Journal, he wrote that he’s learned “to love all parts of our Christian communion,” including those “who voted for me and those who didn’t.” He went on “The View” with this gentle Christian message, claiming regret over “boneheaded” insults in the past, such as when he described childless women as being “miserable,” “sociopathic” and “cat ladies. The hosts weren’t having it, though, pointing out that there is nothing of Christian communion in the administration’s attacks on Black people and immigrants, and leaving a visibly uncomfortable vice president to pretend not to know what they were talking about. Vance may be able to wriggle around his very un-Christian insults and falsehoods about Democratic politicians by calling politics a “dirty business,” as he did in the Wall Street Journal. But it’s impossible to square his claims of grace and salvation with the utter nastiness he unleashes on immigrants, most of whom are Christians themselves. He has yet to apologize for falsely accusing Haitian immigrants — most of whom are Catholic, like himself — of stealing people’s dogs and cats to eat them. Shortly after publishing “Communion,” Vance accused immigrants of making America “dirtier and poorer and less safe and less prosperous.” (This is also flat-out false, as immigration has been proven to boost the economy, and the country is objectively cleaner than it was decades ago, when a thick cloud of smog hung over many American cities.)Through it all, Vance seems to be hoping that the crowd that sees his “Christian charity” face isn’t the same one showing up to hoot at his lame “no homo” jokes about the devout Talarico. This behavior was on display during his recent CBS town hall event, where he tucked away the bad insult comedy and put on his choir boy mask. The dishonesty and hypocrisy reached stratospheric levels when audience members, including a Catholic nun, challenged Vance on his support for mass deportations and his racist lies about immigrants. “To the extent that my rhetoric has been imperfect here,” Vance said, “that’s on me.” Then he framed the administration’s widespread abuses as reasonable, even compassionate, restrictions on immigration. His comments came mere hours after he falsely blamed the riots in France on immigrants, posing on X that “liberals imported the third world into France and other countries” while “ignor[ing] fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility.” No doubt Vance would deflect and deny if he were confronted on it, but there’s no way to interpret his words except as a claim that people of different backgrounds cannot live together without violence — a frequent insinuation of his that is never slowed by the fact that his own wife and children are Indian-American. This is ultimately why — despite the undeniable ugliness of Vance’s insults of Democrats, immigrants, queer people and single women — his humor rarely generates the outrage he’s clearly trolling for. Vance tends to come across as more of a pathetic striver than an effective bully. Verbal jabs work a lot better if the would-be roaster has a sense of self- confidence, or at least the ability to fake it. Whether he’s speaking of love or hate, Vance never really seems to be talking with any conviction at all, beyond the hope that whatever he’s saying will win him more power.

item.title: Fragmented Landscapes
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: I don’t think it’s a surprise at this point when I tell you that I love these artworks by Antwerp-based artist Joost Vandebrug. (I mean, tell me they don’t aesthetically rhyme with the KDO logo circles/moons…)Joost Vandebrug explores how separate views and moments come to be seen as a whole. His landscapes gather fragments into places that feel familiar, even when no single place could contain them. The image takes shape through remembering and looking, while the joins keep its construction visible.Each work is built from dozens of photo-emulsion transfers on handmade paper cards. I transfer and reassemble them individually. Nothing is ever the same — every card has its imperfections. When I lay them together, they form a new landscape — part remembered, part reinvented.Yeah, I love everything about this — the chunky pointillism, analog pixel art, small multiples, even Magic the Gathering vibes (if you think of the artworks as playable decks). Check out more of his work on his website and Instagram. Thanks to my pal Yen for the intro to his work; she snapped a photo of Vandebrug’s work in a gallery she visited recently.

item.title: Blackpool To Coach: Happy Birthday, You’re Fired
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: Much derision fell upon the people who run Blackpool Football Club of League One, the third tier of English football, when it wished head coach Ian Evatt a happy birthday seven hours before firing him on Thursday. It did seem exceedingly cruel, even by the prevailing bastardy standards of our time.Then again, only a simp would believe that human decency enters into decisions like these. Your holidays aren't anyone else's, so stop acting like they are. This is especially true when the only thing keeping you out of a relegation spot is goal differential. In that situation, your employer very well might call you "Gaffer" in the morning and can you by happy hour. That's the gig.The rudimentarily funny part is how the club announced his firing. According to them, Evatt "departed his role," as though he chose to fire himself. This is not just an English politeness thing, either. Teams and the media types who exist to disseminate their team sources' text messages love to describe firings as "a parting of ways," or the coach "leaving his role," or beating feet "by mutual agreement," and over time, that creeps into the language used by normal fans. It's as if we each have an HR goblin in our homes, ready to spring malevolently into action at any moment.
