item.title: Cornyn Nixes Judgeship for OLC Head After Shouting Match With Ted Cruz
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: Author of Boat Strike Memo Is From OhioOutgoing Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX) appears to have killed the judicial nomination of T. Elliot Gaiser, the 37-year-old head of the Office of Legal Counsel at the Trump DOJ who authored legal justifications for some of the administration’s most egregious extralegal conduct, including the lawless boat strike campaign.“He’s not from Texas. He hasn’t been vetted. And this is a lifetime job, and there’s better qualified people to hold that job,” Cornyn told the AP. “This is part, of course, of the constitutional responsibility of senators in the Senate to provide advice and consent. But it’s hard to provide advice and consent when there’s zero consultation, which happened in that case.”Gaiser did not appear on the confirmation hearing yesterday for a batch of Trump judicial nominees (who as a group refused to say that the Capitol was attacked on Jan. 6, 2021). Cornyn’s leverage over the nomination comes from the Senate’s “blue-slip” tradition, still honored by Senate Judiciary Committee Chair Charles Grassley (R-IA), of not moving judicial nominations without the approval of home state senators.Cornyn’s public break with the administration came after he and Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX) got into a loud argument on the Senate floor Tuesday over the Gaiser nomination. The whole imbroglio is heavily colored by Cornyn losing re-election in the GOP primary after Trump endorsed his opponent Ken Paxton, who went on to lose the general election that Cornyn his convinced he himself would have won.Things continued to spill out in public on Wednesday with the Justice Department tacking a whack at Cornyn: “It is deeply disappointing that Senator Cornyn would choose political obstruction over advancing a highly qualified nominee.”Cruz put out his own statement warning that there’s not time to confirm anyone else to the vacant judgeship: “If the Senate Judiciary Committee does not move Gaiser forward, the people of Texas will pay the price because it will effectively give the judicial seat to the Democrats, who will keep it vacant in perpetuity,” Cruz said. “That would be a tragedy.”Another outgoing GOP senator primaried by President Trump got a measure of revenge.Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-LA), the chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, abruptly cancelled a committee vote on the nomination of Jim O’Neill to lead the National Science Foundation.O’Neill previously worked in multiple roles at the Department of Health and Human Services under Robert F. Kennedy Jr. He “did not do enough to stand up for science and against irresponsible decisions and statements from Secretary Kennedy,” said Cassidy, who indicated that some other members of the committee shared his concerns.Cassidy’s move effectively scuttled the nomination.Election 2026 By the NumbersA few new data points as the vote-counting nears an end:Democrats lead in the national House vote has expanded to 14-percentage points, the largest margin by either party since Democrats romped by 16.6 points in the 1974 post-Watergate election.Democrats have won at least 257 House seats, with six races still uncalled by the AP.At least 109 House seats will be held by freshman, the most since at least 1998.: Allies have launched Team Pete PAC to back another presidential run by the former secretary of transportation. (Politico): The Democratic senator from Arizona is bringing longtime aide Emma Brown back into the fold as he considers a White House run. (Politico): “Looking at it right now, it’s absolutely a savagely brutal map,” said Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH), the incoming chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee. (Politico)The Dog That’s Obviously Not BarkingAfter the Trump DOJ brought a flurry of noncitizen voting cases right before the election — touting them with press releases, press conferences, and mug shots — it has brought only one new noncitizen voting case since the Nov. 3 election, the WaPo reports.The Corruption: IRS EditionProPublica reports on under-the-radar Trump administration settlement of a claims against the IRS for leaking taxpayer info.It recalls Trump’s own settlement with the IRS and the planned creation of $1.776 billion slush fund.But it’s not Trump this time.It’s the longtime golf pro at Trump National Golf Club Hudson Valley.And despite the settlement, the case isn’t over yet.Two other people connected to Trump properties are trying to get in on the action: a retired accountant at Trump National Golf Club Hudson Valley and a former lifeguard at the Trump golf club in Westchester County, New York.Colorado Public Radio: In a new contempt of court ruling, U.S. District Judge Charlotte Sweeney excoriated ICE for repeatedly violating court orders with its policy of immediately re-detaining immigrants after they had been ordered to be released from detention. But Sweeney declined to take any further action, ruling that ICE officials had cured the contempt of court by ceasing the practice at issue.Greg Sargent: ICE has $91 billion of no-strings-attached funding to spend on deportations between now and the end of Trump’s second term.Nicholas Kristof: Trump ‘Disappeared’ Them in 2025. I Found Them, Locked Up and Famished.Bo French Booted From Country ClubRepublican Bo French’s racist (and losing) campaign for Texas Railroad Commission has cost him his membership in the River Crest Country Club in Fort Worth. The country club’s board of directors booted him after he refused to resign his membership.Thanks For All the AI Feedback!I received quite a rich and varied response to my question yesterday about which AI tools you’ve found to be useful. Many thanks for taking the time to email.First off, y’all are awesome. You’re a remarkable cross section of creatives and what we now call “knowledge workers” (I hate that term): scientists, engineers, teachers, musicians, writers, attorneys, CEOs, founders, environmental consultants, and IT experts — many of whom are also doing side gigs for fun. Those of you who purport to be retired are busy af, serving on boards and volunteering and running your own pet projects.You’ve discovered uses for AI that range from the practical to the whimsical to the sublime. This initial sampling of reader responses are personal and side projects uses that delighted me:TPM Reader : “I manage my own forested acreage in Washington State for enjoyment, health, and minor income. I was kind of at a point where I wanted to get more focused, more deliberate, and more comprehensive in my management planning and use of my time and labor. My son suggested I get a monthly ChatGPT account to facilitate that. The results have been dazzling.”TPM Reader : “It helped me build two ten foot bird feeder poles with offset arms to stop raccoons and squirrels.”TPM Reader : “Because of ChatGPT I have been able to do a pet project, a searchable index of historic cookbooks in the public domain.”

item.title: Shh! Don’t wake Preznit Fuckwit — international geopolitics makes him sleepy
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: That’s right, the narcoleptic old fart factory’s brain went again yesterday, right in the middle of an APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in China.But before we get to that —This is just so fucking bizarre. Are we all on crazy pills right now?How creepy is this? Why is she there? She has no legitimate function in that room. How does this keep happening, in meeting after meeting? Does she simply invite herself along, and no one says ? Imagine you’re a world leader, sitting across the table from all that. How could you even concentrate, with that spectacle going on? What do you say to your spouse when you get home? ‘You will never fucking believe what happened today. The silly dipshit brought a dateYou know what? Let’s skip over the question of why is Natty there, because here’s a better question: Why is there? What value does presence add? All he does is ramble incoherently about his own imaginary accomplishments, and piss and moan if he doesn’t get a toy.“There’s never been a time like this. But of course it was— right here— in this [unintelligible] palace that President— Quezon bestowed General Douglas MacArthur with a gold— baton, and the rank of Field Marshall in the Philippine Army. I’d like to have you do that for me, if you don’t mind. I’d love that. I mean, why the hell shouldn’t I get that?”Yeah, come on, President Marcos, get with the program. Don’t you know by now that Donny always gets a participation trophy, no matter where he goes? FIFA gave him one. So did NASA. So give the whiny little piss-baby his fucking gold baton before he falls to pieces, like a child in a supermarket who can’t have candy.Seriously, what’s the point of even having Donny there at your meeting? My advice to every international organization — APEC, the Quad, NATO, the G7, the United Nations, the OAS, — is this: the next time you hold a wingding, don’t bother inviting Donny. I promise that you won’t even notice his absence, except for maybe air quality having been improved by the lack of narcoleptic farts. After Dear Leader shit the bed in the Philippines, it was on to China, where Donny was serenely unaware that he was the mark.“They’re treating me extremely well for China, and I have a lot of respect and a good relationship with President Xi ... nobody is gonna play games with us.”Oh my god, this gullible goofus has no idea he was being set up to be swindled. He’s so easily manipulated that it isn’t even funny. the Chinese are treating him ‘extremely well’ — they’re buttering him up so they can pick his pockets. Donny is like the chump at the blackjack table in a Las Vegas casino. He’s losing his shirt, but all he can do is marvel over how they keep giving him free drinks. Donny: Fox bobblehead: “Are you going to tell them to stop buying Iranian oil?”Donny: “You know, when they say that China is working with— with uh, Iran, or Russia’s working with Iran, no, no. What, they’re giving some information? We have all the information that they give. We know exactly what they’re giving. It’s peanuts.”Hang on, did Dear Leader just hand-wave away China and Russia feeding intel to Iran, because ? He did, didn’t he. What in the actual fuck?Look, it’s not just that’s being provided to Iran. China is Iran’s largest buyer of crude oil. Russia is helping Iran re-arm itself. Do you imagine that Donny doesn’t know that, or just doesn’t care, because — as he so idiotically puts it — I can’t decide which scenario is worse. What a great idea it was, to let a greedy and easily-flattered shit-for-brains be president. Tell me, is allowing our adversaries to get away with aiding a country we’re at war with, because you expect you’ll personally benefit from doing so — would that be a I’m hopeful that we’ll find out at Donny’s third impeachment trial, next year.Now I can hear you out there, going ‘but Uncle Jeff, what about the Nodfather? You promised at the top of this post that Donny would be sleeping.’Yes, I know I did, but we had to get through the boring-but-more-important stuff first. Don’t make me come over there and explain how clickbait works.Holy fuck, Dear Leader is out like a light. He doesn’t move a millimeter during the entire clip. The only way to tell that you’re not looking at a still photograph is that you can see Soybean Scott Bessent’s smug haughty head moving in the background, behind Donny.Who thought it would be a good idea to let a doddering demento attend four meetings across two countries in one day? I have an idea. Can we get that Arlington Guard back in here, to stand behind Donny and scream ‘ALL PRESIDENTS WILL MAINTAIN AN ATMOSPHERE OF NOT FALLING THE FUCK ASLEEP AND EMBARRASSING YOUR ENTIRE COUNTRY’?Because that would fucking rule.And now, on to our Daily Claudia.Here are two photos taken in Plymouth, MA, back in the early 1990s, by Daughter Katie. This first one is from before she was old enough to have figured out that whole ‘don’t crop people’s heads off’ thing.And this second one, thankfully, is from after.Have a great Thursday, everyone. Oh wait — one final thing before I let you go.I have no idea what this unsubscriber means by ‘too much porn type stuff.’ Is it the cussing? Folks, I hope you’re all reading these posts and discovering that I have a sweary fucking mouth you plunk down your hard-earned cash on a paid subscription. Oh, and don’t be fooled by all the free drinks at the blackjack table.Okay, you can all fucking well have a great fucking Thursday.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: The NFL Trade Deadline Is Fine Right Where It Is

item.content:encoded: If you were up early last Sunday, you may have borne witness to this NFL season’s most catastrophic play, in which Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson took out Pats QB Drake Maye for the season, and then took out for the season mere seconds later. ACH!Not only did these two injuries severely hamper the postseason prospects of both the Patriots and Lions, but they also turned what would have otherwise been a compelling Munich game into a big ol’ doo-doo fest. item.title: High-End Furniture Marketplace AptDeco Is Taking People’s Furniture and Not Paying Them
item.author: Jason Koebler
item.content:encoded: This article has been updated with comment from AptDeco.Last month, Erin sold a $3,000 large designer table on AptDeco, a white glove high-end furniture marketplace. More than a month later, she feels like she’s been literally robbed.“AptDeco sent three men to physically collect my table on October 13, and here we are on November 16, with no payment and no concrete explanation for where my $2,000 (after their absurd $900 fee) is,” Erin told me. “It genuinely feels like I’ve had something stolen from me.”AptDeco is a Y Combinator-backed company whose entire purpose is to take the risk out of places like Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist for designer furniture resale. It advertises itself as “simple and seamless,” and says “we handle pickup, delivery, and payments,” and claims that it pays sellers “within 5-10 business days.” But over the last few months, people who have sold furniture on the platform say that AptDeco has sold their furniture and taken it from their houses, but hasn’t paid them. 404 Media agreed to only use Erin’s first name because she is still trying to get her money from the company.“Adding to the chorus of people who sold an item thru AptDeco and never received payment. I have no idea what to do at this point,” another says. “Can we do a class action lawsuit?” another reads.“They owed me money since September 30th,” a fourth says. Every recent review and complaint on AptDeco’s Better Business Bureau page is from sellers who have not been paid: “Almost 6 weeks after they picked up and not being paid Pick up was a nightmare too No calls nobody doing anything Do NOT SELL ON APTDECO,” one reads. Another states “I have been in an endless loop with customer service for 2 months trying to get my payout for the bed I sold. I am losing faith that I will ever see this money. Extremely frustrated at this experience.”On AptDeco’s website, everything appears to be business as usual. You can still buy and sell furniture, and there is no indication of anything wrong at all. 404 Media’s repeated attempts to reach AptDeco to ask what was going on went unreturned.In communications with sellers seen by 404 Media, AptDeco’s customer service representatives have repeatedly blamed their payment processor, a “technical bug,” or have said the payment is “moving through the system.” On November 3, AptDeco told Erin that a bug had prevented her from being paid, that the payment team “retried” it, and that she would be paid within 10 days. “I’ve asked our team to prioritize your payout personally, so you should see it in your bank account by then - hopefully sooner! At this point, we’re doing everything we can to get your payout processed,” a customer support email reviewed by 404 Media reads. On Tuesday, two weeks after the company told her the payment had been retried, a different customer service representative followed up and said “I'm truly sorry — I know this isn't the update you were hoping for. Your payout is still being prioritized by our payments team, and I want to be honest with you: I don't yet have a confirmed release date or timeline to share.”Several other people who have sold items on AptDeco recently told 404 Media they’re experiencing the same problem.Harry Heymann sold a Room & Board couch on AptDeco in late September and still has not been paid the $120 he is owed by the platform. The messages he’s gotten from AptDeco customer support read much the same as Erin’s: They claim “a technical bug on our end held up your payout” and the customer service representative said “I’ve asked our team to prioritize your payout personally.” Late last week, he got what reads like an AI-generated message that reads “I know how frustrating this has been. You've been waiting on your $120 payout, the date you were given has passed, and you've had to follow up to get answers. That's not the experience we want for you, and I'm truly sorry. Your case has been escalated to me, and l'm happy to be your point of contact from here. Unfortunately, the issue with our payment processor has not yet been resolved, and our team is still working on it.” Natalie Simmons sold an armoire in late August and told 404 Media she initially had a good experience compared to using other platforms. But then she never got her money. “After so many uncomfortable situations on different social sites I was so happy when I found AptDeco,” she told me. “I received notification that my payment would arrive in 3-5 business days through the portal in app. That was Aug 30th. I tried calling but the voicemail says leave a message and they will respond by email. I emailed several times and finally after 2 weeks and a few voicemails I received an email that there was a glitch with their payment system and I will receive payment within 5-10 business days. After another 2 weeks I called and emailed again that I still didn’t receive payment. They sent another email with the exact same story. I just want to get paid. It’s not even that much but it’s the principle.”It’s not just sellers who have had issues with the platform. One customer, K Turner, bought a couch and tried to return it. Rather than giving her a refund, the company said they would relist it at the price she paid and then give her a “refund” of whatever it sold for minus fees. The couch resold quickly at the beginning of September and the company told her she would quickly get her “refund.” More than a month later, on October 20, they told her “I have gone ahead and processed that refund ($600) manually. Please allow 5-10 business days for this refund to be reflected back to your original form of payment.” She has still not gotten her money. “The communication was decent at first, but once they confirmed the item resold on September 8th, they then went silent. It took me a month to finally get a response. They confirmed that the item resold at the full listing price of $600 and that I would receive my refund to my original payment in 5 - 10 business days,” Turner told me. “That was nearly a month ago, and I still don't have my money. So, they effectively double-dipped. They got my money from the original order and then collected money by reselling it. And who knows if they ever gave the money to the original seller; maybe they triple-dipped. I have threatened legal action twice now.”The customers I spoke to have no idea what happens next. Some of them said they were going to file claims in small claims court or are considering a class action lawsuit. But the company is mostly giving them what appear to be canned, copy-pasted statements that come from a revolving cast of customer support email addresses, and no actual updates. Four emails from 404 Media asking for comment, including emails sent to the company’s CEO, have not been returned. AptDeco promises a high-end, safe experience when compared to somewhere like Facebook Marketplace or Craigslist, and markets itself primarily for more expensive, lightly-used furniture. The people I spoke to said they wish they had just stayed off the platform altogether.“The irony is that I’m now feeling safer selling expensive designer furniture directly to strangers on Facebook Marketplace than through a platform whose entire purpose is supposedly to make these transactions safer and more secure,” Erin said. “At this point, AptDeco has my furniture, I have no money, and I’m left chasing them for something I’m already owed. It’s an incredibly unsettling position to be in, particularly when so many other sellers seem to be experiencing the same thing. The fact that I continue to receive email marketing newsletters and see them selling via Google Ads—paying that platform before their sellers—is infuriating.”After this article was published (and three days after we initially asked for comment), an AptDeco spokesperson gave 404 Media a convoluted explanation involving “bot swarms,” which it blamed for the delays in seller payouts. “Over the past few months, we’ve been dealing with an unprecedented volume of bot activity, some of it malicious. This has created a myriad of challenges that we’ve been actively working to address.These bot swarms, along with the broader cybersecurity challenges of an AI-evolving world, prompted us to significantly strengthen our site’s security to ensure the long-term protection of our buyers and sellers,” the spokesperson said. “To be clear, customer data has not been compromised in any way. However, we’ve been investing heavily in preventative measures to further protect our community. Unfortunately, some of these efforts have resulted in delays in seller payouts. As you can imagine, cybersecurity is a complex and sensitive topic, making it challenging to communicate all the details broadly. That said, the issue has now been resolved, and outstanding payouts are being processed. Any seller with questions can email and will hear back within 1 business day. We appreciate your patience and understanding.”When I asked for clarification because it was not clear how bot swarms would affect payouts, the spokesperson said “the bot swarm did not affect seller payouts.”“We deployed code to further improve protections for our customers (given the bot swarms) which inadvertently impacted seller payout processing. Providing additional technical context would require a detailed understanding of our codebase and would likely be more information than is relevant or useful to readers,” they added. “That said, we sincerely apologize to our customers for the delays and are committed to making things right. The issue has been resolved, our security infrastructure remains extremely robust, and outstanding payouts are being processed. We appreciate you reaching out and giving us the opportunity to clarify. This will be our final comment on the matter.”also pointed out that the company is being sued by American Express for allegedly failing to pay a $158,461 credit card bill from 2024; that case is in default judgment but is ongoing.

item.title: The Energy Tax of Living in a New Place
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Before moving abroad, I was really independent. I loved socialising, visiting new places, trying new things. But over the past few years I’ve become so much more anxious and reserved, and I only just realised why.When you live somewhere familiar, life is second nature. You know the language, the systems, the culture, and the social expectations. You have routines, support and things are predictable.But when you live abroad, the energy required to participate in life increases. Socialising, going to appointments, buying a coffee, answering the phone. Everything requires so much more planning, energy and courage.When you’re already mentally exhausted, you have less energy for the things you want and should do. You avoid situations that feel difficult. You become more reserved, less confident, more isolated and less independent.I’m writing this at the airport after spending 2.5 months in Tokyo and feeling the above . I’ve never been what you’d call outgoing, but after the initial rush of being here wore off after a few weeks, I definitely noticed myself becoming “more reserved, less confident, more isolated and less independent”. Some days, I barely left my apartment because I couldn’t bear summoning the energy to make a plan, negotiate a new restaurant, or figure out how to get from point A to point B on the train. I sought out places that were easy: online ticketing, digital ordering screens, English menus, chain stores & restaurants.The confidence piece is probably the hardest for me. I have to work hard in social situations with people I don’t know, and doing that in a language I don’t speak and in a cultural context I don’t fully understand is challenging, especially when I need to do it 10 times a day. I rely on humor in situations like these and, well, I don’t know how to be funny in Japan. Confidence tends to be a pervasive trait — a dip in one area of your life causes an overall decline across many areas. And all this is coming after living for the past decade in a place where I never felt like I fit in.Anyway, it’s been eye-opening, this shift in energy & confidence. I’m onto the next place soon, but this is something I definitely need to keep an eye on.

item.title: How Much Better Can Matthew Schaefer Get?
item.author: Barry Petchesky
item.content:encoded: Matthew Schaefer, the best NHL defenseman of the next generation and maybe already this one, is a pleasure to watch. The first unanimous Calder winner in 33 years, he finished second on the New York Islanders in both goals and assists last season. As a defenseman! As an 18-year-old! There is a damn teenager at the controls of the Isles' offense, driving play at both ends of the ice and looking so impossibly assured that he was named alternate captain in his second year, and nobody thinks this is weird or fluky. Sure, he was a no-brainer for first overall pick, but even wunderteens usually require some period of adjustment.Year two has started even hotter. Twenty games in, Schaefer leads the Islanders in points (nine goals, 15 assists), all the while playing the fourth-most minutes per game of the entire league. Young legs are nice to have, but he's out here playing entire overtimes without coming off. His defense is good, if not quite elite—he's still vulnerable to being forechecked, and his positioning can sometimes be off—but the stage for the Schaefer Show is 200 feet long. He's a demon in transition and a menace in the offensive zone. "We're watching greatness kind of evolve," teammate Mathew Barzal said.The most complimentary thing I can say about Schaefer's scoring is that he is not by any means a chucker. He's not perched at the blue line, clapping pucks on a prayer, like some empty-calorie offensive defensemen I could name. His very reasonable shot percentage both last year and this represent neither a player who has been especially lucky, nor a volume scorer taking away other, potentially shorter-odds opportunities. He is earning his points with his decisions.

item.title: Black Neighborhoods Are Twice as Likely To House a Data Center, Study Finds
item.author: Matthew Gault
item.content:encoded: Developers build data centers in communities of color at more than twice the rate they do in white neighborhoods, according to a new study from researchers at George Washington University and the Center for Security, Innovation & New Technology (CSINT) at American University.According to the study, “Redlining in the Age of AI: The Relationship between Data Center Locations and Race in the US” majority-Black neighborhoods have 2.2 times the odds of hosting a data center than a white neighborhood in the same state. The number goes up to 2.6 in majority-Hispanic neighborhoods and 4.2 times in majority-Asian neighborhoods. “As the share of Black, Hispanic, and Asian residents in a neighborhood increases, so do the odds that the neighborhood hosts a data center,” the researchers wrote.The researchers ran the numbers by examining 81,000 US census tracts and location data for 5,291 data centers. “We found that these racial disparities persist even after accounting for factors such as population, household income, education, land costs, proximity to major transmission lines, and state fixed effects,” they wrote. “These results hold even though data centers are concentrated in and around metropolitan areas, which are often more racially diverse.”“We really wanted to look at this on a nationwide scale to see: is this something that fits into this broader structural racism story?” CSINT executive director Samantha Bradshaw told 404 Media. “What we did find was yes [...] neighborhoods that have data centers tend to have a higher ratio of people of color.”Bradshaw and co-author Dhanaraj Thakur told 404 Media that they were inspired to do the study after reading stories about data centers in Memphis, Tennessee polluting Black and Brown communities. Another high profile case occurred in Taylor, Texas where a white family donated a tract of land to the city with the intention it become a public part. That land abutted a Black neighborhood. The city never built a park there and now it’s slated to become a data centerAccording to the researchers, the historical legacy of — the process of denying Americans of color loans and other opportunities to keep them in specific neighborhoods — is to blame for some of this. Data centers are often built near transmission lines because they provide ease of access to power infrastructure, for example. Those transmission lines were often built in majority Black neighborhoods in America. Thakur said he doubted that data centers developers were seeking to intentionally put data centers in communities of color. “It’s just how embedded race is with all these other factors,” he said. The study distinguished between several different kinds of data centers and noted there are massive differences between hyperscalers like what Meta, Google, and Grok are building and smaller mixed use buildings that often serve as network transmission hubs as well as compute warehouses, which the study called “co-location facilities.” When a hyperscaler comes to town, the developers sometimes promise economic investment in the community where it’s being constructed and those facilities typically aren’t built in communities of color..Meta is building a $50 billion data center in rural Louisiana. Community leaders there have said it would bring 1,000 permanent jobs and that sales tax revenues have already jumped 2,000 percent, leading to a $50,000 bonus for area teachers. Even here, there is disparity. Most of the hyperscalers that promise massive economic benefits to local communities are built in white rural communities. The study makes several suggestions about what to do about all this including data center-specific zoning regulations, prioritizing racial equity in discussions around building them, and requiring racial impact statements for data centers before they’re built. Thakur and Bradshaw emphasized that tech policy should be a negotiation between the companies that provide the tech and the communities that use it. Data centers have spurred these conversations — they’re physical representations of Big Tech’s powers, a power that Americans recently rejected at the ballot box. “AI has a physical geography, and that geography is shaped by political and social history,” the researchers wrote in the study.“I think the issue around how racial justice, civil rights plays into many other kinds of policies —health, education, housing, whatever it is — we just don't see enough of that consideration in tech policy, and I think this this kind of analysis shows why we should be doing that, thinking about that more,” Thakur said.Bradshaw agreed. “If you look at who's represented in tech policy and who built these systems, who designs them, who engineers them, it's a very specific kind of white male Silicon Valley California ideology engineer, and that is not representative of the technology and its users,” she said. “So I think bringing in these perspectives is really really important because then we can truly think about ways to design a tech future that is for everybody.

item.title: Mass Surveillance and GTA
item.author: Joseph Cox
item.content:encoded: I got an internal ICE document that shows the agency is paying telecommunications giant AT&T for access to raw data. Multiple experts I showed the document to say this is a continuation of Hemisphere, a thought-to-be-shuttered mass surveillance program, but which they say is now back, just in direct payments from ICE to AT&T. “The Biden administration shut down Hemisphere after I and Rep. Biggs repeatedly questioned this warrantless mass phone surveillance program. 404 Media’s reporting shows that the Trump-Vance administration has created a zombie version of Hemisphere surveillance, and given it to their chosen enforcers at ICE,” Senator Ron Wyden said in a statement.Also, happy Grand Theft Auto day! We hope you play and contribute less to the world’s economy.Immigration and Customs Enforcement is paying telecommunications giant AT&T millions of dollars to have AT&T’s analysts sift through mountains of raw AT&T data for a wide variety of investigations, according to an internal ICE document obtained by 404 Media, other procurement records, and experts who reviewed those records. Civil liberty experts havecalled it a mass surveillance program, and they say the data can include trillions of phone records and location data. The AT&T product, interchangeably called Data Analytics and Support Services or Data Analytical Services, appears to be related to an earlier surveillance program called Hemisphere, in which AT&T provided U.S. authorities at state, local, and federal levels access to AT&T user data. Though that program shut down, ICE is still paying for access to raw data under this new arrangement with AT&T, according to the restricted ICE procurement document obtained by 404 Media. The program likely affects more than just AT&T customers because the company connects phone calls for other phone companies, meaning noncustomers are likely swept up too, according to a surveillance expert.“This requirement provides ICE access to AT&T’s raw data and experienced analysts,” the document obtained by 404 Media reads.AT&T told 404 Media the data is made available under a valid legal order, but experts point out it requires an administrative subpoena, which agencies can issue themselves and don’t require a judge’s approval, raising concerns that ICE can use the data for essentially whatever it wants. The document also shows how financial incentives play a part in providing data to ICE.“The Biden administration shut down Hemisphere after I and Rep. Biggs repeatedly questioned this warrantless mass phone surveillance program. 404 Media’s reporting shows that the Trump-Vance administration has created a zombie version of Hemisphere surveillance, and given it to their chosen enforcers at ICE,” Senator Ron Wyden told 404 Media in a statement.Christopher Soghoian, a surveillance expert who worked for Senator Wyden for a decade until September, told 404 Media, “It’s bad enough that AT&T is mining its customers’ private phone records as a paid service for ICE, but because AT&T is also mining the records of other wholesale telecom companies, consumers can’t vote with their wallets and switch carriers to protect their privacy.”Last September, ICE posted a procurement record a contract to AT&T for access to its Data Analytics and Support Services. When ICE announced the purchase, an attached document to the listing was marked as “controlled” and not available to the public. 404 Media subsequently obtained the document through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request with ICE.The Financial Times previously reported on the public procurement records but did not report on the restricted document at the time.This segment is a paid ad. If you’re interested in advertising, Use code 404MEDIA The way cable and local news cover Grand Theft Auto has radically changed over the years. Of course, American culture changed too. Matthew Gault wrote this illuminating piece on just that, and he watched a lot, a lot, of old news coverage of the game franchise to figure out what is different today. (It’s money.), remember when an army unit offered soldiers time off to play the new game, they agreed to more years of military service? Turns out, some people thought that was a great deal. Or at least they really wanted to play GTA at launch. 43 soldiers from the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion signed up for this program, . Sgt. Jamire Smith told the outlet “I’m all campaign. I’m all about the heist,” and “I think I have a good 24 hours to waste on it.” In exchange, Smith agreed to six more years in the Army. I don’t know if the game is good, man., meaning you can’t go into a store and just buy it. You have to download it from the digital store onto your console. The CEO of GameStop, which is obviously a company with its own stupid history too, : “Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop.”The Wachowski sisters are reclaiming the Matrix. The Matrix has been at the center of a lot of recent culture, or really culture wars, long after the original film and even the two earlier sequels came out. The whole exhausting red pill, black pill thing. Lilly Wachowski tried to reclaim that narrative before, by telling Elon Musk and Ivanka Trump when they invoked the red pill. Now, the Wachowskis are trying to reclaim the Matrix more literally. the pair have formally notified Warner Bros “they are exercising their copyright termination rights.” Meaning, the sisters might control the fate of the Matrix as soon as February 2029. The next new sequel is still in development. facing disruptions after the downtime of its internal classified network, from journalist Dustin Volz. “Employees at headquarters are under ‘code orange’ for Thursday day shift, meaning non-essential workers are to stay home unless contacted by their supervisors,” he wrote.Anthropic is going public. The company raised more than $100 billion in a record setting IPO, . That valued the company at around $1.5 trillion. Maybe people saying the bubble would burst after all the Nvidia news were a little hasty.That’s the newsletter for today. Let’s see if they mention any fun criminal encryption stuff in any GTA missions.

item.title: The science of glassblowing. “The constant stimuli of the...

item.content:encoded: The science of glassblowing. “The constant stimuli of the glass studio may not seem anything like a sterile science lab, and yet glass artists need to accrue knowledge of physics and chemistry to achieve any kind of control with this dynamic material.”

item.title: ICE Is Paying AT&T to Dig Through a Mountain of Call Records
item.author: Joseph Cox
item.content:encoded: This article was primarily reported using public records requests. We are making it available to all readers as a public service. FOIA reporting can be expensive, please consider subscribing to 404 Media to support this work. Or send us a one time donation via our tip jar here.Immigration and Customs Enforcement is paying telecommunications giant AT&T millions of dollars to have AT&T’s analysts sift through mountains of raw AT&T data for a wide variety of investigations, according to an internal ICE document obtained by 404 Media, other procurement records, and experts who reviewed those records. Civil liberty experts have called it a mass surveillance program, and they say the data can include trillions of phone records and location data. The AT&T product, interchangeably called Data Analytics and Support Services or Data Analytical Services, appears to be related to an earlier surveillance program called Hemisphere, in which AT&T provided U.S. authorities at state, local, and federal levels access to AT&T user data. Though that program shut down, ICE is still paying for access to raw data under this new arrangement with AT&T, according to the restricted ICE procurement document obtained by 404 Media. The program likely affects more than just AT&T customers because the company connects phone calls for other phone companies, meaning non-customers are likely swept up too, according to a surveillance expert.“This requirement provides ICE access to AT&T’s raw data and experienced analysts,” the document obtained by 404 Media reads.AT&T told 404 Media the data is made available under a valid legal order, but experts point out it requires an administrative subpoena, which agencies can issue themselves and don’t require a judge’s approval, raising concerns that ICE can use the data for essentially whatever it wants. The document also shows how financial incentives play a part in providing data to ICE.“The Biden administration shut down Hemisphere after I and Rep. Biggs repeatedly questioned this warrantless mass phone surveillance program. 404 Media’s reporting shows that the Trump-Vance administration has created a zombie version of Hemisphere surveillance, and given it to their chosen enforcers at ICE,” Senator Ron Wyden told 404 Media in a statement.Christopher Soghoian, a surveillance expert who worked for Senator Wyden for a decade until September, told 404 Media, “It’s bad enough that AT&T is mining its customers’ private phone records as a paid service for ICE, but because AT&T is also mining the records of other wholesale telecom companies, consumers can’t vote with their wallets and switch carriers to protect their privacy.”Last September, ICE posted a procurement record saying it awarded a contract to AT&T for access to its Data Analytics and Support Services. When ICE announced the purchase, an attached document to the listing was marked as “controlled” and not available to the public. 404 Media subsequently obtained the document through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request with ICE. The Financial Times previously reported on the public procurement records but did not report on the restricted document at the time.“OAQ [the Office of Acquisition Management] intends to procure, on a sole source basis, access to raw data and analytical services from a telecommunications company,” the restricted document reads. It says AT&T analysts will transform the AT&T data “into a suitable format” while “ensuring accurate technical interpretation to accomplish HSI’s investigative mission.” HSI is Homeland Security Investigations, the criminal investigative arm of ICE, which has traditionally focused on things like cybercrime and child abuse cases, but under the Trump administration has dramatically refocused on immigration violations and investigating voter fraud.The document says the AT&T data will be used to support “a wide range of HSI investigations and agency priorities,” but the specific sorts of investigations, taking up several lines of the document, are redacted.Another document previously obtained by Senator Wyden’s office lays out the sort of data collected by AT&T and the capabilities available under the Data Analytical Services program. Those services include linking multiple devices or phone numbers to an identified target; identifying devices that have had their SIM cards replaced; determining whether phones associated with an international investigation target have entered the U.S.; and deconflicting international phone numbers associated with targets. That document was provided by the Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP), an obscure White House-affiliated entity that previously funded the Hemisphere program, and which 404 Media reported is behind a growing nationwide network of automatic license plate readers (ALPRs). According to documents previously obtained by the EFF and EPIC, the AT&T program contains more than a trillion phone records.Soghoian added AT&T also provides “wholesale service to other phone companies, helping them to deliver calls.” Through that, “AT&T is able to collect, save, and mine records of calls by customers of other companies, even conversations in which both callers use non-AT&T phone companies.”The restricted document 404 Media obtained says that during Fiscal Year 2025, there was a higher demand for data provided by this AT&T system, and “further significant increase in use is anticipated.”“AT&T is the only vendor who possesses the ability to access AT&T owned raw data,” the document continues. “The requirement is data and analytical services provided by AT&T. If AT&T does not execute the analytical work, the capability will be lost, as no other company has access to the data required.”Public procurement records show ICE paid AT&T more than $2.1 million in 2025 for access to the service, and more than $2.2 million this August, with the possibility to pay up to more than ten million dollars over the coming years.“ICE appears to have contracted for access to the same data and service AT&T provided for the Data Analytical Services (DAS) Program, formerly known as the Hemisphere Project, which is the largest telephone record collection program reported to date. ICE using DAS or something akin to it would potentially come with access to trillions of phone records and location data,” Jeramie Scott, senior counsel at EPIC and director of EPIC's Surveillance Oversight Program, told 404 Media. “This program is ripe for abuse and is being used by an agency known for the abuse of its authority.”“This is AT&T continuing to leverage its phone service to conduct mass, indiscriminate surveillance to sell to law enforcement,” Scott added. “ICE is now taking advantage of AT&T’s surveillance as a service model while likely evading any judicial oversight and conducting no privacy impact assessment prior to using the service to determine whether it should be used in the first place. Spoiler alert: It shouldn’t!”Scott pointed out the data likely includes location information too, and this raises the question whether the program violates the law given Supreme Court rulings Carpenter and Chatrie. The former ruled that law enforcement needed a warrant to obtain phone location data. The latter around location data and geofence warrants.“Americans are pushing back on government surveillance, from Flock cameras to FISA, all across the country and will be rightfully outraged that AT&T is allowing ICE to search through its customers' phone records without a warrant or court oversight,” Senator Wyden added.An AT&T spokesperson told 404 Media in an email, “For decades, we have been a trusted partner to provide reliable connectivity to federal agencies as well as state and local governments. We are required by law to provide information to government and law enforcement agencies when it is demanded under lawful order. We ensure that these requests are valid, and that our responses comply with the law.”After publication of this piece, AT&T provided a second statement: “The contract referenced is with the Department of Homeland Security to support law enforcement efforts to combat issues such as human trafficking, drug smuggling, and threats to critical infrastructure. This is not a contract supporting ICE activities, nor related to ‘surveillance’ as claimed in this inaccurate report. The program compensates AT&T for the cost of analyzing data that falls within the scope of a valid compulsory legal demand and providing the required information to law enforcement pursuant to a court order, search warrant, or subpoena. Like all carriers, AT&T is required by law to respond to valid legal demands, such as subpoenas and court orders. We ensure that these requests are valid, and that our responses comply with the law.”ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment, but previously told the Financial Times, “Nothing new here. For years law enforcement across the nation has leveraged technological innovation to fight crime. ICE is no different.”The precursor to Data Analytical Services was a program called Hemisphere. The New York Times first revealed Hemisphere in 2013, in which AT&T employees sat alongside Drug Enforcement Administration agents and supplied them with phone data going as far back as 1987. Authorities said they stopped federal funding for Hemisphere in September 2024 and shut the program down. But Data Analytical Services is essentially a continuation of that program. The document Senator Wyden’s office previously obtained says that Data Analytical Services was previously called Hemisphere.“Hemisphere is a surveillance program that refuses to die and keeps coming back with different names and different forms,” Soghoian added. “It is now clear that the Biden White House misled Congress when it said that Hemisphere had been shut down. The White House drug office funded program used by state and local law enforcement may be gone, but federal agencies are continuing to pay AT&T for the same services.”Update: this piece has been updated to include another statement from AT&T.

item.title: Yes, I want to pay for that
item.content:encoded: My last psychiatrist was terrible.Before every session, you fill out a form talking about how you’re feeling and so on as a way to evaluate whether or not your ADHD meds are working properly. For months, I’d invariably mention something about feeling pretty shitty about the political climate: ICE kidnapping people, trans folks having their very right to exist attacked, and so on.In our session, she’d ask me, without fail:But how does that affect personally?I’m a cishet white male with a strong social net. It doesn’t really affect me at all.But it affects me because I give a shit about other people, and want to see happy and successful and thriving, and holy shit what an absolutely awful question to ask someone.I see a similar conversation happen often around social services, like, “why should your taxes pay for…”Other people to go to college?Kids to eat for free at school?Free housing for a homeless person?Candy and junk food for someone on SNAP/food stamps?Someone less healthy than you to have surgery?Rehab for someone struggling with addiction?A vacation or fun experience for someone whose disabled and can’t work?Clothes for someone who can’t afford them?A toy or video game for a kid whose parents don’t work?The answer is simple: I give a shit about people.I don’t get why this is weird or confusing or controversial to anyone. I care about people, and I want to see everyone be happy and thrive.If you want to be a selfish asshole about it, we all do better when we all do better.A better educated population means a better chance of curing chronic illnesses, solving social challenges, and inventing cool new stuff.Kids who aren’t hungry learn better.People who have homes are more likely to work and less likely to use drugs or alcohol.Keeping someone alive means they can work and participate in society.Helping someone beat addiction means can work and participate in society.Keeping people clothed means they can leave the damn house, work, and participate in society.But like… I don’t give a shit if someone is “productive” or not.Everyone deserves joy and dignity and compassion, which is why I folks on SNAP or food stamps to be able to buy candy. I want poor people to experience rest and have vacations and for their kids to have toys and fun experiences.I give a shit about people.Isn’t it weird how people never ask this question about all of the awful things are taxes actually get used for right now, today? As a US citizen, my taxes are used to…Kidnap minorities and ship them to illegal labor prisons.Clutter space with internet satellites that fuck up astronomy.Poison the water, soil, and air with industrial waste.Rapidly accelerate planetary warming.I’d much rather some poor kid gets a hot meal or someone who will never work gets to eat a fucking Snickers bar than any of those things.Because I give a shit about people.If you’re upset at the idea that your tax money might prevent someone from dying but upset that your taxes are used to literally murder people, you’re the weirdo, not me.

item.title: Charting American Culture in News Footage of ‘Grand Theft Auto’
item.author: Matthew Gault
item.content:encoded: Some people spent the week leading up to the release of replaying the old games. I, sicko that I am, spent it watching TV news coverage of the franchise from the past 20 years.Grand Theft Auto has been a staple of cable and broadcast TV news since at least the release of in 2001. I’ve been an adult for all of it; I’ve had a front row seat for two decades of moral panics, parental freakouts, and bizarre political theater. The games and the broader culture’s reaction to them have changed dramatically in that time. In 2001, newscasters worried GTA III was training an army of young men to kill. In 2026, earnestly quoted Bell Hooks in its review of GTA VI.For mainstream news, GTA is the ur-video game. The open world that mirrors our own, the prevalence of sex and death, and the increasingly realistic simulations and graphics pointed towards the dream of what a video game could be. GTA is the American id made manifest.You can chart America’s changing culture — especially its anxieties — by watching how the media covered Grand Theft Auto. This was, at first, the game that critics of the medium had always warned us about: a violent sex and death simulator that rotted the brains of the youth just as rock and roll and comics had done in ages past. Twenty years on, the brains are thoroughly rotted, GTA won, and now? Now we’re all worried about money.GTA III and — Murder Simulators, the Assassin of YouthRockstar released in October 2001 and just a year later. The controversy around both started right away and centered around violence, and sometimes, the game’s depiction of women. “This is the world’s most popular video game [...] and millions of kids are mastering it by learning to slaughter bystanders,” Ted Koppel told America.Nightline devoted 20 minutes of its broadcast to GTA in July 2002. It interviewed children who grinned ear to ear as they gunned down people in GTA, their parents who insisted it was just a game, a concerned expert who was sure GTA was training them to kill, and a psychologist who said that was bullshit. It all ended with a roundtable discussion where a police officer, in uniform, explained the differences between video games and real world violence.Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — Congressional Hearings and Sex on TVI was an assistant manager of a Gamestop in Texas in 2004 when Rockstar released Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The level of parental concern in the store was high in the weeks leading up to its release. One mother was so upset by a bearing a cover story about that she told me I was going to hell for “selling a gangster lifestyle” to children.But it was sex, not violence, that the news focused on with . The game had a lot of simulation elements — its protagonist would gain weight if he ate too much — and Rockstar had experimented with a sex minigame called “hot coffee.” Developers cut the minigame from the final release, but it was still on the physical discs that went to stores. Modders uncovered it in the files and were able to patch it back in.California politician Leland Yee got wind of the mod and condemned the Entertainment Software Ratings Board (ESRB) for labeling the game “Mature” instead of “Adults Only.” Cable news went wild. Rachel Maddow weighed in. Hillary Clinton, then a Senator in New York, demanded an investigation. Congress voted to send the FTC after Rockstar for deceiving the ESRB. The ESRB updated the game’s rating to an AO. Walmart, Best Buy, and other retailers . publisher Take-Two shipped new copies with the content completely removed. Take-Two’s shareholders also removed most of its board and put Strauss Zelnick in charge. He’s been the CEO ever since.— The Ballad of Jack ThompsonThe cultural winds had shifted by the time hit stores in 2008. Retailers across the country had midnight release parties where people lined up to purchase the game as soon as possible. Local news outlets interviewed people in line and marveled at how much money might make.But the culture warriors still pointed to GTA as proof of America’s moral decline. Glenn Beck, then an anchor on CNN Headline News, on the game and often spoke to American lawyer Jack Thompson. Thompson hated Grand Theft Auto so much and was so sure it was training young people to kill their elders that he let his crusade against the franchise ruin his life.Thompson against Take-Two aimed at preventing the company from selling at all. The publisher counter-sued, Thompson accused it of perjury, and the parties eventually settled. In its ruling, the courts said Thompson could never use the legal system to stop Take-Two from publishing a game ever again.He didn’t stop though. After the game came out, Thompson Rockstar had based an assassination mission on him. He then sent a letter to Strauss Zelnick’s mom. “Your son, this very moment, is doing everything he possibly can to sell as many copies of GTA IV to teen boys in the United States, a country in which your son claims you raised him to be ‘a Boy Scout.’ More like the Hitler Youth, I would say. Happy Mother’s day, Mrs. Zelnick, which this year is May 11, two weeks after your son unleashes porn and violence upon other mothers’ boys. I'm sure you’re very proud,” Thompson wrote in the letter.The Supreme Court of Florida permanently disbarred him shortly thereafter.Money in the Age of ViolenceIn 2013, made a billion dollars in three days and was the biggest entertainment release of all time. It made more money than any movie, book, album, or video game had ever made before. Every news broadcast about the game led with that fact. “Never has there been an opening like this in the entertainment industry,” CBS News said.Jake Tapper and CNET’s Dan Ackerman lamented that GTA V’s success would hurt the creativity of the video game industry. “It’s become such a hit-driven business. You have to have a big opening day or opening weekend for anyone to take you seriously. And when you have such a hit-driven business, I think people get risk averse and they don’t get as creative,” Ackerman told Tapper. The news still ran segments about the violence and sex in the game, but it was typically couched in a conversation about its runaway financial success. Most anchors brought on experts who told them about the business. They sought to understand what was happening and why people liked the game, rather than condemning it outright. Anxieties of American DeclineIn 2026, cultural fears about violence and sex in video games are gone. Instead, we’re all worried about money. Everyone is sure will make money, the question is if it will make the money?“Why the stakes for GTA VI are so high,” declared the thumbnail for a Bloomberg video about the game. The outlet’s podcast also ran an episode about why the . Newsweek worried that the U.S. economy as people take time off work to play. CBS News’ morning show wondered how much money the game would make and the anchor admitted he once “lost a summer” to Grand Theft Auto. No one discussed violence at all. CNBC’s coverage called the game a “Billion Dollar Hype Machine.”Behind it all is a kind of lament — a worry that might be a final hurrah for this kind of game. Rumors are that it cost a billion dollars. Games are more expensive than ever and the industry has been devastated. A third of the industry lost their jobs in the past 24 months and most of them . Even when a game is successful, companies cut staff. wondered if GTA VI “may be the last great heist.”Underneath all these economic fears, the older panics still lurked. On Fox News, middling collegiate swimmer turned political activist Riley Gaines hoped that the game’s romantic elements would lead to a rise in birth rates. “Hopefully these men realize they like the feeling of love, romantic love, and go out and find it. Because, I’ll tell you what, we’re in a population decline. We need more babies. You can’t have babies, real babies, mouths to feed, from video games,” Gaines said.Twitch streamer Sasha Grey had early access to the game and was streaming it to YouTube and Twitch when YouTube shut down her stream for “nudity.” An early cutscene showed what Grey described as “artistic nip and some booty.” Grey complained to YouTube in a post on X and shared a screenshot of the moment the company shut down her stream. “They allow far worse under their educational category. This game is art, y’know? It’s the biggest release of the friggin’ decade,” Grey said during her stream. She pulled up the post on X to see if she’d gotten a response. “Oh god, the Twitter post got labeled as adult content, which means it’s going to be harder to get seen.”The old protestant advertiser-friendly anti-sex morality is still there, programmed into the computer systems we use every day.

item.title: Songs from the Second Floor (2000) ★★★★★
item.author: Jack Baty
item.content:encoded: I knew nothing about Roy Andersson before watching ‎Songs from the Second Floor (2000). Now he's my current favorite filmmaker. What a bleak, funny, original, totally unique world he's made here.

item.title: ICE List Confirms the Identities of 5,000 Immigration Agents
item.author: Andre Costa
item.content:encoded: ICE List has confirmed the identities of more than 5,000 immigration agents, more than double the roughly 2,200 on our public record on 28 October, the day a staff directory of the Department of Homeland Security was leaked.The leak, is available to the public via the transparency group DDoSecrets under the name Icepick, holds 41,191 records of DHS employees and contractors. A group calling itself the Department of Peace says it took them through the single sign-on service DHS buys from Okta. Okta says it has "no evidence our data or systems were compromised". DHS said it was "aware of a potential breach".A name in the leak does not get anyone onto ICE List. The leak tells us where to look, and a page goes up only when we can tie the name to an agent through a source outside it, such as a court filing, an official record or press reporting. About 2,270 of the named agents on the record are documented in court filings, most of them filed by the government itself.Crucially, a number of the people named in the leak no longer work at ICE, and some have retired. The directory covers the whole department, with 21,329 records from Customs and Border Protection and 6,598 from ICE, and it is a list of accounts, which is a different thing from a list of the people making arrests today. Those who have moved on from the agency show the crucial need for a steady hand with information like this. The ICE List is targeted at the Trump regime's transformation of ICE and Border Patrol, and many of those who left as soon as Trump took charge may indeed oppose the tactics that are now commonplace. For now we are working only through the field agents. We will go through the remaining names afterwards to see whether any have joined ICE or CBP since.More than 20 of the names we have confirmed were searched for on our site from DHS and ICE work computers. Our logs record the network a search comes from and cannot show who typed it. They do show that somebody inside the department went looking for those names on ICE List before we had published them. DHS's own network sent more than 10,000 requests to the site in the two weeks to 29 October.We do not publish home addresses, phone numbers or email addresses. This is a common claim by opponents of our project, and indeed, by the US government itself. As confirmed by multiple investigations, no addresses appear on the ICE List. ICE agents make arrests in masks, in plain clothes and from unmarked cars, and the Trump regime refuses to name them even after they have shot someone. DHS says naming agents puts them and their families in danger. The agents on this record are public officials using the powers of the state in public, and in most cases the government has already named them in a courtroom.Every page lists its sources. Anyone who believes they have been named in error can contact us and we will check the record against the evidence. Footage, documents and names can be sent to the same place.ICE Watch, the app the public uses to send footage, photos and plate numbers to ICE List, is now in testing on Google Play. Join the test to install it on your phone.ICE List and Crust News are paid for by readers. Subscribe to get our reporting by email, or donate to keep the record growing.

item.title: Trifect Up Beyond Repair
item.author: Dave Pell
item.source: NextDraft: The Day's Most Fascinating News
item.content:encoded: My first thought upon watching the Trump/Xi/Putin dictators-in-triplicate fest was that it’s too bad the air travel ground stop didn’t last another week. Trump’s international trips are like an endless Matryoshka doll, with each subsequent international humiliation being worse than the last. And this one was that, times three. The axis of evil has been replaced by the dictatorial triple threat, and the American president is an enthusiastic member of the troika. The whole style over substance affair could, I suppose, be viewed as a win, win, win. Xi got to look like the host with the most leader of the world. Putin, a murderous mafia boss of a semi-failed state, got images that make him look like he’s on equal footing with the world’s superpowers. And Trump got to fawn over his frenemies, in addition to bringing his traveling one-man slumber party to an international audience. I don’t blame him for being tired. Betrayal is more exhausting than it looks. Never judge a man until you’ve walked a mile on his bone spurs. Sadly, with all that winning, no one was at the summit to represent American interests. The land of the free was replaced by the land of the three. Oh well, you win some you threesome. I’d like to be more positive, but you can’t polish a third.+ Here’s the excellent Anne Applebaum with a look at some of the trilateral collateral. “Its true purpose was not to end any wars—and certainly not to end Russia’s bloody invasion of Ukraine—but to produce propaganda photographs and video clips that each of the three leaders will now use to mask their political failures. Certainly this was President Trump’s main goal. Before the three leaders met, he actually told Fox News that the most significant moment was already over: ‘the greeting yesterday, which in the history of China has never happened.’ Xi Jinping, aware of how easy it is to manipulate the American president, had met Trump at his airplane, on the tarmac … For Vladimir Putin, the meeting also created useful propaganda. Now almost five years into a war he believed he would win in three days, he is coping with 1.5 million war casualties; the loss, as of this week, of half of his country’s oil-refining capacity; and even, in the past few days, the destruction of the Kerch Strait Bridge, which links Russia to Crimea … Nevertheless, Putin will use the Shenzhen meeting to tell Russians that their country is still a superpower, still allowed to sit in the same room as the Americans and the Chinese … For Xi, the meeting was useful because he was the host, he set up the photographs, and his propaganda was broadcast around the world. With Trump’s cooperation, he telegraphed American decline, Chinese power, and Russian subservience.” Trump’s Embarrassing, Inconsequential Summit.+ “Mr. Trump, who has spoken for years with admiration about both autocrats, gushed about being welcomed by the two men. ‘We are really making history,’ he said at their meeting.” (Nothing has gone down in history quite as fast as America’s international leadership role under Trump.) (Gift Article): Behind Trump Meeting, Xi and Putin Share a Vision of Usurping U.S. Power.+ It really was all worse than I’m making it sound. Especially the sick love Trump showed for Putin, his “friend” with whom he has a “great relationship.” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk responded with this: “God, protect us from such friends.”One of the more anticipated IPOs in years has finally taken place as Anthropic hit the public markets. The stock initially soared well above its offering price, but then Claude thawed, and it has since settled into more traditional, solid first-day performance. The rest of the market suffered another rough day. Here’s the latest: Anthropic Shares Climb After Multibillion-Dollar I.P.O. “Anthropic has become by far the most valuable company on the stock market with the legal designation of a public benefit corporation, or P.B.C. That status requires Anthropic to prioritize its corporate mission — to develop safe artificial intelligence systems ‘for the long-term benefit of humanity.'” (If, you know, humanity survives the long term.)At the risk of bringing back memories of the great toilet paper rush of 2020, I should let you know that the tech outages of the past week have driven some panic buying at Costco and Walmart. Generators are a big hit, as is general pantry loading. (But if the internet goes down, is there still a point in living?) The prepper crowd is way ahead of the rest of us. But the rest of us are starting to join the prepper crowd. “Once written off as paranoid fantasy, and largely the domain of those with conservative and libertarian views, prepping itself has rapidly joined the mainstream and, in some quarters, has taken on a liberal bent: Rather than hiding away alone, armed to the teeth, there is an emphasis on building resilience and connections among people.” (Gift Article): They’re Prepping for a Broken Digital World. “DoorDash is not an emergency plan.” (Of course not. You need to back it up with UberEats and GrubHub.)+ “We believe many of the major disruptions of the last few weeks, including outages across major enterprises and governments, were partially due to unintended consequences of patching and configuration changes, as IT teams simply cannot patch these vulnerabilities fast enough without compromising their production environments. The second effect is the rise of AI-assisted cyberattacks. Bad actors are using open-weight models and new agentic frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed and scale.” Palo Alto Networks CEO just dropped a truth bomb on the network outages.+ As I explained yesterday, while it looks like our computers weren’t hacked, the events of the last week made it plainly clear that have been.While some of us are stocking up on toilet paper, others still don’t have access to toilets. And it just happens to be World Toilet Day, a funny idea with a serious goal. “The U.N. has stated that access to safe sanitation is a human right. And in just about every country, progress has been made in improving access to sanitary facilities. Since 2015, 1.2 billion people have become part of the world of safely managed sanitation systems.” And from Chris Mims in the (Gift Article): I Tried New York City’s New High-Tech Public Bathrooms—and Saw the Future. “On a day-long tour of New York City’s new, high-tech public bathrooms this week, I found them remarkably tidy—as did the many New Yorkers whom I cornered both before and after they used them.” (Being immediately confronted by a reporter after using a public restroom sounds like something out of an IBS nightmare.)Iowa Chu Talking About, Willis? “The U.S. Army’s plan to detonate about 5 tons of bomb-making chemicals that have become unstable and might explode if moved has some Iowa residents worried that a cloud of lead dust could cause environmental contamination and health problems. The detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is set for Friday, and officials recommend that some residents in nearby Middletown vacate the area. If they can’t leave their homes, they should stay inside and keep windows and doors closed.” (Even though they also warn that the blast could break some windows.) Iowans brace for a lead dust cloud as Army plans to detonate 5 tons of bomb-making chemicals.+ Turn Your Head and Witkoff: “SEC filings reveal that the president’s son-in-law is negotiating for peace while profiting from war.” Jared Kushner’s Undisclosed Investment. (In fairness, I don’t think Jared has an official government role.)+ What the Heil is He Talking About? (Robot voice) Attention plebeians and other human life forms, I am not MAGA and was never really MAGA. Please save this data to your hard drive. Elon Musk claims ‘I’m not MAGA‘ and says he regrets vast sums to back Republicans. (Well, I believe the second part…)+ After a year during which her megahit Choosin’ Texas dominated the charts, “Ella Langley set a new, all-time record for the most CMA Awards wins in one night on Wednesday.” But my favorite milestone of the night was achieved by NextDraft-approved artist Stephen Wilson Jr, who won best new artist at the age of 47. Here’s his CMA performance with Chris Stapleton. A decade ago, he was a scientist shepherding the creation of a digestible dental-cleaning chew for dogs. Years after leaving that gig for a full-time music career, he burst onto the scene in 2024 with this viral cover of Stand by Me.

item.title: Time Wharp
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: Today we’re listening to Time Wharp, an American multi-instrumentalist from Atlanta. The project is by Kaye Loggins, now based in Brooklyn. She played in bands in high school – punk, ska, metal, and “Myspace comedy techno” as she told Into. Terry Riley and the compilation pointed her towards ambient and experimental music. Her solo work as Time Wharp reflects her individual vision and unique collection of happenstance influences. Her album was released in 2022 on Leaving Records, manifesting the label’s “all-genre” ethos. There are elements of minimalism, jazz, leftfield electronic… First, though, we’re playing Radical American Hippy Kraut, whose “Blues 4 dANA” ended our neo-krautrock mix this week. It’s a collaboration with New York’s Charley Lanning aka CH Rom.
