item.content:encoded: i did about monster porn, probably because i’m a perverted freak who reads too many of them. read it, it’s funny and most likely offensive; i was really on one when answering those questions. that said, the most fucked up thing about this interview is that alexander skarsgard didn’t come find me to talk about it, which i kinda thought he might.in the article i reference a shapeshifting gay whale sex novel that i would love to tell michelle obama about, and it’s actually from the ORCA (Organization for the Return of Criminals and Assets) i’m currently in the middle of reading. an orca shifter art thief turned bounty hunter banging a sea otter shifter hacker who might have pissed off the wrong people! an orca shifter former mercenary who hates taking orders banging a great white shark shifter who’d rather work solo! an orca shifter art forger who isn’t keen on field work banging a chameleon shifter with a lucrative secret talent! an orca shifter financier who had no idea he liked kids (ed: as in parenting) banging a panda shifter hellbent on making sure his family’s legacy doesn’t end with him!i also just started reading this fucking banger called (not a pun, unfortunately) by aimee nicole walker which combines two of my favorite things to read: gay sex and solving murders. gay romance crime novels are a recent discovery and i think i’m going to pivot away from minotaur boning for a minute to read some sexy thrillers, because i to be thrilled. i just got the whole series. and look at this other one, . first of all, incredible title. no mistaking what this book could possibly be about. second, is that paul walker on the cover? third, an ex-cop in french prison falls in forbidden love with his parole officer and then his son gets kidnapped??? seven hundred pages of some (complimentary), add to cart.it’s getting cooler out, which means it’s time for my skinny, ugly dog to start wearing his sweaters. for me, the only reason to continue to let this dog live in my home is because he lets me put clothes on him. i get a lot of his cutest sweaters from , including several i just bought because they’re marked way down and i don’t believe in paying full price for a garment this dummy is eventually going to piss on. he also has some from this place furb, and he would look fresh as hell in or or , but those aren’t on sale yet so too bad for him. i don’t believe in giving abe too many nice things ( is what we feed him, you think he deserves designer fashions?) but i might need someone to come and physically restrain me from ordering from found my animal. i keep telling myself the jingling bells will grate on my nerves but my resistance is faltering!my old, tired knee has been bothering me for weeks but i won’t go to the doctor because the last time i went, with an actual bullet lodged in my skull, my liquefied brain oozing out of my eye sockets, he stabbed me with a zepbound needle and told me to get the hell out, then tried to bill my expired writer’s guild insurance $9,000,000 for the pleasure. desperation pushed me to the point of believing that a tube of cream from walgreens might put a dent in degenerating joint pain, especially since if i so much as look at an advil my butthole turns into carrie’s blood bucket, and tylenol is as useless to me as a flintstone vitamin. what is the exact age where medical professionals start to give you the drugs you’ve never heard of that actually fix shit?*topical analgesics taste test: my girl cara’s mom hipped me to this stuff like fifteen years ago and includes “alternative botanical and biologic formulations that are natural and safe” which is against my religion. but i tried it anyway, and it has zero scent (important) plus it works. works-. (creme) bought this in maine because i fucked my shit up on a whale boat. doesn’t stink, works! (gel) has an NSAID and has all the same warnings and side effects as advil but with worse results. (lidocaine) didn’t work great, but i appreciated that you can roll it on and don’t have to get sticky ass medicine all over your hands. works pretty good, i guess? but the smell is . straight up . it made my sinuses hurt, was so strong and bad that i ended up trying to wash it off, then i had to wash the pants i was wearing the blanket i was using when i had it on. too, too much. menthol and camphor, but less bad than the advil. it’s much closer in scent profile to the vicks you rub on your chest when you have a cough, which is kind of comforting and nostalgic, but it doesn’t work well enough to justify walking around with you whole body smelling like that. stinky #3, but more of an herbal stinkyness, which i prefer. it’s so/so as a pain reliever but since it’s oily it makes your skin soft, and that’s something! this came from the health food store, so…………..you feel me. it doesn’t stink, though, and it gets hot as you rub it in and move around, which is a nice sensation but not exactly pain relief. this stuff actually smells pretty decent, and the doctor at urgent care asked me no fewer than ten times if i’d tried it, so it must do .*update: i went to the doctor after i first wrote this and the answer is “when you are about to turn forty-seven.” i finally aged out of the just put some ice on it years and got a course of corticosteroids plus the good shit they give your grandma, god bless. do any orthopedists read this lowbrow shit? please give me your beeper number! okay, i’m about to but you understand in advance that i don’t really know what i’m doing on there, so if i suck at it or it’s secretly evil don’t tell me. it’s called rec league and it’s for “sharing what you love” which, after memes, is the entire reason i even go on the internet. there’s some kind of money element, but i haven’t paid any money nor do i make any, so i have not investigated it further. maybe people get paid to recommend shit? i don’t, so i don’t care. anyway it’s early stages, but my strategy so far has been to occasionally post shit i like without much context and follow back everyone who follows me because reading lists of what people are into is extremely my shit.here is mine: and i will see you over there if you join itmy lady and i are empty nesters because we now have two kids in college, and that is insane. the old kid is studying art, which…………..i have to bite my african-american tongue before i say something that gets my ass in trouble. first of all, as a man, why do you think you should be allowed to create beauty? and, more important than that, shouldn’t you be learning how to fix my car?!!?! homie came over the other night trying to show me a drawing he made and i’m sitting there like “instead of that, could you go rewire the light fixture in the dining room that flickers?” you know what i want to see, playboy? this HVAC system tuned up before it snows! me raising a man is so stupid and funny because on the one hand, all i do is bitch at him about how great women are and how lucky he is to share a planet with us, but on the other? go pick that thing up, brother. then carry that other thing over here, and hurry up. i’m not moving a table? “mow” the “grass???” i wish i fucking would. also i can say “man” officially now, because dude just turned twenty-fucking-one, which is nuts because i’m only nineteen, so how can i have a son who’s older than i am???empty nesting is crazy because wow am i annoying!! like, i for sure irritate myself, but it’s become clear that i bother my lady, especially since she no longer has lunches to pack or homework to check or whatever the hell else you do as a parent that distracts you from noticing all the weird shit your partner is doing. watch the kids brush their teeth to make sure they get the back ones? search the pockets of their dirty jeans for vapes? all i know is that the one thing she doing was having the time to register all the foolishness i get up to, and she’s just now having the awful realization that she’s spent the last ten years of her life married to an insane clown. television roundup!!we finished watching the americans a couple weeks ago and where is my trophy for being correct in . this bitch was tripping right up until the last few minutes of the series and i am thrilled to be rid of her. is incredible as usual this season, and i straight up sobbed at the end of the last episode. is still a gloriously violent fever dream, although i’m ready for them to kill off [REDACTED] and [REDACTED], they are getting on my nerves. , hilarious. is so! freaking! good!! dominic west really loves playing a guy who fucked around on his wife, huh? anyway, sienna miller has a perfect face. i haven’t finished season four of yet but hot damn what a way to start the season??? i did see that shit coming, also i love how tired keri russell looks all the time. is a fucking banger, put linda cardellini in everything, and it hasn’t gotten too scary yet (i’m not done) but the gore is magnificent. you might throw up. somehow the second season of is even better than the first? betty gilpin!! TOMMY LEE JONES!!!!! is a real slow burn but i’m into it. is finally on netflix and yes, i have seen every episode at least a dozen times, but that’s not going to stop me from watching them all again. i think i’m gonna watch that new show because i miss peter krause on the greatest show ever made, , and while i’ve got peacock open: are we watching ? i fuck with rose byrne heavy because of damages and spy, i should just dive in and see where it takes me. i’m very excited about (this is a mike epps supremacy household) because i just love him so much, and his youtube series coulda been daddy is one of the most hilarious things i’ve ever watched??? the couples therapy episode is gold from start to finish, but you should start at the beginning. the baby is the best actor i have ever seen in my life. is a bootleg version of the times’ domino game and i am obsessed with it, it’s fun as hell and i play it whenever i can’t put my phone down but am tired of instagram.love you, big kiss, email my agent if you know somebody who can fix a fat knee.sam!!

item.title: What Happens to Your Body When You Die?
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Kurzgesagt explores what happens to your body when you die.Death isn’t a single switch that shuts down your entire body at once. When your heart stops beating and your brain goes silent, trillions of cells inside you are still alive, desperately trying to keep themselves running. Death isn’t a single moment, but a slow and surprisingly complex process that can last for weeks.What actually happens when you die? What makes death so mysterious, and which cells are the last survivors within your body?

item.title: Bringing the Largest Public ICE Database to Your Phone
item.author: Dominick Skinner
item.content:encoded: After months of rejections, the ICE Watch app has been accepted onto the Google Play store, and we can now invite testers to join and help get the app approved for a full release. Many people will not want to install the app through the store, and the .apk install is still available at its old location. The Play Store will not replace the third party routes.We will pursue an iPhone version as soon as the app passes through the testing period on Android.ICE Watch is the app that lets the public contribute to The ICE List. It has had limited use so far because we could not get it approved for the official Android app store.On November 13, a US federal judge issued a permanent injunction barring the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security from pressuring Apple and Meta to suppress platforms used to monitor ICE activity. That injunction is the reason we chose now to resubmit the app to the Play Store, and may be the reason it was accepted.Google puts a new app through a closed test before it can go onto the store for everyone. A set of testers has to install it and keep it for two weeks before anyone else can. We need those testers now.The app has been in use for five months, so this is early access more than a test.With the app you can swipe through documented ICE operations and the agents nobody has named yet, Tinder-style, and help identify the agents we have not been able to.The full ICE List is in the app too. Browse by state, and send footage or a tip from your phone in seconds. Share a video from your gallery straight to us. Nothing you send appears publicly until a person has reviewed it, and tips are anonymous.We made one serious change for the Google Play version: logins are gone. Anyone who installs from the Play Store gets an anonymous ID. This makes no real difference to most users, but the groups who work alongside us have been asked to install from the F-Droid store or the .apk file instead.If you want to help test it, leave the email of a Google account on your phone at blog.theicelist.org/testers. We will send you a link to install the app. Keep it for three weeks, use it as you would anyway, and tell us what, if anything, breaks at icelist@crustnews.com.If you use an iPhone, you do not have to wait for the iOS app. Open watch.theicelist.org in Safari, tap the Share button at the bottom of the screen, then tap Add to Home Screen. ICE Watch then opens from your home screen like any other app, full screen, and you can send footage and tips from it the same way.The ICE List takes no advertising and no institutional money. It is funded by the public. If you want to help this project grow, please consider supporting it here.

item.title: datasette-arrows 0.1a0
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Datasette 1.0a43 added the ability for plugins to implement streaming export formats. Datasette core supports streaming CSV and TSV - you can export millions of lines of data from a table without needing to load it all into memory, because those two file formats support streaming data in chunks. The register_output_renderer() plugin hook can now be used to implement the same pattern for other formats.I've learned never to release a new plugin feature without accompanying it with a plugin that uses it.Claude Fable 5.2 suggested the Apache Arrow streaming format as a good option, and built this plugin in almost a single shot.Add the plugin to Datasette (datasette install datasette-arrows) and the export dialog gains this new Arrow option:This screenshot is from Datasette's branch - the most recent release doesn't yet group streaming formats such as Arrow with the TSV and CSV in the "All rows in this table" section, but that's coming in the next alpha release.

item.title: A Peek at What We Still Don’t Know About the Worst of Trump II … So Far
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: Trump Sicced the IRS on ProtestersI hinted in yesterday’s Unsanctioned that one of the major benefits of Congress reviving its oversight powers under new Democratic majorities will be to provide a fuller accounting of what’s already happened in the first two years of Trump II.As bad as it’s been on the retribution, corruption, and destruction fronts, we only know a fraction of what’s really gone down. Vigorous congressional oversight — absent under the GOP majorities — promises to gives us a clearer picture of the worst of the Trump II depredations, like the mass deportation operation, and uncover wrongdoing we don’t even know about yet.We get a new peek today at what that might look like in a NYT story that shows the IRS directly involved in targeting left-wing political groups in the aftermath of the assassination of Charlie Kirk. The IRS “initiated at least four criminal investigations” into as-yet-unidentified left-wing groups, according to a portion of an internal memo obtained by the NYT.“The memo describes the work done by a group of a dozen I.R.S. officials detailed to a task force formed in response to Mr. Kirk’s death on Sept. 10, 2025,” the NYT reports.As TPM’s Josh Kovensky has reported at length, while the Trump administration ostentatiously turned Kirk’s death into a national day of mourning, it also seized on the assassination as a pretext to criminalize dissent, invent a left-wing terrorism threat that it falsely claimed had international connections, and scrutinize left-wing political and advocacy groups in an effort to intimidate and cow protests.In the two weeks after Kirk’s death, President Trump designated Antifa as a terrorist organization and signed National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 (NSPM-7). In NSPM-7, Trump ordered the IRS commissioner “to ensure that no tax-exempt entities are directly or indirectly financing political violence or domestic terrorism” and to refer such organizations and their officers and employees to the DOJ for investigation and prosecution.“The memo viewed by The Times is the first window into the work the I.R.S. has actually undertaken to carry out the demands from the White House,” according to the story.In March of this year, the IRS criminal investigations branch began working with the the task force that was operating out of the FBI headquarters, according to the NYT story. The memo covers work done between March and July. The NYT said it reviewed the first six pages of the eight-page memo. The last two pages, which the newspaper did not see, apparently identified the four targeted groups.The protests at Delany Hall, the immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey, have been a particular focus of the task force:I.R.S. officials reviewed financial information, including subpoenaed Venmo records, about people arrested during those protests, as well as businesses that the officials believed could be funding them. At one point, I.R.S. officials used facial recognition and tattoo analysis databases to help identify individuals, the memo said.A quick summary of some of the memo’s highlights, as reported by the NYT:In addition to the Delaney Hall protests, the IRS also assisted in the response to the April shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner, the May shooting at a mosque in San Diego, and the June UFC event on the White House lawn. It’s not clear from the memo what role the IRS had in the UFC event (five men were charged with allegedly plotting to attack the event).At least four tax-exempt groups were referred to the civil side of the agency, which conducts audits;IRS officials have been assigned to nine grand juries.The memo is just a glimpse into one discrete operation during one window of time this year, and it alone can’t really provide a clear picture of the scale and scope of the effort to turn political opposition to the Trump administration into criminal conduct. That’s one area where a Democratic Congress could bring new facts to light and begin to back the Trump administration off from its worst excesses.President Trump brought an ignominious end to the political career of Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX) by endorsing the scoundrel Ken Paxton and costing Texas a Senate seat — and now it’s having knock-on effects in the final weeks before Cornyn leaves office.Cornyn appears to be very much on board with having Ohio native T. Elliot Gaiser — the head of the Trump DOJ’s Office of Legal Counsel — installed as a federal judge in Texas, where he has few personal or professional connections.A coveted federal judgeship going to a non-Texan while bypassing the home state senators’ approved list of potential nominees would be a tough ask by any president under any circumstance (unless you’re Ted Cruz, I guess). But under these circumstances, it’s a lot to expect Cornyn to roll over after getting royally screwed:Cornyn’s remarks came as Bloomberg reported that last year, early in his tenure at OLC, Gaiser pitched a memo that proposed reviving the 1873 Comstock Act to criminalize the transportation of abortion drugs and related medical supplies.Then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche rejected Gaiser’s pitch, according to Bloomberg’s sources: “Blanche pushed back by directing him to table the issue due to his worry that Gaiser’s position would amount to a federal abortion ban — an issue the administration had avoided wading into before the midterms …”In an unusual move, Gaiser contacted Bloomberg directly after it published its story and denied it. “Your story is categorically false, period,” Gaiser said. “I did not push for any nationwide abortion ban.”Where Have You Found AI Most Useful?I ask this question with some trepidation. For a number of reasons, I have been slow to take affirmative steps to incorporate AI into my personal and professional lives.I haven’t activated AI on my Apple devices or integrated it into Google yet. I’ve played around with Claude for maybe two hours over the past six months, and I used Gemini to create a couple of satirical images to make a friend laugh (with mixed results). I’ve not touched ChatGPT, and I haven’t used any of the new personal AI agents like Muse.But I am curious about AI’s utility and how you’re incorporating it as a tool in your lives and work. I’m also pretty leery of the privacy risks involved — so I’d be interested in hearing where you’re drawing the line on entrusting AI tools with personal or sensitive information.At this point, I should acknowledge that AI is a dreadfully imprecise term so let me refine what I mean for the purposes of this question. If you’re scientist, engineer, developer, or otherwise use AI at a high technical level, I’m probably not looking for for feedback from you. But even that can be a fuzzy line to draw. For example, a friend who is not a professional coder used AI to code a draftboard for his fantasy baseball team. So the newest AI tools may put some of what we used to think of as technical work within reach of a layperson. Obviously the AI I’m talking about here is a far cry from the frontier work on artificial general intelligence. You get the idea.Let me try to preempt the emails warning me about the evils of AI or how you’re not using it and will never use it. I get you. My own slow adoption of AI is partly because it gives me pause, too. This has been a new frontier of consumer tech that I’ve been content not to be on the cutting edge of. But it’s pervasiveness at what I’ll call the retail level — quite apart from its role in research and development, core science, and other technical applications — has me prepared to adapt … possibly.Thanks in advance for your feedback. My contact information is immediately below.

item.title: Broken World
item.author: Jason Koebler
item.content:encoded: Very chonky newsletter today as we have published quite a lot over the last 24 hours. Today we look into why everything is busted and have an extremely wild story about how people are using their AI agents. A few hours ago, I went to rent a Lime bike to ride the ten minutes to my therapy appointment. I opened Lime, scanned the QR code, and double clicked my iPhone’s side button to authorize Apple Pay. The app hung for a few moments, then closed. I tried several more times and the same thing happened. In the back of my mind, I wondered what was going on — was the Lime bike broken? Was my cell phone service out? Was it something else? I opened the Uber app and, similarly, wasn’t able to pay. I opened DownDetector and realized that the entirety of Apple Pay, a thing I thought existed only on my phone and not the cloud, was down. I texted my therapist, put my phone in my pocket, and started jogging. Not being able to rent a Lime Bike for several minutes is an extremely minor inconvenience barely worth mentioning. And yet the mental gymnastics my brain did in those few minutes — what’s broken, why is it broken, how is it broken — is something that everyone I know have been repeatedly doing for the last few weeks as seemingly every service and system crashes down around us. Over the weekend, people who I do not normally talk to about my job asked me: What is going on with the airplanes? Why is my bank down? What about Microsoft? The default assumption that many people are making is that these are either being caused by cyberattacks and/or “AI” broadly defined, whether that’s AI gone haywire, “rogue” AI agents, or something else, which is indicative of just how fearful people are of AI. What I have been telling people is, basically, that shit is broken and things are going to keep breaking. For lots of different reasons. It’s often not a hack and it’s often not explicitly AI-related, but everything now sort of looks like that XKCD comic of the dependency domino tower. While not exactly true that AI and cyberattacks are causing these outages, it’s also not entirely wrong, either. What we’re seeing is — I think — a series of infrastructure failures (and some cyberattacks) that are not directly connected but are broadly a symptom of the same general trends and systemic problems we’ve seen across society, the government, and the tech sector over the last several years. First, it’s worth mentioning that anytime there’s a string of outages, there’s a tendency to tie them altogether. And outages or hacks that previously wouldn’t have been noted at all suddenly get more attention and become part of the narrative. Take, for example, the fact that the International Ice Hockey Federation has been targeted by a cyberattack; you probably would not normally hear about this but it has suddenly become part of the broader story. The simplest explanation I can come up with for the broader disastrous trend we’ve seen is that since the pandemic we have seen: mass layoffs of tech workers and software developers mass deployment of AI-assisted and vibe coded products, software updates, and patchesmass layoffs in the government sector and outright destruction of government expertise and oversightthe loss of institutional knowledge associated with those layoffs and funding cutsa failure to invest in upgrading infrastructure/redundancygovernment contracts handed out to the President’s friends and political alliesAI and LLM-assisted/iterative exploit discovery, coding, and deploymentcompanies responding to the AI hacking threat with AI-coded and rushed patchesWhen Elon Musk took over Twitter and named it X, there were many people who thought his layoffs and the associated loss of expertise would result in the site failing basically because of an infrastructural failure. Twitter would basically “go down” because someone would break something and no one would know how to fix it. We haven’t really seen that happen to X, but that same philosophy of firing the experts and YOLOing AI into everything while hoping shit doesn’t break is now the explicit strategy of our entire economy and our entire government. This segment is a paid ad. If you’re interested in advertising, Use code 404MEDIA A man and his Muse sue MetaA little over a week ago, Meta suspended the Facebook pages belonging to Joe Thomas, the owner of South Carolina-based Kong Koatings Epoxy Countertops. For the last few months, Thomas’ Muse agent Baby Mia (which is named after his granddaughter) has run different parts of his business, which includes making and posting AI-generated videos on several of his company’s Facebook pages. The videos feature, for example, AI versions of Thomas and his wife pouring epoxy on a floor and their feet. After Thomas gave the AI agent access to his Facebook pages, Meta’s content moderation disabled the accounts because it suspected that the agent itself was a hacker. Because Thomas does all of his business’s marketing through Facebook ads, he says his inbound leads stopped while his accounts were disabled.“I use AI for everything I do. All my emails, she runs my business. I’ve used it so much, Mia is very intelligent,” Thomas told me on the phone. “Meta shut my accounts down because they detected my AI, shut my accounts down for a week. I was pretty pissed off. She jumped right up and set up emails to Congressmen, Senator Tim Scott. She filed the whole lawsuit herself. I’ve done nothing in this case, I’ve let her handle the whole case […] she sent a fax out to Trump’s office.”The lawsuit claims Thomas lost at least $25,000 worth of work while his page was down but is seeking $75,000 in damages. The lawsuit was filed in Oconee County Court in South Carolina on Monday, according to a copy of the lawsuit I obtained from the court. Yes, it is a real lawsuit, although it obviously may not be successful. See more of my extremely bizarre trip down this rabbit hole here.On the podcast this week, Joseph talks about his investigation into OnlyFakes, the AI-powered fake ID service. And part two of the podcast features my call with Joe Thomas, who is using his Muse agent to sue the company that made it. A new Gallup poll shows that 33 percent of young people they polled between the ages of 15 and 22 have an AI companion.A reminder that we have new merch in stock. 404 ‘Doom Code’ short sleeve t-shirts and trucker hats. We’ve heard from some of you about wanting new designs/different cuts, etc. Promise we are doing a bigger refresh of our merch store as soon as we possibly can. Just waiting on designs and trying to manage how we do fulfillment. Our friends over at Hell Gate are doing a sale. Get 25 percent off an annual subscription a t-shirt. We share notes on running a business with Hell Gate all the time and they’ve become some of our closest friends in the biz, so check them out, especially if you live in NYC. Even as someone who lives across the country, I find my subscription to be easily worth it.The first reviews of are out and people are pretty unanimously saying it’s a masterpiece. This is, obviously, the video game event of … the decade? The millennium so far? I have not played any of them since GTA II so I will abstain from embarrassing myself further, but I trust Jason Schreier and he says it’s very good and possibly tech populist in vibe.BugMeNot, a website where people shared logins to sites that shouldn’t have had logins, has suddenly disappeared without explanation after roughly two decades online. Bummer. Voyager I is now one light day away from Earth. TIL that Voyager I launched a week Voyager 2 and Voyager 2 will not be a light day away from Earth for another decade. Space.com has a good writeup of why this is the case.

item.title: The Dictator Thing
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump’s giddiness around dictators is one of the abiding themes of his two presidencies. You can see it now in the eagerness with which he’s anticipated his summit/meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Indeed, in the last two days Trump’s been casting about for the possibility of adding Kim Jong Un to the trio. These are quite simply the men he admires the most because they embody his actual vision of what a leader should be. It’s easy to get the sense in these meetings that Vladimir Putin heads one of the world’s three great powers. But that simply isn’t the case. Russia is a comparatively minor economy. It has a lot of oil and gas. It has nuclear weapons, really the only thing that makes it a major player on the world stage. As a conventional military power it’s struggled for years to subdue even Ukraine. The U.S. and China are great powers, with mammoth economies vast enough to sustain huge militaries. Russia is really only in this group because it has become what amounts to a junior associate of China and because of Donald Trump’s fixation on it as a kind of model power. In a way, Trump’s eagerness to add Kim Jong Un to the group underlines why Russia is there in the first place.

item.title: What the fuck is on Dear Leader’s head?
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Seriously, what in the actual fuck?The Donny we all saw heading for Bribe Force One yesterday morning was the one we’re all familiar with: the belligerent racist moron with the rat’s nest of yellow piss-mop hair atop his big, dumb pumpkin head.Sure, because nothing says ‘I’m a dignified world leader’ more than wrapping one’s misshapen body in a cheap misshapen suit, gazing at the world through dull, vacant eyes, standing like a toddler who just planted a fresh load into its pull-ups, and spastically waving two child-size flags held in two child-sized fists.And, of course, the shit-emoji hair.Who thought this was a good idea? Let me guess. It was the bunny-boiling diaper nurse. Looking up from the notebook where she’d devoted the last two hours to scrawling over and over and over, she said, ‘Sir! Sir! I know how we can make you even more handsome! Sir!’, and pulled a tube of Grecian Formula out of her diaper bag.It happened because there are no adults left in the room. With the last responsible human being, Susie Wiles, banished to that big farm upstate where she now has lots of room to run around, it’s just Donny, the diaper nurse and and Acting President Nosferatu McGoebbels — and he could give a fuck what Donny and Natty get up to, as long as they leave him alone to actually run the country.So that’s why, while the entire world goes to shit all around us, and, one by one, the online services we’ve come to depend on go , the topic of the day aboard Bribe Force One was Natty going, ‘you know what be cool? Let’s do you up like a poopsicle.’“It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and have all the money, things like that happen — it’s fine.”I’m sorry, but what the fuck kind of answer is ? No, it’s not fine. It’s only if you’re a privileged moron who lives in a pampered bubble, has all his needs taken care of for him, and jets around in a vulgar flying bordello that some emirs bribed him with.Let’s do this. Let’s imagine it’s 2023, and Joe Biden is president. Let’s say all the planes are grounded, you can’t get into your email, and your online banking app won’t work. Now let’s imagine that Biden, brown crap smeared all over his head, shows up goes, Do you think the worthless scribblers of the corporate-controlled press would have accepted that answer, and just gone ‘well I guess it’s fine, if Joe says so’?Absolutely not. They would have roasted Biden alive. Now imagine that Biden had pulled out a couple of flags and started waving them around like a meth-tweaked mental patient. Jake Tapper would have personally taken it upon himself to burn the White House to the ground.Meanwhile, back on Planet Earth, the Senate was holding a confirmation hearing for Acting Navy Secretary, Hung Cao. But let me back up a bit, and fill you in on how Hung Cao came to be our acting head of the Navy.“It’s really an honor to be with you,” Trump said with Cao to his right. “Thank you. And we’re gonna be with this man. This is a great gentleman. I love his name — Hung Cao. I love that name. And that name alone should get you elected, right?”Spoiler alert: Hung Cao’s name get him elected in 2024, because Hung Cao is a fucking crackpot who ran for Senate because, quite frankly, “There’s a place in Monterey, California called Lovers Point. The original name was Lovers of Christ Point. But now they took out the Christ, it’s become Lovers Point — really, Monterey is a really dark place now, a lot of witchcraft and the wiccan community has really taken over there, and we can’t let that happen in Virginia.”Hung Cao seems sane, doesn’t he?And because Donny has a knack for always being able to find the worst person possible for each job, he plucked Wytchfinder Cao from the shitpile of failure and made him his Undersecretary of the Navy.For once in his entire stupid life, Donny didn’t hire a flunkie because he looked good on Fox News. No, this time he picked the dude whose name makes him think of a .And now, Cao — the scourge of witches from Monterey to Virginia — is our Acting Secretary of the Navy.Mark Kelly: “So are you saying the reports of sailors losing 45 pounds are not true?”Hung Cao: “It’s just not what they want. It’s like my kids opening up the refrigerator door and saying, ‘there’s nothing to eat here.’”Kelly: “Somebody doesn’t lose 45 pounds just because they don’t like the options. I don’t think that’s a fair assessment.”Are you fucking kidding me? What kind of answer is, ‘yeah, these sailors are just picky eaters.’In any fair world, Cao would have immediately been transported to a ship in the middle of the ocean and been forced to eat rotting food for eight months. And then if he said anything about it, we could just go ‘shut the fuck up and stop being a prima donna.’It’s stunning how not one of these Donnyverse sewer clowns can ever just simply say ‘yeah, we fucked up. We’ll do better next time,’I guess he realized he .Peltola won with 50.1% of the vote. That’s more than both Dan Sullivans combined, so Preznit Fuckwit and Attorney General Muggsy and all the whiners in the MAGAsphere can sit on it and twirl.Now let’s have us our Daily Claudia.Today’s curation comes courtesy of the Google Photos app, which, for some reason, all on its own and without my prompting, took it upon itself to send me a link to a collection it created and called ‘Claudia eads.’ Here’s some of what it picked.In the living room on February 14, 2016.On the patio on August 30, 2016.In the living room on January 1, 2017.In the back yard on May 7, 2020.And at Blu Pointe in Newburgh, on January 30, 2025.Have a great Wednesday, everyone. I could get used to having Google’s janky curation robot do my work for me. Hey bro, you want to write tomorrow’s post?here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Life after coding
item.content:encoded: Lately, I’ve been giving a lot of thought to what I would do if I wasn’t a web developer.I posted about this in a handful of online communities I’m in, and are struggling with these same feelings. If you care about the craft of web work, it’s hard not to feel like the work you love is being ripped away from you.The trades seem relatively well protected… at least for now. I’m pretty confident I could learn plumbing or electrical work and go into a trade if I wanted to.But I’ve already changed careers once in my life, and don’t know that I have the energy or financial ability to go through that lengthy process again.Even for the more lucrative trades like electrical or welding, it would take a handful of years to get back to the level of income I’m making now. And none of them offer the level of work from anywhere flexibility that web work provides.But so many of my peers across the industry are enthusiastically training their robot replacements or acting like they have no other option but just go along with the inevitable. I’m not sure unionization is actually possible for a lot of people.AI evangelists spend so much time talking about how AI will free us from drudgery and allow us to spend more time enjoying life.In reality, it’s stealing all the fun stuff and leaving us with the shit. But even if that weren’t true, they never talk about how you’re supposed to “enjoy life” if you have no money, no home, no food, and no social safety net.

item.title: How homelessness and racism intersect.
item.author: SRS0=kL4K=JH=mail70.suw17.mcsv.net=bounce-mc.us19_228507186.17295061-8782042e9f@eforward.registrar-servers.com
item.content:encoded: Homelessness Funding Is on the Line. Here’s How to Protect It.Today, the National Alliance to End Homelessness is leading a national day of action to protect federal homelessness funding (National Alliance to End Homelessness). Advocates are asking Congress to add a few lines to its next spending bill that would require the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to renew every Continuum of Care project expiring this fiscal year for 12 months, without a new competition (National Low Income Housing Coalition).The Continuum of Care program is the largest federal source of money for local homelessness work. It pays for programs like permanent supportive housing, where people get a stable home along with services like health care and job support (National Low Income Housing Coalition), and transitional housing, which gives people a safe place to stay while they look for a permanent home (National Association of Counties).The Trump administration has spent the past year trying to limit spending on homelessness. In July 2025, the president signed an executive order directing agencies to end support for Housing First policies, which give people a permanent home quickly without first requiring sobriety, treatment or a job (The White House). But Housing First has been federal policy under presidents of both parties since 2003 (Associated Press), and it has proven to be the most effective way to rehouse people (National Alliance to End Homelessness).HUD then wrote new rules for this year’s Continuum of Care grants that put the president’s order into practice. In August, a federal judge ruled that those rules were unlawful. HUD had set aside $1.3 billion of this year’s funding for new transitional housing and service-only projects, a change that would have cut money from many programs already keeping people housed (National Association of Counties). The judge also struck down rules that required programs to follow the president’s executive orders and restricted diversity efforts. But in September, an appeals court let HUD move forward while it considers the case. Under HUD’s plan, only 60 percent of funding would be protected for renewals, down from nearly 90 percent. Advocates estimate that 97,000 people who were once unhoused could lose their housing as a result (National Low Income Housing Coalition).The delays are already hurting people. In Los Angeles, providers that serve domestic violence survivors and unhoused people have cut staff and drained their reserves while HUD held up their grants (LAist). As of September, more than 1,300 renewal grant agreements across the country, about one in five, had not been fully executed. “If HUD doesn’t start to reimburse agencies quickly … we’re going to see more suffering on the street,” said Myong Kim of the Downtown Women’s Center in Los Angeles.The people impacted by these funding cuts are disproportionately people of color. Black people are 14 percent of the U.S. population but 33 percent of people experiencing homelessness. Latino people make up 27.5 percent of the unhoused population, and Native and Pacific Islander people are also overrepresented. These numbers reflect generations of policy, from redlining to exclusionary zoning to landlords and lenders who still screen people out by eviction records and criminal background (National Alliance to End Homelessness). Today, Black renters are 28 percent of renters in the places Eviction Lab tracks, but 39 percent of the people facing eviction (Eviction Lab).While funding for housing is under attack, more places are choosing punishment instead. Since the Supreme Court’s 2024 ruling in Grants Pass v. Johnson, more than 350 cities and 14 states have adopted tougher laws on street homelessness (Stateline). In 2022, we spoke with Jamaal of ACT UP Philadelphia about the violence of encampment sweeps (Anti-Racism Daily). “Philly says all the time, ‘We can’t afford to house people, the housing is too expensive,’ but every time we turn around, they increase funding to the police,” he told us. I think about that line a lot, because it’s still true in so many cities.To be clear, renewing these grants won’t end homelessness on its own. We still need far more affordable homes, higher wages and an end to policies that punish people for being poor. But keeping existing programs running is the least Congress can do, and it’s within reach this month. If you have five minutes today, I encourage you to send that email. For many families, these few lines in a spending bill could decide whether they stay housed this winter.

item.title: Trump lost the race he bet everything on
item.author: 1axbqhwmo0qcdwqoqfjj3xipe99odyaoflv15f@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: Last night, Mary Peltola officially won Alaska’s Senate race. The Division of Elections updated its results to show she held an outright majority. The outcome is undeniable.With Peltola’s victory, Donald Trump lost the one fight he cared about most.For months, Trump obsessed over this race. Even as he watched Republicans get swept from coast to coast, his focus stayed fixed on Alaska.Weighed down by his historic unpopularity, his party lost Senate seats in Texas, Kansas, Iowa, North Carolina, Ohio and South Carolina. Even Mississippi.State after state, as the election returns came in, Trump could do nothing to stop the bleeding.Yet, as his party imploded, Trump seethed and raged about Sen. Dan Sullivan’s looming defeat in Alaska.He spread misinformation about how Alaskans vote. He lied about the results, insisting that votes cast for a different candidate belonged to the incumbent.He ordered his Justice Department to sue to block certification. When my law firm beat back that lawsuit, the DOJ came after me personally. Trump went on national television and said I should go to jail.None of these attacks changed the vote count. With each new batch of ballots, Peltola’s lead grew.Last night, the dam broke.Peltola now leads by 12,458 votes. More importantly, she has won more than half of all the votes cast in the race.There will be no ranked-choice tabulation, and no room for conspiracy theories about whose votes “really” belonged to whom.And with that, Trump’s lies collapse once and for all.Sullivan’s campaign says he won’t concede until the results are certified. The campaign insists it will “let that process run its course until every legal vote is counted and certified.”Fortunately, election results are stubborn. The numbers are what they are. They do not require a concession to be accurate. They do not care about the losing candidate’s feelings or his stage of grief.Despite all of Trump’s bluster, Mary Peltola will be the next senator from Alaska. A Yup’ik Alaskan and former congresswoman, she made history in 2022 as the first Alaska Native elected to Congress. She will be sworn in on Jan. 3, 2027, with the rest of the newly elected class.She will join a radically changed Congress. In the House, Democrats will hold a historic 260-seat majority. But it is the 56 seats in the Senate that have truly upended Trump’s agenda.With margins like these, Trump will no longer be able to confirm his cronies and sycophants. His judicial nominees will languish. Any Supreme Court vacancy will remain unfilled.With 56 seats, Democrats won’t just control the Senate for the next two years. They are almost certain to hold the majority for the next four. And if a Democrat wins the presidency in 2028, a Democratic Senate will be ready to fill every vacancy Trump leaves behind.Trump will fare no better with his legislative agenda. Democrats in Congress will decide which bills reach his desk. Trump will be reduced to nothing more than a signature — signing or vetoing the bills placed before him.The question remains: Why Alaska? Of all the defeats and humiliations Trump suffered this year, why did Dan Sullivan’s loss sting the most?Trump will say it’s because he believes Democrats cheated. But Trump has never cared about cheating.In 2020, he told Georgia’s secretary of state to “find” 11,780 votes that did not exist. In September, he stood before the Republican convention in Dallas and instructed his supporters to “cheat like hell” in this year’s elections. In any event, Trump’s lies are no longer sustainable. We now know that Peltola won an outright majority. No theory about confused voters or a second Dan Sullivan can explain away a candidate who won more votes than everyone else combined.The simplest answer is the most likely. Trump’s focus on Alaska is the fixation of an elderly man whose mental faculties are declining.It is the same fixation that has caused him to dedicate his presidency to a White House ballroom, a public golf course in Washington, D.C., and a triumphal arch. All while his party burned.Whatever the reason, Trump bet everything on Alaska, and he lost. For the rest of us, Peltola’s victory is cause for celebration. Let’s take a moment to enjoy it.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed’s fighting style terrifies MAGA
item.content:encoded: Jesse Watters can’t seem to stop admiring Dr. Abdul El-Sayed. The Fox News host loves to talk about how Michigan’s Democratic nominee for the Senate is “in great shape” and how “Abdul . . . beat the machine” — meaning the party establishment’s candidate, Rep. Haley Stevens — in a hard-fought primary. During an interview in August, Watters clearly enjoyed El-Sayed’s jokes and blunt speech, which included calling his opponent, former Rep. Mike Rogers, a “beta,” and asking the host if he was circumcised when Watters tried to corner him on gender-affirming surgery for minors. The next day, Watters made no bones about El-Sayed’s appeal. “I like him,” he said. “I don’t want to like him. I like him for some stupid reason.”But the reason was obvious. The doctor-turned-politician has an aggressive bro style that appeals to someone like Watters. Quick-witted with bulldog energy, El-Sayed never backs down from a fight. But despite Watters’ admiration, Fox News has become obsessed with taking El-Sayed down. It’s not because he’s Muslim, though Republicans are ratcheting up the racism in their efforts to derail his campaign. It’s because he is a model for how Democrats can escape their reputations for being weak and feckless. El-Sayed has a lot going for him. He spent years running public health services in the Detroit area and speaks eloquently and with authority about people’s struggles to afford healthcare, even writing a book about Medicare for All. Most importantly, he’s an excellent communicator who can boil down complex policy ideas into easily digestible concepts without dumbing them down. A video of him explaining to Trump voters why universal healthcare is cheaper than the insurance system went viral for good reason. One can see that, for these voters, it’s likely the first time someone plainly explained how removing executive salaries and profit incentives from healthcare makes it cheaper. Other politicians, like Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., or Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., are good at explaining progressive policy. But what really seems to scare Republicans about El-Sayed is his political persona as a brawler — and for good reason. Vice President JD Vance learned this last week when he lobbed a strange insult at El-Sayed during a rally in Michigan for Rogers. The Democrat, Vance said, is “a little weasel who should shut his mouth and show a little gratitude.”This is a common and deeply racist attack from Vance, who portrays non-white progressives as undeserving recipients of white people’s largesse — a caricature that has no relation to reality. El-Sayed left a position as an assistant professor at Columbia University to work in public health, where he won awards for his success in protecting children’s health from environmental pollution. During this same period, Vance worked as a venture capitalist who was close with tech billionaire Peter Thiel.El-Sayed resisted the temptation to “well, actually” Vance, and instead hit back by calling the vice president and those around him “carnival barkers” who ““JD Vance called me a little weasel today,” El-Sayed said. “I’m like, ‘No, no, no. What you’re talking about is a Wolverine,'” a reference to the mascot for the University of Michigan, where the Democrat got his undergraduate degree. As Salon’s Sophia Tesfaye recently wrote, El-Sayed has been courting Fox News viewers by appearing on the channel and running endless ads on it, all without softening his left-leaning message. He clearly hopes his bravado will woo some of the network’s audience, just as it won over Watters. For his part, President Donald Trump is worried that El-Sayed is right. He’s been openly complaining at rallies and on Truth Social about how charming the candidate is in his Fox appearances. In early October, Axios reported that the White House contacted the network to complain about El-Sayed’s coverage. Trump was especially miffed at the Democrat’s interview with Martha McCallum, during which the host’s efforts to bait him into saying something that could be spun as “radical” failed. Instead, MacCallum embarrassed herself by defending billionaires hoarding wealth, to which El-Sayed said that he’d rather pay for schools than be so “focused on allowing a billionaire to make another billion.”Since then, it seems that Fox producers got the White House’s message that they have to do something to dirty up El-Sayed. But they’ve learned the hard way that it won’t work to come at him directly, because he ends up dominating interviews and beguiling those who, like Watters, love his commanding and clever style. MacCallum later tried to redeem herself by interviewing progressive activist Corbin Trent and pretending he was a stand-in for El-Sayed.At first glance, Trent performed as Fox producers no doubt hoped he might. He took MacCallum’s bait by defending the Muslim Brotherhood, something that the host could not get El-Sayed to do. The problem, though, is that Trent has no discernible relationship to the candidate. While he has worked for other progressives, including Sanders, I found no evidence that he has even met El-Sayed, much less is qualified to speak for him.This attempt to hobble El-Sayed was revealing; it’s clearly all Fox News has. If the network tries to bring El-Sayed on again to ask him the same questions, they know from experience that he’ll probably just win over even more of their viewers. This isn’t idle speculation. MS NOW recently conducted a focus group with regretful Trump voters in Michigan and found that five out of the six are voting for El-Sayed. Republicans should be worried about the young male demographic in particular. Trump won male voters under 30 by a narrow margin in 2024, but they are jumping ship and now strongly favor Democrats.El-Sayed is a compelling model for a new kind of Democrat. Polling by Strength In Numbers/Verasight shows that even Democratic voters take a negative view of the party, but not because they think their leaders are too progressive. “[T]he single most common complaint about their own party is that it is too weak, too cautious, or not fighting hard enough,” writes G. Elliott Morris in an analysis of the poll.The Democratic base wants the party to take a more aggressive stance toward their GOP opponents, which will be key to building a more lasting coalition — especially one that includes younger and more male voters. El-Sayed is doing just that, and it has the right scared.

item.title: Trust Fall is in the Error
item.author: Dave Pell
item.source: NextDraft: The Day's Most Fascinating News
item.content:encoded: We’ve been hacked. I’m not talking about the Microsoft downtime, the air travel grounding, the bank inaccessibility, the Apple outage, or the fact that, for about 45 minutes this morning, my NextDraft pun generator wasn’t working. The more we learn, the more it looks like those software snafus were likely due to attempted upgrades, ill-advised patches, and endeavors aimed at AI-enabling communication systems that were originally built with two cans and a long string. But while it looks like our computers weren’t hacked, the last week made it plainly clear that have been. We didn’t know what was going on during these tech failures, and when we were given a series of explanations by the hack jobs in the administration, we didn’t believe them. And why would we? They lie as a matter of policy. They lie every time they speak. The truth has systematically been twisted into a pile of misinformation more tangled than the box of old plugs, cables, and cords you never got around to throwing out. As George W Bush famously explained: “Fool me once, shame on — shame on you. Fool me — you can’t get fooled again.” In an age defined by isolation and loneliness, Billy Joel may have prophesied the loneliest thing of all when he sang: Honesty is such a lonely word. So, when you hear the administration-offered statements like Marco Rubio’s proclamation that “there’s ‘zero’ information that U.S. outages are caused by a malign actor,” you’re right to have zero certainty they’re telling the truth. You’re getting that explanation a malign actor. You don’t trust them because they’ve spent years intentionally hacking your trust to smithereens. We have been trust-falled into the deepest bowels of hell. At this point, even Charlie Brown wouldn’t try to kick a football held by anyone in this administration. And that’s why I’m trying to explain that the biggest hack of this era is that we’re all worried our government is lying to us about the causes of the outages. Trust is glitching. Trust has been hijacked. Our democracy’s terms of service have been rewritten, and our citizenry is no longer willing to blindly click to agree. I’d suggest that when it comes to matters of IT, you’d be better off getting explanations from tech companies than from the administration, but we don’t trust tech companies either.+ Nicole Perlroth wrote the book on cybersecurity (So, yes, you can trust her), and she shared some thoughts on X: “We were told to ‘move fast and break things.’ VCs told us to celebrate the idea that ‘software would eat the world.’ Now we’re telling ourselves we can simply ‘roll out AI’ across everything, as though nothing underneath will buckle. We never stopped to ask: SHOULD WE? … Nobody ever asked: What if, in the name of progress, we were creating the ripest attack surface in human history?”+ With enough work and time and the right leaders, there may still be time to rebuild the trust upon which democracy depends. But that could change if Grand Theft Auto VI goes down, too.“Democrat Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, overcoming allegations that members of her campaign helped recruit a candidate who shares the incumbent’s name and completing a political comeback in a state President Donald Trump repeatedly won by wide margins.” Democrat Mary Peltola wins US Senate race in Alaska. (Maybe Trump did make one true statement. I’m almost getting tired of all the winning.)+ The Second Dan Sullivan Made No Impact on Alaska Senate Race. (Let that be a lesson to all future campaign strategists. If you want a real impact, you’re gonna need at least three Dan Sullivans.)“‘Down with the ,’ people shouted, referring to the entrenched patronage networks that reward party loyalty over merit in nearly every sphere of life. When another group chanted a World War II slogan—’Albania for the Albanians, death to the traitors’—my fixer said, ‘This one is for you.’ He meant Americans. What had first sparked the protests, in May, were plans by Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of the American president, to build an ultra-luxury resort in a fragile nature preserve in the country’s south, where flamingos gather.” Ariel Sabar in (Gift Article): How Jared Kushner Sparked a Revolution in the Balkans. (The midterms may be the first step toward America forgiving itself for Trumpism. It’s gonna take the rest of the world a lot longer.)That which doesn’t kill the regime makes it stronger? … “The mood was something I’d never encountered here before. Not shock and awe, but shock and dread. The dread comes from the dawning awareness that this latest war with Iran, started by America and Israel, is going to end with Iran more dominant than ever over its neighbors. The Gulf Arabs never urged the United States to start this war, but once it did, they assumed it had a plan to finish it.” Thomas Friedman in the (Gift Article): Shock and Dread in the Gulf. “The prevailing sentiment was most pointedly conveyed to me by an Eastern European diplomat at the conference, citing an aphorism from Cold War days: ‘The trouble with being an ally of the United States is that you never know when it will turn around and stab itself in the back.'” “In a 7-mile-wide city of barely 800,000 people, the AI boom has minted thousands of fortunes worth $10 million or more, many of them at the two biggest companies. At the midpoint of Anthropic’s IPO price range, its average employee would each own shares worth $72 million, according to a (Gift Article) analysis of PitchBook data. The average OpenAI insider’s stake is worth almost $126 million, based on the firm’s most recent valuation.” Anthropic’s IPO Is Igniting a Massive AI Wealth Boom in San Francisco. (This gold rush is so massive, we may have to change the name of our football team to the San Francisco 26ers.)+ Meet and Greet (and Beat): “In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. It is believed to be the first time that Xi, in power for more than a decade, has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China.” (Oh, man, he’s really gonna try to get one over on Trump this time…)+ “I learned that I’m overly credulous when it comes to men’s stated intentions (‘You can recognize that a man is unavailable, evasive, selfish, or inconsistent,’ the bot said, ‘and nevertheless continue to treat his expressions of desire as evidence that something more meaningful might develop’) and that I’m looking for love in all the wrong places (‘You sometimes recognize a man’s limitations but behave as though they are negotiable’). Anna Holmes in (Gift Article): ChatGPT Analyzed 32,245 of My Text Messages.+ Sean Duffy Stars in The Real World: “I have a great idea. Let’s take that money in $100 bills and have a national weenie roast instead. It will be a lot more fun and about as effective in fixing the existing air traffic control system … Like upgrading a Model T for a highway, overhauling the air traffic control system architecture will never be able to achieve sufficient airspeed.” $50 Billion Won’t Fix Air Traffic Control. It Needs to Be Scrapped. (Can we maybe scrap it at a moment when I’m not on a flight?) Speaking of Model Ts and highways, California has banned Waymo self-driving cars from freeways.+ Caviar Wishes and Abstain Dreams: Almost nobody’s vying for an invite to Trump’s second meme coin dinner. “In the run-up to the first gala, in May 2025, Trump’s coin was riding high. Some bought millions of dollars worth of coins to attend, and it took at least $55,000 worth of coin holdings to score an invite. This time, however, one prescient buyer earned an invite for just $518.” (He’s still overpaying.)AI is cool and all, but is an invention: “The novelty streetwear garment was designed to keep burritos both warm and concealed while sneaking them into the cinema for illicit mid-movie snacking.” (Forget the cinema. I’m getting one of these to sneak a second burrito into my man cave.)

item.content:encoded: It's a miracle that this movie even exists. It makes me happy every time I watch it. I can't get over the fact that Roger Ebert wrote the screenplay and that it includes lines like, "Ere this night does wane, you will drink the black sperm of my vengeance!" So fun.
